title: LUCAS Drones To Be Built In Containerized Robotic Micro Factories Designed To Be Forward Deployed
zh_title: LUCAS 无人机将内置于集装箱式机器人微型工厂中，旨在进行前沿部署
summary: 加州一家名为 Machina 的机器人公司获得了 900 万美元的奖励，用于开发集装箱系统，以机器人方式批量生产接近需求点的低成本无人作战攻击系统 (LUCAS) 机身。正如 TWZ 经常指出的那样，LUCAS 无人机以及类似的单向攻击武器在美国作战行动和军事规划中发挥着越来越重要的作用。 Machina 的获奖是五角大楼推动使用集装箱式 3D 打印和其他更靠近前线的先进制造系统的最新例子，以缩短可能严重退化的供应链
content:
加州一家名为 Machina 的机器人公司获得了 900 万美元的奖励，用于开发集装箱系统，以机器人方式批量生产接近需求点的低成本无人作战攻击系统 (LUCAS) 机身。正如 TWZ 经常指出的那样，LUCAS 无人机以及类似的单向攻击武器在美国作战行动和军事规划中发挥着越来越重要的作用。 Machina 的获奖是五角大楼推动使用集装箱式 3D 打印和其他更靠近前线的先进制造系统的最新例子，以缩短在重大冲突中可能严重退化的供应链。无人机的分散生产还使各单位能够更加灵活，并可以随时根据自己的特定需求定制自己的生产。例如，一个单元可以生产最适合即将到来的任务的多种设计变体，而不必使用它们所运送的任何东西。 Machina 创始人兼首席执行官 Ed Mehr 周五下午对 TWZ 表示，国防部有机工业基础现代化挑战赛的这份为期 18 个月的合同要求 Machina 证明其可以利用其 RoboCraftsman 系统在部署地点制造 LUCAS 无人机。在许多其他地区大规模生产它们的决定将在稍后做出。在爱德华兹空军基地进行飞行测试期间，由 Machina 的 RoboCraftsman 系统创建的 LUCAS 无人机六英尺半比例测试模型。
(Machina) 使用 3D 打印和其他先进制造技术进行无人机和组件的集装箱化生产是一个新兴行业。Machina 系统是围绕这一概念构建的快速增长的功能之一，尽管许多功能都专注于小型无人机。梅尔说，最初，该计划要求 Machina 在美国大陆的两个地点建立所谓的“边缘工厂”。然而，最终目标是能够将它们部署到科威特等国家的转发地点。梅尔告诉我们，边缘工厂由该公司的集装箱式 RoboCraftsman 制造单元组成。这是一个 20 英尺 x 36 英尺的系统，完全安装后重 120,000 磅，本质上是两个机械臂，根据各种要求使用还原制造方法用金属形成机身。有效负载重量、范围和其他因素被输入 nTop 公司设计的软件系统中，然后机械臂根据所需的规格将金属切割成所需的形状因数。 Machina 使用金属而不是许多无人机所用的复合材料，因为“它不仅更便宜，而且用途更广泛，而且现在可以使用像我们这样的自动化工艺进行加工，而复合材料都是通过手工铺层完成的，”Mehr 解释道。
下面的 Machina 视频展示了 RoboCraftsman 系统如何在输入的引导下形成金属来制造机身。Mehr 表示，这避免了使用模具和轧辊等设备，从而大大加快了流程并允许大规模生产。 “基本上，代理人工智能代理可以探索并生成具有不同参数的完全不同版本的机身，”梅尔提出。 “因为现在它已经参数化了，你只需更改参数，就可以得到另一个机身，然后评估该机身是否适合他们想要的要求。”这样，RoboCraftsman 系统“只需在软件中即可轻松生成 20、30、40、50 种不同的设计，

【原文 English Original】
A California robotics company called Machina has been issued a $9 million award for a containerized system to robotically mass-produce Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS) airframes close to the point of need. As TWZ has frequently noted , LUCAS drones, and one-way attack weapons like them, are playing an increasing role in U.S. combat operations and military planning. The award to Machina is the latest example of the Pentagon’s push to use containerized 3D printing and other advanced fabricating systems closer to the front lines to shorten supply chains that could get severely degraded in a major conflict. Decentralizing production of drones also allows units to be more flexible and tailor their own production to their specific needs at any given moment. For instance, a unit can produce variations of multiple designs that are best suited to an upcoming mission instead of having to use whatever they are shipped. (Machina) This 18-month contract from the Defense Department’s Organic Industrial Base Modernization Challenge calls for Machina to prove it can build LUCAS drones at deployed locations with its RoboCraftsman system, Ed Mehr, founder and CEO of Machina, told TWZ Friday afternoon. A decision on producing them at scale in many other locales will come later. A LUCAS drone six-foot half-scale test model created by Machina’s RoboCraftsman system during a flight test at Edwards Air Force Base. (Machina) Creating containerized production of drones and components using 3D printing and other advanced manufacturing techniques at the forward edge is a burgeoning industry. The Machina system is one of a rapidly growing number of capabilities built around this concept, although many focus on smaller drones. Building Drones Near The Point Of Need Initially, the plan calls for Machina to set up so-called “Edge Factories” at two locations in the continental United States, said Mehr. However, the ultimate goal is to be able to deploy them to forward locations in countries like Kuwait. The Edge Factories consist of the company’s containerized RoboCraftsman manufacturing cells, Mehr told us. A 20-foot by 36-foot system that weighs 120,000 pounds fully installed, it is essentially two robotic arms that form the airframe out of metal using reductive manufacturing based on a variety of requirements. Payload weight, range and other factors are punched into a software system designed by the nTop company and the robotic arms then cut the metal into the desired form factor based on the required specifications. Machina uses metal instead of composites that many drones are made out of because “not only it is cheaper, it is more widely available and now can be processed with an automated process like ours versus composites, which are all done by hand layup ,” Mehr explained. The following Machina video shows how the RoboCraftsman system, guided by the inputs, forms the metal to craft the airframe. This avoids having to use equipment like dies and rolls, dramatically speeding the process and allowing production at scale, Mehr stated. “Basically, the agentic AI agents can explore and generate whole different versions of an airframe with different parameters,” Mehr proffered. “Because now it’s parameterized, you can just change the parameters and you get another airframe, and then evaluate if that airframe is good for the requirement they want.” This way, the RoboCraftsman system “can easily generate 20, 30, 40, 50 different designs just in software, and then put it through simulations to figure out which one actually meets the requirement for that,” the Machina CEO added. “The concept is that we’re going to bring this capability closer to the point of need, so that you can build a different requirement for let’s say PACOM versus U.S. CENTCOM versus in Ukraine,” Mehr said. “They can easily switch and build a drone that they need.” Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS) drones in the U.S. Central Command region. (CENTCOM) (U.S. Central Command Public Affairs) Under this contract, each Edge Factory will consist of one or two RoboCraftsman cells and each cell can make a LUCAS airframe in two to five days, depending on the size, Mehr said. A scaled deployment of 10 or more cells would take place under a new contract, he added. The systems can make “anywhere from a one-off all the way to the thousands, sometimes tens of thousands,” Mehr said. It all depends on the number of RoboCraftsman systems that are ordered. At the moment, Mehr envisions that each 12-foot airframe will cost “somewhere around $15,000 to $40,000,” depending on the complexity. This range is a relatively common price point for Russian Shahed-136 variants and U.S. knockoffs under the LUCAS program. The company has already produced a six-foot, half-scale airframe that was recently tested at Edwards Air Force Base, said Mehr. However, that initial test proved problematic. “The first design had some challenges with crosswind mitigation,” Mehr told us. “Since then, we have moved the location of the engine slightly to enable better crosswind mitigation, and now we’re running again. And the beauty is for us to go from one design to the next is just like a couple of months, a maximum of three months. Like we can just then try it again.” A six-foot, half-scale LUCAS drone, made by a Machina RoboCraftsman system, being tested at Edwards Air Force Base, California. (Machina) Mehr said that Machina is not working with SpektreWorks, which designed and made the LUCAS drones previously supplied to the U.S. military and already used in combat. SpektreWorks declined to comment. The Edge Factory contract is one of several Machina has been awarded to use these systems to help build and repair military hardware. In July, Machina was issued a qualification contract by Lockheed Martin to produce fuel tanks for AGM-158 Joint Air-To-Surface Standoff Missiles (JASSM). That plan called for the creation of a 200,000-square-foot facility “designed to house up to 50 RoboCraftsman cells and support high-rate production of mission-critical metal structures for defense programs including JASSM,” according to a media release at the time . “By integrating forming, machining, welding, and assembly under one roof, Machina Factory 3 compresses production timelines from months to days.” “Lockheed Martin Ventures invested in Machina Labs for its powerful combination of speed, flexibility, and scalability, and our teams have worked closely to transition key capabilities to production,” said Chris Moran, vice president and general manager, Lockheed Martin Ventures. “Machina’s work advances capacity, reduces risk, and helps ensure we can deliver mission-critical capabilities at scale. We congratulate Machina on this milestone as a supplier, which further strengthens an innovative and resilient American Defense Industrial Base.” U.S. Air Force Staff Sgt. Seth Blackwood, 363rd Training Squadron Aircraft Armament instructor, directs the installation of an AGM-158 JASSM onto a B-52 during a Combat Capability Demonstration April 16, 2024, at Sheppard Air Force Base, Texas. (U.S. Air Force photo by Rachel Ross) Rachel Ross Earlier this year, a Machina RoboCraftsman platform helped repair a C-17 Globemaster III cargo jet that was damaged during a tornado, Mehr told us. The system “fabricated a first-of-its-kind replacement part for the damaged C-17 without the need for dedicated tooling,” the company noted . “Machina deployed a RoboCraftsman at the RSO [ Rapid Sustainment Office ], where production for a left nose panel began in March 2026 and was completed in May 2026. The aircraft returned to flight on July 30, 2026 at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio.” Damage to a C-17 Globemaster III cargo jet caused by a tornado that was eventually repaired with a Machina RoboCraftsman system. (Machina) We asked the Pentagon for information about why they selected Machina and their metrics for success, but we have not heard back yet. Pentagon Pushing For Deployable Manufacturing The U.S. military has been pushing for several years for the employment of mobile additive and other forms of advanced manufacturing “to produce unmanned aircraft components in remote or austere environments and reduce dependence on traditional supply chains,” the Air Force’s innovation arm, AFWERX, noted last month . The idea is to place these systems in a wide array of locations, produce the quantity needed and tailor the airframe for the mission. In one such case, the Air National Guard and Air Force Special Operations Command partnered with the San Diego-based Firestorm company in 2023 “to create an expeditionary assembly unit capable of mass-producing unmanned aerial systems,” according to the Pentagon . The result was called an Expeditionary Manufacturing Cell or xCell. “It’s basically an expeditionary 3D printer,” Master Sgt. Richard Stone, 194th Air Support Operations Group innovation officer, explained at the time. “The basis of the technology is … it’s about the size of a [shipping container] and it can print out, for this specific use case, drones.” “Inside this [shipping container], it’ll print out all the components,” said Stone “But then you have what’s called RPA, which is robotic process [automation.]” The xCell “prints the individual pieces and then uses RPA to assemble the major components of the drone,” the Pentagon added. A render of Expeditionary Manufacturing Cell or xCell which is capable of mass-producing unmanned aerial systems. Theoretically, xCell can be hidden in plain sight while running on local resources to 3D-print items on the battle field. (Courtesy photo from Firestorm) 194th Wing “The user can take these components and, almost like Legos, put them together,” said Stone. “So if you want a longer drone with a specific payload, you can take those components and put them together and the computer will tell you, ‘This is where the wings go and this is where the center of gravity should be.” The company went on to produce Tempest drones that were flying with 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, during Exercise Balikatan 2026 at Cagayan North International Airport in the Philippines, AFWERX noted. A Firestorm Tempest Drone with 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, is staged for preflight checks during Exercise Balikatan 2026 at Cagayan North International Airport, Lal-Lo, Philippines, April 23, 2026. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Ernesto Lagunes) Cpl. Ernesto Lagunes Our own Jamie Hunter recently interviewed Craig Anders, senior vice president of growth at Aevex, about the company’s ForgeX containerized 3D drone printing system . The ForgeX system “represents being able to take the fight further forward, print drones on demand, print them out towards the front of the lines, cut down the logistics trail, and absolutely revolutionize the battlefield,” said Anders.  The goal is to be “able to kick these planes out the door on short timelines to go out and get the missions done, work within the local area to make sure that the mission can be accomplished by any means necessary,” he added. Anders said the ForgeX printers fabricate three types of drones, the Vandal , Onyx and Raker . He added that the system can produce up to 880 a year. Growing U.S. Reliance On LUCAS The U.S. military first announced it had begun fielding LUCAS, which was reverse-engineered from the Iranian-designed Shahed-136 , in December 2025. This came just months after TWZ laid out a detailed case for why the U.S. military should start acquiring Shahed-136 clones in large volumes. LUCAS made its official combat debut in the opening phases of major combat operations against Iran earlier this year. The pusher-propeller, combustion-engine-powered kamikaze drones were first launched from the ground, a U.S. official told us at the time. They can also be fired from ships. In March, CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper told us the LUCAS drones were “indispensable. ” The following video shows Cooper answering our question about the LUCAS drones. CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper on LUCAS: LUCAS is indispensable. pic.twitter.com/VaLXmjawA6 — Clash Report (@clashreport) March 5, 2026 Now the Army is looking to expand the use of these weapons to the Pacific, Maj. Gen. Bernard Harrington, head of the 7th Infantry Division, told us during the Association of the U.S. Army (AUSA) conference last month. “So we see that playing a key role in order to be able to achieve that effect at mass, … [and] in an affordable manner, while also being able potentially to preserve something that’s more exquisite for something that requires an exquisite munition.” “So as we start modeling out what it looks like to be able to penetrate a portion of the anti-access/area denial network in support of the joint task force in the PACOM [U.S. Pacific Command] area of operations, we started looking at, well, how do I bend – how do I achieve mass at a cost curve?” the 7th Infantry and MDC-PAC commander explained. “What effect am I really trying to achieve on a system in order to provide that window of opportunity for that joint force commander?” A map showing Chinese military outposts in the Spratly Islands at the southern end of the South China Sea. This gives a good sense of the anti-access/area denial bubbles that China has already established and continues to expand upon. (DOD) “So maybe I don’t necessarily need to sink a ship, but if I take out certain systems on that vessel, well then it creates this temporal window opportunity,” he continued. “Then that joint force commander can surge in that carrier strike group or bomber task force.” While the exact details of the LUCAS program requirements have been hard to pin down, it’s likely that multiple drone types from multiple manufacturers could become part of the program as time goes on. Ed Mehr gave us an idea of what that could look like: “Shahed clearly inspired LUCAS, which stands for Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System. But we shouldn’t confuse the inspiration with the destination. The future isn’t about mass-producing replicas of one drone. Different theaters and missions demand different performance, and therefore different designs. That could mean a LUCAS-style drone or a wide variety of Group 2 and Group 3 unmanned aircraft. The real breakthrough is making that diversity affordable. We’re developing flexible manufacturing technologies that can produce many different designs cost-effectively using one of the cheapest and most proven aerospace materials: sheet metal. It’s what aircraft have been built from for generations. We’re bringing it into an era where manufacturing can adapt as quickly as the mission.” We won’t know how the Machina contract ultimately pans out until sometime in mid-2028. Regardless, given the importance of both the LUCAS drones and deployable, additive and advanced manufacturing are becoming, this is likely a first step in what could be a whole new logistics concept that could underpin a significant portion of the growing LUCAS program. Contact the author: howard@twz.com The post LUCAS Drones To Be Built In Containerized Robotic Micro Factories Designed To Be Forward Deployed appeared first on TWZ .

Fundraiser by Su Lee : Wipe Away Su Lee's Tears from her Composing Nights
Su Lee is organizing this fundraiser.
Dear friends, music lovers, and new music supporters,
It’s me, Su Lee, and I am currently working on my dissertation concert (for my Ph.D. in composition) which will be held on Sept. 9th 2019 Monday at 7:30pm in Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall at University at Buffalo.
The title of my dissertation composition and concert is Die Radikalen Tasten (The Radical Keys) in terms of aesthetics, Klang (sound), and theme.
I am writing a concerto for organ with keyboard ensemble, namely for our own tremendous Fisk Op.95 organ at UB. It will involve organ soloist with 1 assistant, 2 pianos (1 quarter-tone flat piano), 2 harpsichords (1 quarter-tone flat harpsichord), and 2 vibraphones which is a very rare instrumentation for microtonal new music.
The 1st half of the program features significant keyboard works from the 20th century such as Messiaen's solo organ work and Ives's quarter-tone piano pieces. As a special request from Dr. Fuller, who was in charge of the installation of the Fisk Op.95 organ at UB, I'm playing my very first organ transcription of Wagner's orchestral work.
The 2nd half of the program features my own 'radical' politically inspired compositions including a choral piece with organ accompaniment (dedicated to the UUCB Choir family) and my dissertation organ concerto. Both works are based on the Korean Democratic Uprising in May 1980 and the protest song written for the victims of the subsequent Gwangju massacre - a song that has became widely popular for activists and protesters, including those participating in the on-going Hong Kong protests.
Overall, it is a very colorful and unique combination and a rare program which is a you-don’t-want-to-miss concert.
I am modestly asking you for a little or big help in making my dissertation concert happen smoothly, especially given my financial struggles in not being able to even work legally for money off campus in America due to my visa status.
Your generous donation will be spent towards, (besides helping me wipe away all my tears and whining from composing numerous nights over the past few months and rehearsing in the upcoming days and nights):
Nine Musicians’ Performance Fee, about $3,000 – 3,300
Rent/Labor for Lippes Concert Hall in Slee Hall, about $1,000
Other concert related costs; buying performing materials, copying/binding score/parts, printing poster/program book, audio/video recording, photographing, tuning, reception, etc. about $1,200 – 1,500
Fortunately, I got awarded the MDRF (research fund) for $3,000 at UB so that I can be reimbursed afterwards, but I need money upfront now to pay first, and possibly more, to pay my dream team musicians fairly and to cover other costs.
Your genuine help means SO MUCH to me being an international Ph.D. student with many restrictions on earning money (3 months summer break without job, seriously!), as it will lighten my financial burdens and psychological anxiety when I absolutely need to focus more on my creative activities.
Simply speaking, you are contributing to a potentially "fabulous" new music piece, stimulating my further musical activities and making me believe that life (and the world) is so beautiful!
Every single one of your names will be acknowledged in my concert program book, and to thank you all, but not nearly enough, I like to give you in return as below:
$1~$49: a thank-you-card with a cover of a handwritten excerpt of my score
$50~$99: a thank-you-card like above AND a dvd of my dissertation concert (after my concert)
$100~$199: a thank-you-card AND a dvd like above, PLUS the autographed full score of my dissertation composition
$200~$299: EVERYTHING above AND one additional dvd of my Masters organ recitals (your choice of “Über den Namen B-A-C-H” or “Celebrating Lou Harrison’s 100th Birth-Year at Thunder Night”)
$300 or more: EVERYTHING above, PLUS a gift pack of Korean snacks/sweets/tea etc.
Please write me an email with your home address!
I am really excited to prepare my dissertation concert. Though I feel like this is sadly going to be my last self designed concert during my time in Buffalo (at UB), so I cannot wait to see many of you there!
Thank you so much for reading this and considering your donation.
I promise to pay you back with my "fabulous" new compositions and my performance, with the great help of my dream team of musician fellows!
Please feel free to spread the link to your social pages like Facebook, Instagram, or Twitter, or to emails, to help get the word out!
FYI, I am collecting your donations from now till October and GoFundMe takes 2.9% for transaction fee plus $0.30 PER Donation. Or you can donate by sending me a check to my place (email me for asking my address please!)

content:
内容摘要：中华人民共和国 (PRC) 正在扩大对 RISC-V（一种开源芯片设计标准）的使用，并扩大其对管理该标准的国际非营利组织的影响力。近年来，人们越来越担心被切断与 Arm 和英特尔等西方行业领导者设计的芯片的联系。中国公司现在不仅为消费设备而且为服务器和数据中心制造 RISC-V 芯片，尽管它们的功能不如专有芯片。 V100于10月推出，由国家支持的实体共同创建，号称是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片。国家级政策文件传统上避免直接讨论RISC-V，但今年9月，《电子信息制造业“十五五”规划》宣布，要求推进RISC-V研发和产业化，开发人工智能（AI）RISC-V芯片。 RISC-V 为自力更生带来了明显的好处，并且芯片可以进行调整，包括针对军事用例进行优化。
然而，中国的分析师担心芯片的“玻璃天花板”，甚至国家 IT 替代计划也指出，在政府系统中用于替代外国技术的 RISC-V 芯片的份额“可以忽略不计”。 10月19日，深圳芯片制造商进迭时空与香山处理器团队在第六届RISC-V中国峰会上推出了新型46核服务器芯片V100。[1]其制造商宣称其是首款完全符合RISC-V服务器标准的通用芯片（21世纪经济报道，10月19日；科技日报，10月20日）。 RISC-V 是一种开源指令集架构 (ISA)，是处理器运行的语言。与全球几乎所有计算机和手机中使用的 Arm 或 Intel x86 等专有 ISA 不同，任何人都可以使用 RISC-V，无需支付许可费或需要其他权限。由英国和美国公司制造的 Arm 和英特尔处理器必须遵守这些国家政府实施的许可和出口管制。相比之下，RISC-V 主要由 RISC-V International 监管，这是一家总部位于瑞士的非营利组织，旨在避免此类漏洞。最近推出的服务器芯片代表了中华人民共和国（PRC）该行业更广泛的趋势。
北京最初在 2010 年代中期开始将 RISC-V 视为对抗西方技术霸权并扩大其在新兴技术领域结构性力量的一种方式（中国简报，2023 年 12 月 15 日）。此后，北京通过国家主导的政策支持鼓励其发展，从城市层面开始，逐步上升到国家层面。尽管这些芯片的功能仍然落后于西方竞争对手，但它们越来越多地部署在数据中心的服务器中，而不仅仅是嵌入消费设备中。从市政厅到五年计划 2023年以来，地方层面对RISC-V的支持已经明确，特别是在上海、北京和深圳等一线城市（中国简报，2023年12月15日）。北京经济技术开发区的目标是到 2030 年使 RISC-V 产业价值超过 500 亿元人民币（70 亿美元），据一些估计，届时全国市场将达到约 2200 亿元人民币（210 亿美元）（北京市政府，2025 年 1 月 3 日；中国日报）

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: The People’s Republic of China (PRC) is expanding its use of RISC-V, an open-source chip design standard, as well as its influence over the international nonprofit organization that manages it. This follows growing fears in recent years of being cut off from chips designed by Western industry leaders such as Arm and Intel. PRC firms are now creating RISC-V chips not just for consumer devices but for servers and data centers, even though they are less powerful than proprietary chips. The V100, launched in October and co-created by a state-backed entity, is billed as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards. National-level policy documents have traditionally avoided discussing RISC-V directly, but in September, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to advance RISC-V research, development, and industrialization, and to develop RISC-V chips for artificial intelligence (AI). RISC-V brings clear benefits for self-reliance, and the chips can be adapted, including being optimized for military use cases. Analysts in the PRC worry, however, about a “glass ceiling” for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible.” On October 19, Shenzhen-based chipmaker SpacemiT (进迭时空) and the state-backed XiangShan (香山) processor team launched the V100, a new 46-core server chip, at the sixth RISC-V Summit China.  [1] Its makers bill it as the first general-purpose chip fully compliant with RISC-V server standards ( 21st Century Business Herald , October 19; Science and Technology Daily , October 20). RISC-V is an open-source instruction set architecture (ISA), which is the language that processors run on. Unlike proprietary ISAs, such as Arm or Intel’s x86 that are used in almost all of the world’s computers and phones, anyone can use RISC-V without paying a license fee or requiring other permissions. Arm and Intel processors, made by British and U.S. companies, must abide by licensing and export controls put in place by those countries’ governments. By comparison, RISC-V is mainly overseen by RISC-V International, a Switzerland-based nonprofit that avoids such vulnerabilities. The recently unveiled server chip is representative of broader trends in the sector within the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Beijing initially began to view RISC-V as a way to counter the West’s technological hegemony and extend its structural power in emerging technologies in the mid-2010s ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Since then, it has encouraged its development through state-led policy support, starting at the city level and moving up to the national level. Although the chips’ capabilities remain behind those of Western rivals, they are increasingly being deployed in servers for data centers, not just embedded in consumer devices. From City Halls to the Five-Year Plan Since 2023, local-level support for RISC-V has been explicit, especially in first-tier cities like Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen ( China Brief , December 15, 2023). Beijing’s Economic-Technological Development Area aims for a RISC-V industry worth more than renminbi (RMB) 50 billion ($7 billion) by 2030, at which point the national market will reach around RMB 220 billion ($21 billion), according to some estimates ( Beijing Municipal Government , January 3, 2025; China Daily , October 22). National-level documents have tended instead to use the term “open source” to implicitly refer to RISC-V. In mid-September, however, the 15th Five-Year Plan for the Electronic Information Manufacturing Industry announced calls to “advance the research, development, and industrialization of RISC-V” (推进第五代精简指令集 (RISC-V) 研发与产业化), and to support RISC-V artificial intelligence (AI) and embedded system chips ( Ministry of Information and Industry Technology , September 15).  [2] Server Ambitions, Smartphone-Class Silicon RISC-V’s strength so far has been in cheaper control chips for appliances and cars, but newer chips signal data center servers as an emerging use case. The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) calls the open-source XiangShan core the most powerful of its kind in the world ( China Daily , March 26). Beyond the latest processor from SpacemiT and XiangShan, Alibaba now offers a server-class design, the C950, that it says performs on par with Apple’s M1 chip, which it released in 2020, on a standard performance test ( The Register , March 25). Engineers usually judge how well a core is designed via a two-step process. First, they run an industry-standard test, which times how long a processor takes to complete a set of tasks, and turns that time into a score. Second, they divide the score by the core’s clock speed, which is the number of steps it takes each second, measured in gigahertz (GHz). The result measures how much work a core does in each step (see Figure 1). On this metric, PRC progress is substantial: XiangShan’s cores have roughly doubled since 2021. Measured at the speeds they actually run, the best cores in the SpacemiT/XiangShan processor are well behind Nvidia’s leading Grace server processor, and those produced by Arm and Intel (see Figure 2). Alibaba’s C950, which it licenses to other chipmakers, comes close to or beats Grace based on the firm’s internal testing. RISC-V Buys Assurance and Customization RISC-V offers the PRC with two benefits: the assurance of sustainable access, and adaptability for military purposes, which would be risky use-cases for employing Western chips. The fear of being cut off from access to chips has been acute since Huawei learned in 2019 that its access to Arm’s designs could be suspended ( BBC , May 22, 2019). As an open-source architecture, RISC-V can be modified and tailored to user requirements. In some instances, however, this has allowed it to be adapted for military purposes. A team at Information Engineering University, an institution affiliated with the People’s Liberation Army, was able to customize command for data encryption to a small RISC-V chip, accelerating encryption by about seven times with only about two percent more circuitry.  [5] These benefits are another part of the reason why the PRC has pushed to deepen its influence over RISC-V at the international level. Chinese firms now hold half of the 24 top-tier memberships in RISC-V International ( RISC-V , accessed November 3). U.S. firms are deepening their stake in the RISC-V ecosystem too. Nvidia said in July 2025 that its CUDA software, the backbone of AI computing, would support RISC-V processors, and Qualcomm bought the RISC-V server designer Ventana in December 2025 ( The Register , July 21, 2025; Qualcomm , December 10, 2025). Conclusion Beijing continues to emphasize RISC-V to advance technological self-reliance and resilience. Although it is starting to use RISC-V chips in servers and data centers, the chips function at well below the capabilities of the most advanced processors. Analysts in the PRC have worried about a “glass ceiling” (玻璃天花板) for the chips, and even the state IT substitution program (信创) has noted that the share of RISC-V chips it has used to replace foreign technology in government systems is “negligible (微乎其微)” ( Sina Finance , April 7). It is nevertheless too soon to dismiss the hype over the PRC’s RISC-V development. RISC-V currently also enjoys support from U.S. companies. This makes the international standards that govern RISC-V an important battle ground in the competition to shape this arena of open-source technology. It remains unclear, however, whether the United States will seek to build a U.S.-led ISA ecosystem or discourage U.S. and allied firms from taking part in Chinese-led RISC-V projects. Neither option is cost-free, although if Washington does not take action, a key part of the semiconductor supply chain could end up being controlled by Beijing. Notes [1] A core is the part of a processor that reads and carries out software instructions. [2] The plan was released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and the National Development and Reform Commission, but grew out of work by eight agencies that drafted the country’s first national guidance on RISC-V in 2025 ( Reuters , March 3, 2025). [3] For Figure 2, panel A estimates the real speed of a single core by multiplying its points per gigahertz by the clock speed at which it actually ships, and shows the result relative to a core in Nvidia’s Grace server processor (set at 100). Intel and AMD do not publish comparable SPECint2006 figures, so their desktop cores are set equal to Arm’s Cortex-X925, which independent testing by Chips and Cheese found to be within the margin of error of the fastest AMD and Intel cores on the newer SPECint2017 test ( Chips and Cheese, March 3 ). Panels B and C compare whole server chips. The first is the number of cores. Each core works on its own task, so more cores means more work at once. The second is memory speed, or bandwidth: how many gigabytes of data a chip can move to and from its memory each second. In large data-center jobs this is often the real limit, because even a fast core sits idle while it waits for data. The lower panels of Figure 2 compare other measures of performance for entire server chips. The V100 has 46 cores; Nvidia’s Grace has 72; and the top Intel and AMD server chips have 128–192. The V100 also moves data to and from memory at about half their speed. It draws far less power, however, at 120 watts, compared to about 250 for Grace and 500 for the Intel and AMD chips ( GitHub , accessed October 27). [4] Figure 3 measures AI performance in trillions of simple calculations per second (TOPS). Since AI models run on vast numbers of such calculations, higher TOPS values translate to faster AI. The left panel divides TOPS by the power a chip draws, in watts, to show energy efficiency, which matters most in battery-powered robots and drones. The right panel shows raw TOPS for laptop chips. Companies quote TOPS in different ways that can double or even quadruple the headline number, so the chart puts every chip on the same basis. Even if the SpacemiT processor reaches 30 TOPS, this is still short of Microsoft’s bar of 40. By The Register’s estimate, even Alibaba’s best design would roughly match Apple’s M1 ( The Register , March 25). [5] Zhang Xiaolei, Dai Zibin, Guo Pengfei, et al., “Design and Verification of a RISC-V-Based AES Cryptographic Acceleration Engine [基于RISC-V的AES密码加速引擎设计与验证],” Application of Electronic Technique [电子技术应用] 49, no. 2 (2023): 39–44. Results are from FPGA prototypes built on the open-source Hummingbird E203 core. The post RISC-V Open-Source Chip Push Puts Strategy Over Capability appeared first on Jamestown .

title: III MEF Extends Curfew for Junior Members in Okinawa Following Murder Indictment

summary: 2026 年 10 月 31 日，美国军人、冲绳县警察和酒吧老板在冲绳市 Koza Gate 街进行联合巡逻，以促进负责任的基地外行为并加强与当地社区的关系。 III MEF 照片 美国军方延长了原定于周日到期的冲绳初级军人宵禁，并继续对购买和消费酒精实施限制。 E-1 至 E-4 年级的宵禁延长了 30 天，并从凌晨 12 点到凌晨 5 点限制他们在个人住房内。
content:
2026 年 10 月 31 日，美国军人、冲绳县警察和酒吧老板在冲绳市 Koza Gate 街进行联合巡逻，以促进负责任的基地外行为并加强与当地社区的关系。 III MEF 照片 美国军方延长了原定于周日到期的冲绳初级军人宵禁，并继续对购买和消费酒精实施限制。根据美国海军陆战队第三远征军 (MEF) 周四发布的新闻稿，E-1 至 E-4 级人员的宵禁延长了 30 天，并从上午 12 点到凌晨 5 点限制他们呆在个人住房内。宵禁此前曾针对较高级别人员实施，但后来被取消。但是，午夜后禁止所有人员在主要住所外购买或饮用酒精饮料。一名被指控在冲绳那霸抢劫并杀害一名妇女的海军陆战队员被捕，导致行动暂停 48 小时，随后于 10 月 8 日实施宵禁。该海军陆战队队员于 10 月 25 日被起诉。服务新闻稿中写道，在经过详细分析以及联合和跨机构领导人的反馈后，第三海军陆战队远征部队选择延长宵禁。本杰明·T·中将
第三远征军司令兼冲绳地区协调员沃森会见了冲绳地区协调委员会的代表，讨论了降低整个部队风险的前进方向，并在日本驻日美军的同意下发布了更新后的自由指南。该指南涵盖的时期为11月8日至12月。 7. 指挥官保留在条件允许时在各自指挥范围内制定更具限制性的自由政策的能力，并鼓励指挥官向部队明确传达这些决定。 2026 年 10 月 6 日，美国海军陆战队中将、第三海军陆战远征军司令本杰明·T·沃森（中右）在日本冲绳考特尼营举行的参谋会议上与主要领导人发表讲话。沃森向第三海军陆战队远征军领导人发表讲话，强调了海军陆战队的核心价值观以及他对整个部队的标准、纪律和问责制的期望。指导意见中写道：“在未来几周内，冲绳地区协调员将把反思期间制定的更广泛的评估结果和建议转发给驻日美军供考虑。”更新后的自由准则恰逢周六宵禁期间冲绳一名海军陆战队员因涉嫌酒后驾车被捕，这引发了对美军确保冲绳人员纪律的批评。
日本防卫大臣小泉进次郎在周一的新闻发布会上被问到时表示，日本防卫省已要求美国确保其人员严格纪律，采取有效措施防止再次发生，并严格执行夜间宵禁。根据文字记录，小泉表示：“我希望他们认真对待这段反思期间发生的事情，彻底执行纪律，确保此类事件不再发生。”日本防卫大臣表示，美国和日本官员正在讨论如何采取措施防止事件发生。 “我们的目的是尽快得出结论、公布并付诸行动。我们将继续与美方密切合作，彻底解决此事。”

【原文 English Original】
U.S. service members, Okinawa Prefectural Police officers and bar owners conducted a joint patrol at Koza Gate Street in Okinawa City to promote responsible off-base conduct and strengthen relationships with the local community on Oct. 31, 2026. III MEF photo The U.S. military extended a curfew on Okinawa for junior service members that was scheduled to expire on Sunday and is continuing to impose restrictions on the purchase and consumption of alcohol. The curfew for grades E-1 through E-4 was extended for 30 days and restricts them to their personal housing from 12 a.m. to 5 a.m., according to a Thursday news release from the III Marine Expeditionary Force (MEF). The curfew was previously in place for higher grade personnel but was lifted. However, all personnel are prohibited from the purchase or consumption of alcohol outside of their primary residence after midnight. The curfew was implemented on Oct. 8 following a 48-hour operational pause in response to the arrest of a Marine accused in the robbery and death of a woman in Naha, Okinawa. The Marine was indicted on the charges on Oct. 25. The III MEF opted to extend the curfew following a detailed analysis and feedback from joint and interagency leaders, reads the service release. Lt. Gen. Benjamin T. Watson, commanding general of III MEF and Okinawa Area Coordinator, met with representatives from the Okinawa Area Coordinating Committee to discuss the way forward to reduce risk across the force, and with concurrence from U.S. Forces Japan issued the updated liberty guidance. The guidance covers a period from Nov. 8-Dec. 7. Commanders retain the ability to establish more restrictive liberty policies within their respective commands when conditions warrant and are encouraged to clearly communicate those decisions to the force. U.S. Marine Corps Lt. Gen. Benjamin T. Watson, center-right, the commanding general of III Marine Expeditionary Force, speaks with key leaders during a staff meeting on Camp Courtney, Okinawa, Japan, Oct. 6, 2026. Watson addressed III MEF leaders, reinforcing the Marine Corps’ core values and his expectations for standards, discipline, and accountability across the force. US Marine Corps photo “In the coming weeks, the Okinawa Area Coordinator will forward the results of the broader assessment and recommendations developed during the Period of Reflection to U.S. Forces Japan for consideration,” reads the guidance. The updated liberty guidelines coincide with the Saturday arrest of a Marine in Okinawa during the curfew hours on suspicion of drunk driving, which has prompted criticism of the U.S. military’s efforts on ensuring personnel discipline in Okinawa. Japan Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, when asked in a Monday press conference, said that his Ministry have requested that the U.S. to ensure strict discipline among its personnel, implement effective measures to prevent a recurrence and strictly enforce the nighttime curfew. “I want them to take seriously what happened during this period of reflection and to thoroughly enforce discipline and ensure that such incidents do not recur,” said Koizumi, according to a transcript . U.S. and Japanese officials are in discussions on how to implement measures to prevent incidents from occurring, the Japanese Defense Minister said. “Our intention is to reach conclusions as soon as possible, announce them and put them into action. We will continue to work closely with the U.S. side to thoroughly address this matter,” said Koizumi. For exercise Keen Sword, which ran from Oct. 19-29, the municipal authorities of Yonaguni Island and Ishigaki Island requested the Japan Ministry of Defense to ensure U.S. military personnel carrying out training on their islands during Keen Sword were restricted to the training areas, not allowed liberty, prohibited from consuming alcohol and when moving through civilian areas were accompanied by Japan Self-Defense Force personnel, according to documents posted on municipal government website. Japan Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has also made it a priority to address the issues surrounding the U.S. presence in Okinawa. “Even now, more than 80 years after the end of the war, Okinawa Prefecture still has a large concentration of U.S. military facilities and areas and we take seriously the heavy burden of these bases that the people of Okinawa bear. What is important is to steadily produce results one by one, and we will do our utmost to realize a reduction of the base burden in Okinawa in a tangible way,” the Japanese Prime Minister said during the Okinawa Policy Council meeting on Friday . Friday’s meeting was the first one held in 13 years, which saw Takaichi and her cabinet ministers meeting with Okinawa Governor Genta Koja and prefectural officials to discuss matters pertaining to the island, which included the U.S. military presence as well as economic and development issues. In a Friday post on X , Koja outlined his request in regard to the U.S. military presence in Okinawa. “Regarding the reduction of the burden related to military bases, we called for the removal of the dangers posed by Futenma Air Station as soon as possible, the establishment of a clear timeline for its return, the prevention of any recurrence of incidents involving U.S. military personnel and a fundamental review of the Japan-U.S. Status of Forces Agreement,” reads the post. In his regularly scheduled press conference on Friday , Koizumi said he told Koja that the MOD would take the governor’s request seriously and do its utmost to reduce the burden of U.S. military bases on Okinawa. “The Ministry of Defense will promptly consider what kind of response is possible based on the requests received today,” said Koizumi.

Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

title: All five defendants in San Po Kong subversion case intend to plead guilty, court hears
zh_title: 新蒲岗颠覆案五名被告均拟认罪
summary: 两名男子因涉嫌在新蒲岗一栋工业大楼进行非法武器训练而被捕，他们向香港法院表示，他们打算承认共谋颠覆罪。湾仔区域法院。资料图片：HKFP。据当地媒体报道，学生邓毅博和服务员陈晓俊周四在区域法院出庭。辩方告诉陈士丹法官，两人计划认罪。两人是去年 12 月被指控串谋颠覆罪的五名被告之一。所有五人现已在法庭上表示
content:
两名男子因涉嫌在新蒲岗一栋工业大楼进行非法武器训练而被捕，他们向香港法院表示，他们打算承认共谋颠覆罪。湾仔区域法院。资料图片：HKFP。据当地媒体报道，学生邓毅博和服务员陈晓俊周四在区域法院出庭。辩方告诉陈士丹法官，两人计划认罪。两人是去年 12 月被指控串谋颠覆罪的五名被告之一。五人现已在法庭上表示他们打算认罪。法官表示，五人定于明年 3 月 15 日一起提出抗辩。在此之前，他们将继续被还押。据当地媒体报道，十月份，另外三名被告——学生黄杰伦、保安彭嘉良和保安李俊森——告诉法庭，他们将承认颠覆罪指控。黄还被指控持有儿童色情制品。检方10月在法庭上表示，已与辩方达成认罪协议：在黄承认颠覆罪后，持有儿童色情制品的指控将被存档。去年 12 月，唐和陈被指控时均为 23 岁。李当时26岁，彭24岁，黄21岁。2024年10月1日，人们在香港历史博物馆观看有关国家安全的视频装置。
图片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。检方指称，2024年11月1日至2025年12月11日期间，五名被告伙同及伙同其他不明人士，组织、策划、实施或参与以武力或以武力相威胁的行为，以颠覆国家政权、推翻香港特别行政区权力机构。根据第二十三条逮捕 这五人是去年12月11日和12月12日被捕的10人之一。警司周学贤表示，警方于 12 月 11 日持法院搜查令突击搜查新蒲岗工业大厦的一个单位，发现里面有 6 名男子，其中一名正在为其他人进行战斗训练。周说，警方缴获了五支气步枪、两支气手枪、五把军刀和一把长剑的仿制品，以及带有反政府标语的物品。他用粤语说：“此外，我们还发现了疑似爆炸物。”他补充说，警方爆炸品处理科正在检查这些物品。警方其后在大埔及油麻地拘捕另外三名男子。 12月12日，他们逮捕了一名妇女。所有这些人都是根据《维护国家安全条例》中的“非法钻探”条款被捕的，该条例是该市当地制定的安全立法，称为第 23 条。其中五人后来被指控串谋颠覆国家政权。

【原文 English Original】
Two men have told a Hong Kong court that they intend to plead guilty to conspiracy to commit subversion after they were arrested on suspicion of illegal weapons training in an industrial building in San Po Kong. District Court in Wan Chai. File photo: HKFP. Student Tang Ngai-pok and waiter Chan Hiu-chun appeared at the District Court on Thursday, local media reported . The defence told Judge Stanley Chan that the duo planned to plead guilty to the charges. The two are among five defendants who were charged with conspiracy to commit subversion last December. All five have now stated in court that they intend to plead guilty. The judge said the five were set to enter their pleas together on March 15 next year. They will remain remanded in custody until then. In October, the other three defendants – student Wong Kit-lun, security guard Gallian Pang and security guard Lee Chun-sum – told the court that they would plead guilty to the subversion charges, local media reported . Wong was also charged with possession of child pornography. The prosecution said in court in October that a plea bargain had been reached with the defence: after Wong pleaded guilty to subversion, the charge of possession of child pornography would be left on file. Tang and Chan were both 23 years old when they were charged last December. Lee was 26 at the time, while Pang was 24 and Wong was 21. People watch a video installation on national security in the Hong Kong Museum of History, on October 1, 2024. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The prosecution alleged that between November 1, 2024 and December 11, 2025, the five defendants conspired together and with other persons unknown to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by force or threat of force with a view to subverting state power and overthrowing the body of power of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Arrests under Article 23 The five were among a group of 10 people who were arrested on December 11 and December 12 last year. Superintendent Chow Hok-yin said that officers raided a unit at the San Po Kong industrial building on December 11 with a court warrant and found six men inside, one providing combat training to the others. Officers seized five air rifles, two air pistols, replicas of five military knives and a long sword, as well as items bearing anti-government slogans, Chow said. “Additionally, we found objects suspected to be explosives,” he said in Cantonese, adding that the objects were being examined by the force’s Explosive Ordnance Disposal Bureau. Police later arrested another three men in Tai Po and Yau Ma Tei. On December 12, they arrested a woman. All of them were arrested under the “unlawful drilling” provision of the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, the city’s locally enacted security legislation known as Article 23. Five were later charged with conspiracy to commit subversion.

title: How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation
zh_title: 上海基金经理康伟如何将他的妻子 Alice Huang 介绍给 Jensen，并建立了价值 75 亿美元的 Nvidia AI GPU 走私业务

content:
黄仁勋经历了令人震惊的失宠——从地球上最富有的人之一、人工智能繁荣的主要推动者之一，到卷入两起婚外情丑闻，并在不到两周的时间里从英伟达辞职。虽然许多人都关注这位英伟达前首席执行官与爱丽丝·黄（Alice Huang）的关系，后者据称向中国情报部门传递信息，但《华尔街日报》深入挖掘了将她介绍给詹森的人——上海的明星基金经理康伟，他恰好也是黄女士的丈夫。有报道称，康伟在2010年代认识了黄仁勋，当时他的投资公司大量涉足中国游戏公司。目前尚不清楚这段介绍是否早于康与爱丽丝的关系和婚姻，但与黄女士关系密切的消息人士表示，她在 2020 年代就能够与詹森走近。据《华尔街日报》报道，尽管是情侣，但康似乎接受了爱丽丝与詹森的关系，与这对夫妇关系密切的人表示，康经常开玩笑说她是亿万富翁的私人助理。不过，康伟不仅仅是一名普通的企业高管。在2007年接手中海基金之前，他曾作为申银万国的策略师在金融界名声大噪。这使他成为当时中国最年轻的共同基金总裁之一，最终于2010年独自创业并创立了上海河西。
也正是在这个时候，黄乐（黄乐）进入金融行业，先是在香港汇丰银行的私人银行部门工作，后来转到中信证券，并担任副总裁职务。正是在中信工作期间，黄乐与康有交集。上海河西于2014年和2015年与该证券公司签署了协议，到2016年，公司登记记录显示黄女士已加入该投资公司。据《经济时报》报道，黄爱丽入驻上海河西后，她获得了该公司25%的股份，而这些股份全部来自于康。剩余股份由康伟（48.75%）和他的商业伙伴朱晓明（26.25%）共同持有，黄丽娟（Alice Huang）通过上海玉玺投资管理咨询有限公司持有25%的股权。与此同时，康伟也开始向他的商业伙伴和投资者介绍黄丽娟（Alice Huang）作为他的妻子。一年后，朱和康在河西基金的一项投资获得了一笔巨额意外之财，两人在如何分配利润的问题上发生了争执。尽管如此，该交易产生的巨额利润使上海河西以约5亿元人民币从中国企业集团世纪华通手中收购了视频游戏公司杭州盛丰。
交易两年后，即2019年，杭州盛丰的所有权转移给一家境外实体，该实体最终并入Osmanthus Vale Holdings——一家在英属维尔京群岛注册成立的控股公司，并将黄乐（Alice Huang的中文名字）列为其唯一所有者。随后，该公司成立不到两个月就被第七大道控股收购。虽然黄女士是这笔交易的签署人，但据信她充当了“白手套”的角色，即代表他人行事以隐瞒身份的人，但目前尚不清楚这是针对上海河西和康维还是其他第三方。关于Alice H的信息并不多

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang had a stunning fall from grace — from being one of the richest people on Earth and one of the primary drivers of the AI boom to being implicated in two extramarital affair scandals and resigning from Nvidia in under two weeks. While many are focused on the former Nvidia chief’s relationship with Alice Huang, who was allegedly passing on information to Chinese intelligence , the Wall Street Journal dug deeper into the person who introduced her to Jensen — Kang Wei, a star fund manager in Shanghai who also happened to be Ms. Huang’s husband. There have been reports that Kang Wei met Jensen Huang in the 2010s, when his investment firm was heavily involved in Chinese gaming companies. It’s not clear if this introduction predated Kang’s relationship and marriage to Alice, but sources close to Ms. Huang said that she was able to get close to Jensen by the 2020s. Despite being a couple, the WSJ reported that Kang seemingly accepted Alice’s relationship with Jensen, with people close to the couple saying that he would often joke that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire. Kang Wei is not just an average business executive, though. He made a name for himself in the finance world as a strategist for Shenyin Wanguo before taking over the Zhonghai Fund in 2007. This made him one of the youngest mutual fund chiefs in China at that time, before finally setting out on his own and founding Shanghai Hexi in 2010. It was also around this time that Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le, entered the financial industry, first working at HSBC’s private banking arm in Hong Kong, before moving to CITIC Securities, where she attained a vice president position. It was during her time at CITIC that Alice crossed paths with Kang. Shanghai Hexi signed a deal with the securities firm in 2014 and 2015, and by 2016, corporate registry records show that Ms. Huang had joined the investment firm. The Economic Times reports Alice Huang’s move into Shanghai Hexi resulted in her getting a 25% stake in the company, all of which came from Kang. The remaining shares were shared between Kang Wei, with 48.75%, and his business partner, Zhu Xiaoming, with 26.25%, with Alice Huang’s 25% ownership stake being held through Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management Consulting Co., Ltd. Meanwhile, Kang also started introducing Alice Huang as his wife to his business associates and investors. One year later, Zhu and Kang had a falling out when one of their investments under a Hexi fund resulted in a major windfall, with the two partners disagreeing on how the profits were to be shared. Nevertheless, the massive profit generated by the deal allowed Shanghai Hexi to purchase Hangzhou Shengfeng, a video game company, for around 500 million yuan from Chinese conglomerate Century Huatong. Two years after the transaction, in 2019, Hangzhou Shengfeng’s ownership was transferred to an offshore entity, which was eventually consolidated under Osmanthus Vale Holdings — a holding company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands and listed Huang Le, Alice Huang’s Chinese name, as its sole owner. It was then purchased by 7Road Holdings less than two months after it was founded. While Ms. Huang was the signatory in this deal, it’s believed that she served as a “white glove,” a person who operates on behalf of another to conceal their identity — but it remains unclear if this was for Shanghai Hexi and Kang Wei or some other third party. There is not much information on Alice Huang’s activities between 2019 and 2021. However, Shanghai Hexi invested in Shanghai Longjing Information Technology, a data center-focused subsidiary of Century Huatong in 2020, where Ms. Huang served as a director between 2021 and 2022, according to a report by The Wire China . At about the same time, 7Road Holdings expanded into cloud computing, just before ChatGPT brought AI LLMs to the forefront. The U.S. government’s ban on the export of Nvidia chips to China put this investment in jeopardy, though, forcing it to spin off the business as 7Road International in Singapore. We don’t know when 7Road Holdings sold its Singapore subsidiary, but corporate records show that by the time the company was renamed Megaspeed in March 2023, it was already under the ownership of Huang Le Limited and led by Ms. Huang. It was sold again in November 2023 to Swiftdata, a company owned by Singaporean Tan Yong Pong. Axios said that she left the firm as a managing director soon after this acquisition, but sources said that she kept working with the company afterward, with Kang Wei helping her get it off the ground. In the same year, Shanghai Century Litong was founded to build AI data centers in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with Jiangsu Lettall Electronic Co., an electronic components manufacturer, holding a 90% stake, while the remaining 10% is owned by Century Longteng, as reported by BigGo Finance . It should be noted that Century Longteng was renamed from Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management, with the firm pivoting its business from finance to cloud computing, and that even though Alice Huang has already exited the company by this time, it’s under the control of Huang Yu, who some sources say is Ms. Huang’s sister. A year after these data center acquisitions, Alice Huang began to be spotted in public with the former Nvidia CEO. A LinkedIn post showed her having drinks with a leather-clad Jensen Huang alongside other tech executives from NetThunder and Gigabyte at a post-Computex 2024 event. She was once again seen having dinner with him in a Taipei restaurant as reporters tried to interview him while one kid demanded his attention off camera. But more than these public sightings, Alice herself boasted about her “closeness” to the then CEO. People close to her said that she regularly posted photos with Jensen on her WeChat account, and even shared others with potential customers to help establish her credibility. She even reportedly claimed that Mr. Huang would celebrate her birthdays with restaurant dinners and gifts, with one Nvidia China sales employee also saying that she was a familiar face at the company’s annual event for China partners. An investigation revealed that from 2023 to 2025, Megaspeed imported $4.6 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips, while another $2 billion was routed through Speedmatrix , Megaspeed’s subsidiary with offices in Johor, Malaysia. Shanghai Century Litong also reportedly bought AI GPUs from other sources, with estimates putting the total number of banned chips moved through Alice Huang’s assistance at around 240,000, putting the shipments’ worth at around $7.5 billion. But even as Ms. Huang was making her international moves, Kang Wei was facing trouble at home. Chinese regulators fined him 2.5 million yuan, or approximately $380,000, in 2025, for violating sections of China’s Securities Law. This also led to a warning letter against him, issued in August 2026 by the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Despite running into trouble with the authorities, this massive paper trail showed how Kang Wei actively made moves that put Alice Huang close to Jensen Huang. Some questions remain, though, about the U.S. intelligence community’s claims that she worked with the Ministry of State Security (MSS), China’s primary intelligence and counterintelligence agency. If it’s true that Alice Huang worked with the MSS and passed on information to the agency, did she specifically target Jensen Huang, or did the spy agency simply discover their indiscretion and use that to force her to cooperate? Was all this planned by the MSS, or were they just shrewd business moves that allowed Kang to make more money while going under the radar of regulators? These are questions that only Kang Wei and Alice Huang (or the Chinese spy agency) can answer. But no matter the case, the fact remains that China acquired advanced AI chips that were supposed to be out of its reach because of this couple’s connections.

title: TIMELINE: Jensen Huang’s fall from Nvidia grace
zh_title: 时间表：黄仁勋从 Nvidia 的恩典中跌落
source: Rappler 菲律宾（调查/南海/选举）
summary: 黄仁勋从英伟达辞职之前，丑闻仍在发酵，其后果震撼了科技行业和地缘政治。他与女商人、被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽（Alice Huang，无亲属关系）和两名英伟达员工的婚外情被发现，在中美关系紧张和人工智能主导地位争夺之际，这可能会颠覆该公司的业务。英伟达董事会对黄仁勋成为外国情报行动目标的报道展开了独立调查。黄仁勋是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在人工智能问题上的盟友和顾问
content:
黄仁勋从英伟达辞职之前，丑闻仍在发酵，其后果震撼了科技行业和地缘政治。他与女商人、被指控为中国间谍的黄爱丽（Alice Huang，无亲属关系）和两名英伟达员工的婚外情被发现，在中美关系紧张和人工智能主导地位争夺之际，这可能会颠覆该公司的业务。英伟达董事会对黄仁勋成为外国情报行动目标的报道展开了独立调查。黄仁勋是美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在人工智能问题上的盟友和顾问，这增强了美国对人工智能领导地位的渴望。作为私营部门的领导人，黄仁勋对英伟达处理器的走向具有影响力，这一丑闻的影响引发了关于美国是否应该允许先进人工智能芯片出售给中国的争论。以下是导致黄仁勋倒台的关键点的时间表：JENSEN 和 ALICE。 2024 年 6 月 7 日发布的一张照片显示，NVIDIA 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 与一名女性在台湾台北，经路透社消息人士确认为 Alice Huang。路透社于 2024 年 6 月 7 日获得：新加坡 Megaspeed 的黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 和 Alice Huang 的第一张已知照片。两人在台北电脑展上坐在一起。 2025 年 1 月：美国总统唐纳德·特朗普首次会见黄仁勋。这次会议在白宫举行。外出就餐。
2026 年 11 月 9 日获得的 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，路透社与单独获得的照片进行比较后，路透社确认一名女性为 Alice Huang，她于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台湾台北一家餐厅与 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋（黑衣）一起参加晚宴。CTI 通过 REUTERS TV 2025 年 5 月 22 日：看到黄仁勋和 Alice Huang 一起离开台北的一家餐厅。 2025 年 12 月 8 日：特朗普表示，美国将允许英伟达向中国出口其第二好的人工智能芯片 H200 处理器。 2026 年春季：据《纽约时报》11 月报道，国务卿马可·卢比奥监督起草一份机密备忘录，警告特朗普政府高级官员黄仁勋与黄爱丽丝关系密切。 2026 年 3 月 25 日：特朗普任命黄仁勋为总统科学技术顾问委员会成员。 2026 年 5 月：黄仁勋加入特朗普的美国代表团访问中国，会见中国国家主席习近平。特朗普旨在敦促北京向美国企业开放。 9 月 14 日：黄仁勋在年度 All-In 峰会现场录音期间接到唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 的电话。两人反对减缓人工智能发展的提议，并讨论了美国在人工智能领域的领导地位。 9月24日，中国国家主席习近平对美国进行国事访问期间，黄仁勋和妻子洛丽出席特朗普举办的白宫国宴。
10 月 8 日：特朗普授予黄仁勋国家科学奖章，这是美国授予科学家和工程师以及其他科技行业领袖的最高荣誉。在特朗普颁奖的同一天，总统透露在 2026 年夏季购买了最多 160 万美元并出售了最多 100 万美元的 Nvidia 股票。 10 月 29 日：《纽约时报》（NYT）报道黄仁勋和 Alice Huang 关系“密切”。报告补充说，美国情报官员担心黄爱丽代表中国情报部门行事。与此同时，英伟达表示这种关系并不“不寻常”。 11 月 5 日：美国众议院共和党议员寻求

【原文 English Original】
The resignation of Jensen Huang from Nvidia comes after a scandal still unfolding, with its aftereffects rocking both the tech industry and geopolitics. The discovery of his extramarital affairs — with businesswoman and alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang (no relation) and two Nvidia employees — have threatened to upend the business amid US-China tensions and a race for AI dominance. Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation into reports Huang was targeted in a foreign intelligence operation. Huang is an ally and adviser to US President Donald Trump on matters of artificial intelligence, which feeds into American aspirations for AI leadership. As a private-sector leader, Huang wielded influence as to where Nvidia processors could go, and the fallout from this scandal brings up the debate over whether the US should allow advanced AI chips to be sold to China. Below is a timeline of key points leading up to Jensen Huang’s fall: JENSEN AND ALICE. A photo shows NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with a woman confirmed by a Reuters source to be Alice Huang in Taipei, Taiwan released on June 7, 2024. Obtained by Reuters June 7, 2024: The first known photo of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed is seen. The two are seated together at Computex Taipei. January 2025: US President Donald Trump meets Jensen Huang for the first time. This meeting is held at the White House. EATING OUT. A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (in black) at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan May 22, 2025. CTI via REUTERS TV May 22, 2025: Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are seen leaving a restaurant together in Taipei. December 8, 2025: Trump said the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors, its second-best AI chips, to China. Spring of 2026: Secretary of State Marco Rubio ​oversees drafting of classified memo warning senior Trump administration officials that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, according to a November New York Times report . March 25, 2026: Trump appoints Jensen Huang to his President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. May 2026: Jensen Huang joins a US delegation of Trump’s that was visiting China to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump aimed to urge Beijing to open up to US business. September 14: Jensen Huang takes a phone call from Donald Trump during a ​live taping of the annual All-In summit. The two speak against proposals to slow AI development and discuss US leadership in AI. September 24: Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, attend a White House state dinner hosted by Trump during the state visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to the US. October 8: Trump awards Jensen Huang the National Medal of Science, the United States’ highest honor for scientists and engineers, alongside other tech industry ​leaders. The same day Trump gave the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million in Nvidia stock during the summer of ​2026. October 29: The New York Times (NYT) reports that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang had a “close relationship.” The report added US intelligence officials were concerned Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Nvidia meanwhile says the relationship was not “unusual.” November 5: Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives seek a closed-door briefing on November 18 from Jensen Huang on the allegations detailed in the NYT report. November 8: Jensen Huang tells Nvidia employees he was unfaithful to his wife, without giving specifics. Nvidia’s board launches an independent investigation into reports the CEO was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Must Read Nvidia probes whether CEO Huang was target of foreign intelligence effort as he admits affair November 9: Nvidia and Jensen Huang are sued in a proposed class action accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang’s ties with a suspected Chinese spy. November 10: Jensen Huang’s affair facilitated the shipment of at least $7.5 billion ​worth of the company’s chips to Chinese firms, The Information reported . Meanwhile, Republican US Senator Kevin Cramer calls for Jensen Huang’s resignation, and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer calls on Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act, which would give Congress power over advanced chip exports. November 11: The ⁠CEO also ​had an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to ​him, according to a NYT report. The Nvidia board meets to decide on Jensen Huang’s ouster. Must Read Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down in big blow to AI boom November 12: Nvidia announces Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO . Colette Kress, executive vice president and CFO of Nvidia, was appointed interim CEO while the board begins a search for a permanent replacement. A separate report found sources that said Jensen Huang had a second affair with a different, unnamed Nvidia employee. – with reports from Reuters/Rappler.com

summary: 禽流感爆发后香港暂停京都家禽进口中国劳工布告栏 星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 香港在禽流感爆发后暂停京都家禽进口 在 H5 禽流感爆发后，香港于 11 月 13 日暂停从日本京都府进口家禽和鸡蛋。该禁令在日本当局发出通知后立即生效。贸易数据显示，香港进口了约1,030吨冷冻家禽，近250家加工厂香港食品安全部门已指示当地业界
content:
禽流感爆发后香港暂停京都家禽进口中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
禽流感爆发后香港暂停京都家禽进口
H5禽流感爆发后，香港于11月13日暂停从日本京都府进口家禽和鸡蛋。该禁令在日本当局发出通知后立即生效。贸易数据显示，香港进口了约1,030吨冷冻家禽和近250家加工厂
香港食品安全当局已指示本地业界，自 11 月 13 日星期五起立即暂停从日本京都府进口禽肉及相关产品，包括禽蛋。预防性进口禁令是由日本农业当局正式通知该县爆发高致病性H5禽流感而触发的，旨在保障全境公共卫生。
食物环境卫生署食物安全中心证实，该措施适用于所有源自京都府的禽肉及禽蛋货物。食品安全监管机构发言人解释说，在日本农林水产省就该地区发生的疾病发出警报后，立即实施了进口管制。
该发言人补充说，该中心已就疫情与日本当局建立了直接沟通，并将在兽医遏制措施的实施过程中保持密切联系。此外，当地官员将密切关注世界动物卫生组织与日本兽医机构发布的最新疫情动态和监测数据，并指出，如果流行病学情况需要，政府将采取进一步的监管应对措施。
政府统计处编制的贸易数据反映，本地对日本家禽供应的需求稳定，今年首九个月，香港从日本进口约1,030吨冷冻家禽肉和约2.4994亿个家禽蛋。
食品安全当局强调，边境管制站仍严格执行标准进口检验协议，以确保只有合规且无病的货物才能到达当地消费者，并建议家禽进口商和餐饮经营者在暂停期间密切监控采购来源。

Hong Kong halts Kyoto poultry imports after avian flu outbreak | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 13 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong halts Kyoto poultry imports after avian flu outbreak
Hong Kong suspended poultry and egg imports from Japan's Kyoto Prefecture on 13 November after an H5 avian influenza outbreak. The ban, effective immediately, follows a notification from Japanese authorities. Trade data show Hong Kong imported about 1,030 tonnes of frozen poultry and nearly 250 mill
Hong Kong food safety authorities have instructed the local trade to suspend the import of poultry meat and related products, including poultry eggs, from Kyoto Prefecture in Japan with immediate effect on Friday 13 November. The precautionary import ban was triggered by an official notification from Japanese agricultural authorities reporting an outbreak of highly pathogenic H5 avian influenza in the prefecture, aimed at safeguarding public health across the territory.
The Centre for Food Safety of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department confirmed that the measure applies to all poultry meat and poultry egg consignments originating from Kyoto Prefecture. A spokesman for the food safety watchdog explained that import controls were enacted swiftly following an alert from the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Japan regarding the disease occurrence in the region.
The spokesman added that the centre had already established direct communication with Japanese authorities regarding the outbreak and would maintain close contact as veterinary containment measures proceed. In addition, local officials will monitor ongoing epidemic updates and surveillance data published by the World Organisation for Animal Health alongside Japanese veterinary agencies, noting that the government will implement further regulatory responses should the epidemiological situation warrant.
Trade figures compiled by the Census and Statistics Department reflect steady local demand for Japanese poultry supplies, with Hong Kong importing approximately 1,030 tonnes of frozen poultry meat and roughly 249.94 million poultry eggs from Japan during the first nine months of this year.
Food safety authorities stressed that standard import inspection protocols remain strictly enforced at border control points to ensure that only compliant and disease-free consignments reach local consumers, advising poultry importers and catering operators to monitor sourcing origins closely during the suspension.

zh_title: 观点：中国休战可能会阻碍加拿大稀土生产
source: 北方矿工 Northern Miner（北美矿业）
summary: 观点：中国休战可能会阻碍加拿大稀土开采 - 2023 年 8 月，北方矿业地质学家 Ed Walker 在魁北克北部 Torngat Metals 的 Strange Lake 稀土项目中处理钻芯。图片来源：Torngat Metals/Business Wire。作者：Noah Chaikin，2026 年 11 月 13 日 与中国的长期贸易休战可能会缓解制造商对稀土供应的担忧，同时使潜在的加拿大替代品更难融资。 11 月 9 日，北京将 2025 年 10 月对全球稀土出口的更广泛限制的暂停期限延长至 2027 年 1 月 10 日，以配合与华盛顿的贸易休战。李
content:
观点：中国休战可能会阻碍加拿大稀土生产 - 《北方矿业报》
2023 年 8 月，地质学家 Ed Walker 在魁北克北部 Torngat Metals 的 Strange Lake 稀土项目中处理钻芯。图片来源：Torngat Metals/Business Wire。
作者：诺亚·柴金 2026 年 11 月 13 日
与中国更长期的贸易休战可能会缓解制造商对稀土供应的担忧，同时使潜在的加拿大替代品更难融资。 11 月 9 日，北京将 2025 年 10 月对全球稀土出口的更广泛限制的暂停期限延长至 2027 年 1 月 10 日，以配合与华盛顿的贸易休战。 2025 年 4 月推出的许可规则仍然有效，包括影响电动机中使用的永磁体的许可规则。
与成熟的中国供应商合作使制造商有理由推迟与加拿大矿山开发商的供应协议，这些协议可能需要测试新材料并接受更高的价格。 Wicheeda 和 Strange Lake 都没有生产。买家将承诺未来的供应，帮助开发商获得建设项目所需的融资。
据国际能源署 (IEA) 称，到 2025 年，发达经济体政府对关键矿产的融资承诺将达到约 650 亿美元（918 亿加元），是 2023 年水平的四倍多。该机构追踪的 24 家主要矿业公司的资本支出当年下降了 9%，其中电池金属支出下降最为明显。对于加拿大稀土开发商来说，公众的支持仍然需要与愿意致力于替代供应的客户相匹配。
悉尼大学美国研究中心九月份警告说，中国放松管制可能会让坚定的买家比犹豫不决的竞争对手付出更多的代价。该中心将难以吸引买家与 Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) 于 2026 年 5 月对其澳大利亚 Nolans 项目做出投资决定之前的多年拖延联系在一起。 Arafura 要求在提取高级债务之前签订具有约束力的销售协议，涵盖计划中的 80% 的钕和镨产量，这说明了买家犹豫不决会阻碍融资的原因。
Defense Metals（多伦多证券交易所代码：DEFN；美国场外交易代码：DFMTF）提议的不列颠哥伦比亚省 Wicheeda 稀土项目收到了加拿大出口发展局 2025 年 6 月表示的安排高达 2.5 亿美元开发和建设贷款的兴趣。融资仍以贷款人的项目审查为条件，而 2026 年 5 月与韩国韩华海洋 (KRX: 042660) 和韩华集团 (KRX: 000880) 签署的供应和投资备忘录并不保证购买。
这些讨论需要产生用于进一步分离的混合稀土碳酸盐的约束性销售，支持 Wicheeda 完成可行性研究并在 2027 年确保承购的目标，然后在 2028 年完成融资。
Torngat Metals 于 2025 年 10 月与法国加工商卡斯特 (Carester) 就魁北克北部的 Strange Lake 项目签署了为期 10 年的协议，这表明一些买家已经做出了多元化的长期承诺。该合同涵盖为 Carester 的 Caremag 子公司提供部分分离的含有镝和铽的流。
Torngat 正在为其拟议运营中的分离氧化物寻找更多买家。 2025 年 6 月宣布的高达 1.65 亿加元的公共贷款将用于支持施工前工作，从而使更大的建设融资方案有待整合。 Torngat 的目标是在 2030 年进行矿山调试，但需获得监管部门的批准。
