content:
这是一个与时间一样古老的故事。亿万富翁书呆子男孩遇见女孩。女孩后来被怀疑是间谍。 11 点的消息。哦，还有报道称他与一名直接下属的员工有染。当英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋犯下“浪漫”错误时，他不会半途而废。世界上最有价值的公司的老板——好吧，无论如何，直到最近——昨天，11 月 12 日公开辞去了首席执行官、总裁和董事会成员的职务，立即生效。我们不知道他是跳下去的还是被推的。他在承认有外遇后离开了。尽管他从未指定过外遇对象，但据报道，其中一件事是与黄乐（又名黄乐）发生的。她是中国公司 Megaspeed 的负责人，该公司是 Nvidia 的合作伙伴。 Megaspeed 被指控为中国政府的幌子，用于将 Nvidia 芯片转移到中国，尽管这一点尚未得到证实。一些美国官员还怀疑 [PDF] 她为中国情报部门工作，尽管美国司法部表示尚未就此得出结论。当《纽约时报》报道称詹森还与英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔有染时，压垮了詹森的棺材。哎呀，伙计！此后，英伟达首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 被任命为临时首席执行官。我怀疑她不会在这个岗位上呆太久。首席财务官不是首席执行官。这些工作根本不一样。在大多数公司中，黄仁勋将被首席运营官取代。这不可能发生在这里。
Nvidia 没有 COO。无论是在 Nvidia 内部还是外部，黄仁勋都被视为 Nvidia，Nvidia 也被视为黄仁勋。如今，亿万富翁首席执行官被视为无所不知、统治一切的神王。很多时候，这都是废话。英伟达的情况并非如此。黄仁勋于 1993 年 4 月 5 日与他人共同创立了 Nvidia。他在第一天就被任命为首席执行官，此后从未离开过这个职位。起初，公司步履蹒跚。当它于 1999 年发布 GeForce 256 并将其作为首款 GPU 进行营销时，它开始走上成为 PC 游戏玩家首选芯片制造商的道路。今天仍然如此。这是一个巨大的利基市场，但它并不能让一家公司成为价值数万亿美元的企业。不，当 2006 年 Nvidia 推出 CUDA 时，就达到了令人眼花缭乱的高度。这种编程架构向科学和其他非图形工作负载开放了 GPU 的并行处理能力。从那时起，CUDA 将成为大多数高性能和人工智能计算的基础。黄是这一切的中心。直到现在他还是这样。在 KubeCon 北美（Kubernetes 的贸易展）上，超过一半的人工智能项目都使用了 Kubernetes，我与许多 Nvidia 员工进行了交谈。他们都提到了两件事。首先，他们处于震惊状态。也许中美高层和政府官员都知道黄在玩火；我采访过的普通开发人员对此一无所知。
第二个是，黄仁勋每个月都会召开一次全体员工大会，他不是一场形式上的企业动员大会，而是回答每个人的问题，并给他们真正的答案。他很了解自己的技术，并且真正领导着他的公司，而不是仅仅给容易上当的股票买家留下深刻的印象。英伟达无法取代他。实在不行啊。我想起了 1985 年约翰·斯卡利 (John Sculley) 迫使史蒂夫·乔布斯 (Steve Jobs) 离开苹果公司的情景。如果你还没有老到记得的话，苹果公司曾一度表现不错，但到了 90 年代中期，它就迷失了方向。乔布斯下台后，苹果公司重新焕发了魔力，并开始崛起为世界顶级公司之一。

【原文 English Original】
It's a story as old as time. Billionaire nerd boy meets girl. Girl is later suspected of being a spy. News at 11. Oh, and it's also been reported that he was having an affair with one of his direct-report employees. When Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang makes a "romantic" blunder, he doesn't do it halfway. The boss of the world's most valuable company – well, it was until recently, anyway – publicly resigned yesterday, November 12, as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately. We don't know if he jumped or if he was pushed. He left after admitting to having an affair. Although he never named an affair partner, one of the affairs was reported to be with Alice Huang, AKA Huang Le. She's head of the Chinese company Megaspeed, which was an Nvidia partner. Megaspeed is accused of being a front for China's government that was used to transfer Nvidia chips to China, although this hasn't been proven. Some US officials also suspect [PDF] she's working for Chinese intelligence, although the DoJ said it hasn't yet reached a conclusion about this. The final nail in Jensen's coffin came when The New York Times reported he had also allegedly had an affair with Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. Jeeze, guy! In the aftermath, Nvidia's CFO, Colette Kress, was appointed interim CEO. She won't, I suspect, be in the job for long. CFOs are not CEOs. The jobs aren't remotely the same. In most companies, Huang would be replaced by the COO. That can't happen here. Nvidia doesn't have a COO. Both inside and outside of Nvidia, Huang is seen as Nvidia, and Nvidia as Huang. These days, billionaire CEOs are perceived as God-kings who know all and rule all. Much more often than not, that's BS. That isn't the case with Nvidia. Huang co-founded Nvidia on April 5, 1993. He was appointed CEO on day one, and he never left the job. At first, the company staggered forward. When it released the GeForce 256 in 1999 , which it marketed as the first GPU, it started on its path to becoming the chip manufacturer of choice for PC gamers. It still is today. That's a great niche, but it doesn't make a company a trillion-dollar business. No, the path to that dizzying height came when, in 2006, Nvidia unveiled CUDA . This programming architecture opened its GPUs' parallel-processing capabilities to scientific and other non-graphics workloads. From there, CUDA would become the foundation for most high-performance and AI computing. Huang was at the center of it all. He still was until now. At KubeCon North America , the trade show for Kubernetes, used in well over half of all AI projects, I spoke to many Nvidia employees. There were two things they all mentioned. First, they were in a state of shock. Maybe the top brass and government officials both in China and the US knew Huang was fooling with fire; the developer rank-and-file folks I spoke to hadn't had a clue. The second was that every month, Huang held an all-hands meeting where, instead of a per-forma corporate pep rally, he answered questions from everyone and gave them real answers. He knew his technology well and actually led his company instead of just impressing gullible stock buyers. Nvidia can't replace him. It really can't. I'm reminded of when John Sculley forced Steve Jobs out at Apple in 1985. If you're not old enough to remember, Apple did fine for a while, but then by the mid-90s, it lost its way. Apple got its mojo back, and started its rise to being one of the world's top companies only after Jobs came back in 1996 . The big difference, of course, is that Huang's not coming back. I heard many people say that Huang was "too big to fail." True, morality no longer matters much in the US – see Trump's kleptocracy – but this is different. Huang betrayed not just his wife, but his board, employees, and stockholders. If, as some suspect, the board knew full well what was going on, they should be tossed out too, but that's a story for another day. Oh, and as for Trump's suggestions that Apple's former CEO Tim Cook should become Nvidia's CEO? Give me a break. Now the question of the day is: how can Nvidia recover from this blow? I don't think it can. I used to say that I didn't know where the AI companies were going, but I was sure that so long as capital kept flowing into Big AI, Nvidia was the one company you could count on that would make money . I think I was wrong. What does that mean? In the short term, Nvidia stock, after dropping 14 percent in early trading on Thursday, is down "only" five percent. Despite all the Sturm und Drang over Huang's departure, the NASDAQ is actually, when I wrote this, up. Even Nvidia's bonds are holding steady . Amazon and Google, which have their own horses in the AI TPU races, are hoping, of course, that Nvidia's misfortune will help them lever open the AI hardware market. In these early hours, I don't see that happening. Frankly, I'm amazed at how stockowners are shaking off Huang's resignation. The AI fever dream, for now, is continuing unabated. That said, can this go on? This irrational exuberance rests on the belief that, no matter what happens, AI will continue to rule the stock market. Eventually, though, the bubble may pop, and that could put some strain on the global economy. For now, people are ignoring how bad this blow is, or perhaps they're not aware of it. In a few years, I expect Huang's affair will be seen as the first needle in the AI bubble. ®

content:
规避出口管制：彭博社报道称，爱丽丝·黄（黄仁勋丑闻的中心女性，与黄仁勋有染，美国情报官员认为她是中国间谍）可能参与了走私人工智能芯片，这些芯片随后被安装在上海的一个数据中心。彭博社报道称，“据一位因讨论敏感话题而要求匿名的知情人士透露，部分服务器最初出售给总部位于新加坡的 Nvidia 官方云合作伙伴 Aperia Cloud Services。” “但文件显示，这些硬件并没有留在这个岛国，而是落入了爱丽丝在上海一家庞大的人工智能设施中创立的一家中国公司手中。该项目与爱丽丝有很多联系，包括她所擅长的 Megaspeed 在 2024 年的投资者演示中使用了数据中心的渲染图。”彭博社继续说道：“具体来说，Aperia 从戴尔科技公司购买了 22 台包含 Nvidia H800 芯片的服务器，华盛顿在 2023 年限制这些服务器向中国销售。彭博社向一位知情人士提供了这些服务器的序列号，该人士证实 Aperia 是戴尔的客户。”这似乎违反了美国的贸易限制。
特朗普政府声称将非常积极地确保美国制造的芯片（例如英伟达制造的芯片）最终不会为中国人工智能提供动力，但现实要复杂得多。有人说商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克对英伟达很宽容。据《纽约时报》报道，卢特尼克“经常就如何监管先进技术的销售，特别是英伟达对亚洲的芯片销售与高级官员发生冲突”。 “这引起了政府和国会其他人的指责，称商务部与英伟达及其联合创始人黄仁勋过于亲密，尤其未能充分监管该公司对中国的芯片销售。”英伟达显然与商务部关系非常融洽：“现任和前任官员表示，在商务部，英伟达的待遇与其他公司不同，其问题得到高度重视并通过特定渠道发送。卢特尼克先生经常与黄先生打电话发消息，商务部精心准备在卢特尼克先生五楼办公室举行的私人会议。英伟达的所有事务都通过卢特尼克先生的高级副手杰夫·凯斯勒处理，据说他很少采取任何重大行动英伟达的总法律顾问还有权直接制定新规则，包括在影响该公司的法规草案中发表评论。
英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 在商务部内因积极主动的外展活动而闻名。去年底，商务部内部关于 Megaspeed 是否向中国走私英伟达芯片的调查被叫停，并在泰特直接联系商务部调查人员并援引凯斯勒先生的名义进行调查后，转交给了司法部。它影响了与中国的人工智能竞赛。纽约场景：布鲁克林弗拉特布什的一座建筑随机倒塌，造成八人死亡“消防队员和护理人员涌入现场。消防员将尸体倒入坑中

【原文 English Original】
Skirting export controls: Bloomberg is reporting that Alice Huang—the woman at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, with whom he had an affair and who is believed by U.S. intelligence officials to be a Chinese spy—possibly played a part in smuggling AI chips that were then installed at a data center in Shanghai. "Some of the servers were originally sold to Aperia Cloud Services, an official Nvidia Cloud Partner headquartered in Singapore, according to a person familiar with the matter, who requested anonymity to discuss a sensitive topic," reports Bloomberg. " But instead of staying in the island nation, the documents show, the hardware wound up in the hands of a Chinese company Alice founded, at a sprawling AI facility in Shanghai. That project has several ties to Alice, including that Megaspeed—which she was high up at—used a rendering of the data center in a 2024 investor presentation." "Specifically, Aperia purchased 22 servers from Dell Technologies Inc. that contained Nvidia's H800 chips," continues Bloomberg, "which Washington restricted from sale to China in 2023. Bloomberg provided serial numbers of those servers to a person familiar with the transaction, who confirmed that Aperia was Dell's customer." This appears to be in violation of U.S. trade restrictions. The Trump administration has claimed to be pretty aggressive with making sure U.S.-made chips, such as those manufactured by Nvidia, don't end up powering Chinese AI, but the reality is much more complicated. Some say Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has gone easy on Nvidia. Lutnick "has frequently clashed with top officials over how to regulate sales of advanced technology, particularly Nvidia's chip sales to Asia," reports The New York Times. "That has drawn accusations from others in the administration and in Congress that the Commerce Department has become too cozy with Nvidia and its co-founder, Jensen Huang, and failed to adequately police the firm's chip sales to China, in particular." Nvidia has apparently been very cozy with the Commerce Department: "Within the Commerce Department, Nvidia is treated differently than other firms, current and former officials say, with its issues given high priority and sent through specific channels. Mr. Lutnick frequently calls and messages with Mr. Huang, and the department prepares carefully for their private meetings together in Mr. Lutnick's fifth floor office. All Nvidia matters are routed through Jeff Kessler, a top deputy to Mr. Lutnick, who is said to rarely take any significant action without the commerce secretary's approval. Nvidia's general counsel has also been given direct access to shape new rules, including leaving comments in draft regulations affecting the company. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is known within the Commerce Department for his aggressive outreach. An inquiry inside the agency into whether Megaspeed was smuggling Nvidia chips into China was shut down late last year and transferred to the Justice Department after Mr. Teter reached out directly to Commerce Department investigators, invoking Mr. Kessler's name in doing so." It's likely more will come out regarding the Trump administration's willingness to look past issues with Jensen Huang—and the degree to which it's affected the AI race against China. Scenes from New York: A building in Flatbush, Brooklyn, randomly collapsed, leaving eight dead. "Firefighters and paramedics swarmed the scene. Firefighters poured into the pit where the excavation had been taking place, hauling aside brick and concrete in search of victims and survivors. Ambulances parked nearby, awaiting patients to deliver to hospitals. Soon, drones would hover over the scene—some operated by emergency workers, others by news crews," reported The New York Times. " A fire truck that had parked on Flatbush extended its long ladder directly into the apartments in the neighboring building that had been exposed to the open air — a jarring sight, like the cross-section of a dollhouse." QUICK HITS " Anthropic PBC 's initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter, as interest increases for potentially the biggest first-time share sale ever," reports Bloomberg. "Operators of small-town water stations locked out of control panels across the Midwest. Networks on two Texas-bound energy tankers breached as they crossed into the Atlantic Ocean. Hundreds of refrigerators in European grocery stores ratcheted up to a blistering 120 degrees Fahrenheit," reports The Wall Street Journal. " Three cyberattacks since this summer with real-world impacts and one main suspect: Iranian hackers." Was Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan totally wrong? asks Charles Lane at The Washington Post. "Dutch Prime Minister Rob ​Jetten will try to save his minority government from collapse in a meeting with coalition ‌partners on Friday, after a heated debate over wealth taxes exposed deep divisions a day earlier," reports Reuters. "Jetten's three-party coalition threatened to fall apart less than 9 months after its installation , as parties bickered over a deal with the left-wing opposition to support a ​2027 tax plan in exchange for a slight increase of wealth taxes." The post The Chinese Connection appeared first on Reason Magazine .

title: USS City of Bismarck Welcomes New Military Crew Commander

content:
2026 年 11 月 13 日

日本横须贺——

由军事海运司令部运营的远征快速运输舰俾斯麦市号（EPF 9）迎来了新任指挥官，中校。蒂亚·迈尔斯在横须贺舰队活动船上举行的仪式上。迈尔斯从中校手中接过指挥权。 VanAnh McCormick，在将该船移交给 MILCREW II 之前担任军事船员 I 的指挥官。

“从我们的人员流动开始，我们不再是 MILCREW II 和 CIVMAR；我们都是俾斯麦市号航空母舰，”迈尔斯在向由水手和公务员组成的混合船员发表的讲话中说道。 “‘保持媒体报道’是我们的全部工作！我们必须在场并准备好参与，同时互相支持，以确保我们的成功。Crew I 奠定了基础，我们的工作就是在此基础上继续发展。Possumus Efficiemus：我们可以而且我们将会实现。”

迈尔斯是南卡罗来纳州哥伦比亚人，2014 年从弗朗西斯马里恩大学毕业并获得数学学士学位后，被任命为海军军官。她还拥有海军研究生院的高级工商管理硕士学位。

在海上，迈尔斯曾在阿利伯克号航空母舰 (DDG 51)、珍珠港号航空母舰 (LSD 52) 和哈珀斯渡口号航空母舰 (LSD 49) 上服役。
在岸上，她在圣地亚哥海军水面和水雷作战发展中心和水面高级作战学校担任两栖作战战术教官。迈尔斯接替了麦考密克，麦考密克于 2026 年 7 月接管了 MILCREW I 的指挥权，并带领船员完成了有史以来的首次 EPF 部署。部署期间，船员航行超过4000海里，访问了4个海外港口。机组人员为“锐剑”演习提供了后勤保障，并完成了任务要求的所有准备工作。此外，供应部门还入围了 David M. Cook 食品服务卓越奖的决赛。

俾斯麦号是EPF级第九艘舰艇。这些浅吃水、全铝制商用双体船旨在以 35 节的平均速度将 600 短吨军用货物运输 1,200 海里。该船设有用于直升机操作的飞行甲板、车辆卸载坡道部署以及增强沿海操作和港口通道的浅吃水。这些能力使 EPF 能够在严峻或受损的港口提供灵活的物流支持、快速运输和救灾。

该船的船员由军事人员和文职海员组成。 MILCREW 轮流部署，基地设在圣地亚哥，而该舰的母港是横须贺，由美国第七舰队负责作战控制。
军事海运司令部负责指挥和支持大约 140 艘民用船只的行动，这些船只为美国海军舰船补充海上补给、执行专门任务、在全球范围内预置战斗货物、提供支持服务以及向部署的美国部队运输军事装备和补给品。

【原文 English Original】
13 November 2026

YOKOSUKA, Japan --

The expeditionary fast transport USS City of Bismarck (EPF 9), operated by Military Sealift Command, welcomed its new commanding officer, Lt. Cmdr. Tia Myers, during a ceremony aboard the ship at Fleet Activities Yokosuka. Myers assumed command from Lt. Cmdr. VanAnh McCormick, who served as the Military Crew I commander before turning the ship over to MILCREW II.

“Starting with our turnover, we are no longer MILCREW II and CIVMARs; we are all USS City of Bismarck,” Myers said in her address to the hybrid crew of sailors and civil service mariners. “It is all of our job to ‘keep the press!’ We have to be present and ready to engage while supporting each other to ensure our success. Crew I laid the foundation, and it is our job to build upon it. Possumus Efficiemus: We can and we will accomplish.”

A native of Columbia, South Carolina, Myers commissioned as a naval officer in 2014 after graduating from Francis Marion University with a bachelor’s degree in mathematics. She also holds an executive master’s degree in business administration from the Naval Postgraduate School.

At sea, Myers served aboard USS Arleigh Burke (DDG 51), USS Pearl Harbor (LSD 52) and USS Harpers Ferry (LSD 49).

Ashore, she served as an amphibious warfare tactics instructor at the Naval Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center and Surface Advanced Warfighting School in San Diego. Myers relieved McCormick, who took command of MILCREW I in July 2026 and led the crew through its first ever EPF deployment. During the deployment, the crew sailed more than 4,000 nautical miles and visited four overseas ports. The crew provided logistics support for Exercise Keen Sword and completed all ready for tasking requirements. In addition, the supply department became a finalist for the David M. Cook Food Service Excellence Award.

Bismarck is the ninth ship in the EPF class. These shallow-draft, all-aluminum, commercial-based catamarans are designed to transport 600 short tons of military cargo 1,200 nautical miles at an average speed of 35 knots. The ship features a flight deck for helicopter operations, a vehicle offload ramp deployment, and a shallow draft that enhances littoral operations and port access. These capabilities allow the EPF to deliver flexible logistics support, rapid transport and disaster relief in austere or damaged ports.

The ship operates with a hybrid crew of military personnel and civil service mariners. The MILCREWs rotate for deployments and are based in San Diego, while the ship is homeported in Yokosuka under the operational control of U.S. 7th Fleet.

Military Sealift Command directs and supports operations for approximately 140 civilian-crewed ships that replenish U.S. Navy ships at sea, conduct specialized missions, preposition combat cargo worldwide, provide support services, and transport military equipment and supplies to deployed U.S. forces.

title: Global Microsoft 365 outage disrupts services across 74 countries
zh_title: 全球 Microsoft 365 中断导致 74 个国家/地区的服务中断
summary: 全球 Microsoft 365 中断导致 74 个国家/地区的服务中断 |中国劳工布告栏 周五，2026 年 11 月 13 日·香港 香港和中国劳工英文新闻 全球 Microsoft 365 中断中断了 74 个国家/地区的服务 11 月 13 日，大规模的全球系统中断袭击了微软的云生产力套件，导致至少 74 个国家和地区的电子邮件、消息传递和人工智能服务瘫痪。香港航空公司表示，航班时刻表保持正常，但警告可能出现通讯延误。一场大规模的全球系统中断袭击了微软的云生产力套件
content:
全球 Microsoft 365 中断导致 74 个国家/地区的服务中断 |中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
全球 Microsoft 365 中断导致 74 个国家/地区的服务中断
11 月 13 日，微软的云生产力套件遭遇大规模全球系统中断，导致至少 74 个国家和地区的电子邮件、消息传递和人工智能服务瘫痪。香港航空公司表示，航班时刻表保持正常，但警告可能出现通讯延误。
据 The Standard 报道，11 月 13 日上午，微软的云生产力套件发生了大规模的全球系统中断，导致至少 74 个国家和地区的电子邮件、消息传递和人工智能服务瘫痪。
尽管 Microsoft 365 云服务在全球范围内出现广泛中断，香港主要客运航空公司确认其航班时刻表于 11 月 13 日保持正常，但航空公司警告旅客可能出现通信延误和后台中断。
这次中断影响了全球用户，电子邮件、消息平台和人工智能工具等服务都无法访问。此次中断的规模至少覆盖 74 个国家，凸显了全球企业和政府运营对微软云基础设施的依赖。
在另一项进展中，英伟达表示，美国的出口管制实际上将其排除在中国人工智能数据中心市场之外，但路透社的一份评论发现，围绕这家美国芯片制造商的受限处理器构建的中国计算项目价值超过 30 亿美元。
特朗普政府发言人表示，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的人工智能特别工作组成员于周四举行会议，讨论了鼓励美国关键部门报告人工智能网络攻击的方法。
在周五举行的2026星岛全球经济峰会上，香港科技大学计算机科学与工程系讲座教授贾家亚认为，人工智能的发展虽然深刻改变了工作模式，但不会造成大规模失业，而是会创造大量新的就业机会。

content:
流感季节进入第五个月，香港一名儿童死亡中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
流感季节进入第五个月香港一名儿童死亡
一名儿童死于严重流感，这是今年第三例此类死亡。由于流感活动仍高于基线，卫生官员敦促接种疫苗。本季度已记录了 29 例严重儿科病例。
卫生防护中心11月13日宣布，一名先前报告严重流感病例的儿童死亡，成为本港今年第三宗因流感死亡的儿童。
该地区自六月下旬以来一直处于流感季节，目前已持续四个多月。根据最新监测数据，尽管近几周总体流感活动出现下降迹象，但仍高于基线水平。
本季已记录29例儿童重症病例。其中22人康复出院，2人情况稳定，2人情况危急，3人死亡。
卫生防护中心主任梁哲贤医生提醒市民，本港仍处于流感季节。他指出，上一季的数据显示，未接种疫苗的儿童患流感严重并发症或死亡的可能性是接种季节性流感疫苗的儿童的五倍左右。
该中心敦促所有六个月或以上的人（有已知禁忌症的人除外）如果尚未接种疫苗，请立即接种。今年的季节性流感疫苗接种计划大约在两个月前开始，公共和私营医疗部门的疫苗供应充足。
合资格人士可在约270个公共服务点免费或资助流感疫苗注射，包括卫生署辖下110间指定诊所、医院管理局辖下76间家庭医学诊所及38间公立医院，以及基层医疗机构辖下45间地区康健中心及服务点。超过1,900名私家医生参与疫苗资助计划，在全港超过3,200个地点提供服务。
梁博士呼吁严格个人及环境卫生。高危人群，包括儿童、老人、慢性病患者或免疫力低下者，在乘坐公共交通工具或人员密集场所时应佩戴外科口罩。他警告说，孩子的病情可能会迅速恶化，如果出现呼吸急促、喘息、嘴唇发紫、胸痛、神志不清、持续发烧或抽搐等症状，家长应立即寻求紧急护理。

Friday, 13 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Child dies in Hong Kong as flu season enters fifth month
A child has died from severe influenza, the third such death this year. Health officials urge vaccination as flu activity remains above baseline. 29 severe paediatric cases have been recorded this season.
A child previously reported as a severe influenza case has died, becoming the third paediatric death from influenza in Hong Kong this year, the Centre for Health Protection announced on 13 November.
The territory has been in a flu season since late June, now lasting more than four months. While overall influenza activity has shown signs of declining in recent weeks, it remains above the baseline level, according to the latest surveillance data.
This season has recorded 29 severe cases among children. Of these, 22 have been discharged after recovery, two are in stable condition, two are in critical condition, and three have died.
Dr Leung Chit-yin, Director of the Centre for Health Protection, reminded the public that Hong Kong is still in the flu season. He noted that data from the previous season showed that unvaccinated children were about five times more likely to suffer severe complications or death from influenza compared with those who received the seasonal flu vaccine.
The centre urged all individuals aged six months or older, except those with known contraindications, to get vaccinated promptly if they have not yet done so. This year's seasonal influenza vaccination programme began about two months ago, and vaccine supplies in both public and private healthcare sectors are adequate.
Eligible persons can receive free or subsidised flu jabs at about 270 public service points, including 110 designated clinics under the Department of Health, 76 family medicine clinics and 38 public hospitals under the Hospital Authority, and 45 district health centres and service points under the Primary Health Care Agency. More than 1,900 private doctors are participating in the Vaccine Subsidy Scheme, offering services at over 3,200 locations across the territory.
Dr Leung urged strict personal and environmental hygiene. High-risk individuals, including children, the elderly, and those with chronic conditions or weakened immunity, should wear surgical masks on public transport or in crowded places. He warned that a child's condition can deteriorate rapidly, and parents should seek immediate emergency care if symptoms such as rapid breathing, wheezing, blue lips, chest pain, confusion, persistent fever or convulsions appear.

SilentAir 劫持亚洲电信网络以拦截 SMS 2FA 代码并监视台湾用户
SilentAir 劫持亚洲电信网络以拦截 SMS 2FA 代码并监视台湾用户
Swati Khandelwal报告2026年11月13日网络间谍/威胁情报
一个新发现的间谍组织利用亚洲移动运营商内部的黑客设备拦截特定人员的电话和短信，这些人员大多来自台湾。
总部位于斯德哥尔摩的电信和网络安全软件公司 Enea 本周在至少六个亚洲国家发现了该组织的攻击源，并将其命名为 SilentAir。它高度确信 SilentAir 是一个国家级行为者，但仅将其活动与中国联系起来，信心度较低。
该公司已告知运营商其在何处找到 SilentAir 源。据称，SilentAir 目前已中断，但可能会恢复。报告没有透露这些运营商是否已经清理了被黑的设备。
移动运营商使用 SS7 和 Diameter 协议来交换路由呼叫和文本并启用漫游的信令消息。此流量穿过称为 IPX 的共享网络，该网络在运营商之间的高度信任基础上运行。 SilentAir 从被黑设备向 IPX 发送攻击。
为了进行拦截，SilentAir 向目标的家庭网络发送了 UpdateLocation 消息或其等效的 Diameter 消息。该消息声称，被黑客入侵的设备现在正在为目标的手机提供服务。如果家庭网络接受它，该人的电话和短信将被转移给攻击者。
其中一些攻击有效。对于某些目标，该公司观察到两因素身份验证（2FA）代码在转移生效后立即被拦截。这表明有人试图闯入这些人注册的其他帐户。
该报告没有提供类似的语音通话证据，也没有说明是否有任何帐户被盗用。
该公司从 SilentAir 看到的攻击中，拦截占 18.3%。对于典型的监控公司（大多数信号攻击背后的公司）来说，该公司早期研究中的份额为 2.1%。
一些目标是本国的政治和政府要人。在极少数情况下，多个国家的 SilentAir 设备会协同对抗此类目标，该公司表示，这些目标指向单个控制器。
攻击呈爆发式发生，一个月内从一个或几个订户到数千个订户，两次爆发之间的间隔长达几个月或更长时间。
在台湾以外，目标主要位于其他东南亚和东亚网络，有时也位于东非、中亚、中东和欧洲。使用被黑客攻击的运营商自己的网络的人也可能成为目标，但该公司无法看到该流量。
该公司通过研究针对运营商之间链路的攻击发现了 SilentAir。自 2025 年初以来，它一直在追踪来自一些通常不会发送攻击的亚洲运营商的异常攻击，其中大部分是通过 SS7，有时是通过 Diameter。后来的分析甚至更早地发现了可疑活动。
根据该公司的技术报告，托管 SilentAir 的网络以奇怪且不一致的方式处理转移目标的后续消息。这就留下了两种解释：外部有人伪造了这些网络的信令地址，或者每个网络内部的设备已被接管。

SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
Swati KhandelwalNov 13, 2026Cyber Espionage / Threat Intelligence
A newly identified spying group used hacked equipment inside Asian mobile operators to intercept the calls and texts of selected people, mostly in Taiwan.
Enea, a telecom and cybersecurity software company based in Stockholm, found the group's attack sources in at least six Asian countries and named it SilentAir this week. It assessed with high confidence that SilentAir is a state-level actor, but linked its activity to China only with low confidence.
The company has told the operators where it found SilentAir sources. It said SilentAir has been disrupted for now but could return. The report does not say whether those operators have cleaned up the hacked equipment.
Mobile operators use the SS7 and Diameter protocols to exchange signaling messages that route calls and texts and enable roaming. This traffic crosses a shared network called the IPX, which runs on a high level of trust between operators. SilentAir sent its attacks into the IPX from the hacked equipment.
For interception, SilentAir sent the target's home network an UpdateLocation message, or its Diameter equivalent. The message claimed that the hacked equipment was now serving the target's phone. If the home network accepted it, calls and texts for that person would be diverted to the attackers.
Some of these attacks worked. For some targets, the company observed two-factor authentication (2FA) codes being intercepted immediately after the diversion took effect. That points to an attempt to break into other accounts registered to those people.
The report gives no similar evidence for voice calls, and it does not say whether any account was taken over.
Interception made up 18.3% of the attacks the company saw from SilentAir. For a typical surveillance company, the kind of firm behind most signaling attacks, the share was 2.1% in the company's earlier research.
Some targets were political and government VIPs in their own countries. In rare cases, SilentAir equipment in several countries worked together against such targets, which the company said points to a single controller.
The attacks came in bursts, from one or a few subscribers to several thousand over a month, with gaps of up to several months or longer between bursts.
Outside Taiwan, targets were mostly in other Southeast and East Asian networks, and at times in East Africa, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe. People using the hacked operators' own networks may also have been targeted, but the company could not see that traffic.
The company spotted SilentAir by studying attacks on the links between operators. Since early 2025, it has tracked unusual attacks, mostly over SS7 and sometimes Diameter, from some Asian operators that would not normally send attacks. Later analysis found suspicious activity even earlier.
The networks hosting SilentAir handled follow-up messages for diverted targets in odd and inconsistent ways, according to the company's technical report. That left two explanations: someone outside was faking those networks' signaling addresses, or equipment inside each network had been taken over.
The company then saw equipment inside one operator both send and receive attack commands, which confirmed the second explanation. That equipment behaved exactly like SilentAir sources in other networks.
Detecting and blocking the attacks was hard at first because the attackers understood mobile networks and signaling defenses well. After the attacks were contained, the company recovered traces of unauthorized access. It could not analyze the malware it believes SilentAir used.
The report does not name the countries, the operators, or any of the targets. In some countries, SilentAir attacks came from more than one operator.
SilentAir also sent silent SMS on a very large scale, mainly to subscribers in Taiwan. These are texts that the phone does not display or alert on.
During the day, most silent SMS went to subscribers on other networks, such as Southeast Asian networks. One of their main uses appears to have been checking whether a diversion had worked, the company said.
If the test text reached the hacked equipment instead of the phone, the attackers knew they were getting that person's texts.
Most silent SMS went out at night, and most of those went to people in Taiwan. The company said the purpose of those messages is not confirmed. They may be a bulk check that earlier diversions were still in place, since phones are least likely to re-register to their real location at night.
The silent texts carried spam-like motivational or promotional lines, often in English. The company believes the text was a disguise. If an operator along the way stripped a message's silent setting, the recipient would see it as spam and ignore it.
The company's low-confidence link to China rests on several signs. SilentAir focused on Taiwan and did not target Chinese networks or subscribers.
Its tracking and interception attacks also followed a working day in UTC+8, which is China Standard Time. They started at 9 a.m., almost stopped on weekends, and paused or slowed around Chinese holidays.
The company also considered a link to Liminal Panda, a group behind earlier telecom intrusions. It called the link possible but unconfirmed and does not tie the two groups together for now.
In several hacked operators, SilentAir attacks happened during a known Liminal Panda infection. At other times, the two showed no sign of working together. They also went after operators in the same part of Asia, though Liminal Panda has no known focus on Taiwan.
SilentAir's behavior also partly matches that of SCTPE, a little-known Linux trojan that runs in the kernel and is designed to send and receive SS7 and Diameter traffic.
Singapore's Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) has described the same tool in a government advisory. There, the tool is called SIGweaver. The agency said CrowdStrike identified it on January 21 and links it to Liminal Panda with moderate confidence.
But Enea said SilentAir answered messages it had not sent itself, which the known SCTPE program cannot do. SilentAir's operational security also seemed far better than Liminal Panda's.
Separately, the company's GTP firewall has detected Liminal Panda activity at several customer operators since the first quarter of this year. The company blocked the group's GTPDoor traffic there and saw Liminal Panda infections, or strong signs of them, in at least 5 to 10 operators.
The GTPDoor backdoor, first documented on February 27, 2024, hides commands within GTP-C, the protocol that establishes mobile data connections between networks. The company also found evidence of a new version that hides commands in GTP-U, the part of GTP that carries users' data. GTP-U traffic is harder to inspect, though the company believes the new version serves mainly as a backup.
The company said any attacker could reuse these techniques, and it told operators to:
Deploy GTP-C and GTP-U firewalls and configure them to share information with their SS7 and Diameter firewalls.
Go beyond the industry's basic recommendations for signaling security.
Treat the whole IPX as untrusted.
Add detection for signaling protocols inside their own networks.
Connect signaling security with the rest of their IT security.
The report does not advise people whose calls and texts may be targeted.

You know it’s bad when the Outlook outage overshadows Jensen Huang’s additional cheating allegations. Yes, there are three women now.
Microsoft Outlook experienced a widespread outage, disrupting email, calendars and a range of workplace tools for users around the world. (EPA / Hannibal Hanschke)
“Is there a problem with Outlook?” was the question from my wife as we settled down for bed last night.
The reason, I found out, goes a little like this… At about 8pm our time, Microsoft acknowledged online that people in the Americas couldn’t reach their Exchange Online mailboxes.
Soon afterwards, it conceded that users in any region could be affected. By Downdetector’s count, Outlook complaints peaked above 138,000 around then. At the time of Microsoft’s latest update, when I woke up this morning, the outage was still running – so I wrote about it in the Business Maverick newsletter.
The first theory was load. Microsoft said part of its infrastructure was straining, so it paused deployments, rerouted traffic and restarted servers. Then it corrected itself. Demand hadn’t surged. A number of servers had unexpectedly dropped out, and the survivors were buckling under the extra weight.
The second theory was the health check. Servers were failing automated tests and removing themselves from service, and Microsoft pointed to the component that processes server health. It found no recent change linked to the start of the trouble. A different health-check method brought a subset of servers back. A system built to tell healthy machines from sick ones may have been the thing that was sick.
Then came the false dawn. By evening in New York, which was about 1am here, Microsoft said restored servers were stable and users would see a gradual recovery as their clients reconnected. Reports had fallen to roughly 34,000.
A couple of hours later it admitted that the restored servers could go unresponsive again once traffic reached them. It began limiting some types of traffic in some locations and rebuilding a subset of servers on an earlier configuration. Its latest update says a change meant to improve serviceability hadn’t taken as expected, and engineers were looking for other ways to add capacity.
We're continuing to work on recovering our frontend servers while implementing further traffic optimization actions to improve service stability and increase capacity. A more comprehensive update can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as https://t.co/pYdahqxDv3 if the admin center is not available to you.
— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 13, 2026
The blast radius is the real story: Copilot couldn’t reach work data. Defender’s Safe Links couldn’t verify URLs. Purview’s data-loss prevention, labelling and eDiscovery tools were hit, along with Intune enrolment, Graph API calls, Planner, To Do and Universal Print. Some Windows 365 Cloud PCs became unreachable. Even the document I use for the market table didn’t want to save...
Unfortunately, Teams calls largely held up, but calendars didn’t. Which means everyone can complain about the outage, but IT can’t resolve it.
Files in SharePoint stayed accessible.
Reuters also reported that the outage hit connectors used by OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s AI services, and OpenAI said new connections to Microsoft connectors might be broken. So things may be broken this morning, be kind with yourself. DM
Current status as per Microsoft’s official update portal:
“We’re continuing to pursue multiple workstreams to pinpoint the underlying cause of the traffic influx and advance the recoverability of the backend servers. We’re taking a measured approach to identify and repair affected infrastructure to improve the ability to confirm the developed changes were applied. We’re tracking the results of this approach to verify the servers are showing the anticipated recovery and performance intended.
As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident. We will continue to treat this incident with urgency and priority until full resolution. Once mitigated, we will provide full details of the root cause, defense-in-depth repair items, and more within a Post-Incident Report.
Scope of impact: This issue may affect users attempting to access the affected Microsoft 365 services.”

title: Australian Army’s littoral transformation is the right move, experts say

content:
新加坡——专家告诉 Breaking Defense，澳大利亚军队最近成立的[沿海机动大队](https://www.defence.gov.au/news-events/releases/2026-03-30/new-littoral-manoeuvre-group-builted-brisbane)对于该国武装部队来说是正确的举动，特别是在印太地区紧张局势持续存在的情况下。

澳大利亚在其[2024年国防战略](https://www.defence.gov.au/about/strategic-planning/2024-national-defence-strategy-2024-integrated-investment-program)中宣布了将其地面部队转变为一支以沿海为重点的部队的计划，其中呼吁军队“针对沿海机动进行优化，具有远程陆地和海上打击能力”。

今年三月，澳大利亚陆军成立了濒海机动大队，以加强该军种“在沿海和岛屿地区调动、部署和支持地面部队的能力”。

但随着[一些项目的预算削减迫在眉睫](https://thenightly.com.au/politics/defence-budget-cuts-loom-as-aukus-funding-Pressure-drives-review-of-military-spending-c-23076920)为AUKUS支出腾出空间，专家警告说，该单位需要充足的资源，以确保其能够履行这一职责。
在三边协议承诺支出增加之后，该国正在进行预算审查，以腾出资金用于采购核潜艇，尽管该国承诺将国防支出提高到[国内生产总值的百分之三]产品](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/04/australia-pledges-to-boost-defense-spend-to-3-of-gdp-says-us-remains-key-partner/) 在未来几年。

上个月，濒海机动大队在与印度尼西亚的一次训练活动中完成了大规模两栖演习。

澳大利亚国立大学国际安全与情报研究教授约翰·布拉克斯兰（John Blaxland）告诉《突破防务》，这样的演习表明澳大利亚设想与盟友和伙伴合作部署部队来观察和保护关键的沿海地点，并在冲突中控制海上咽喉要道。

布莱克斯兰说：“濒海机动大队是澳大利亚的一个激进的组织设计概念，反映了对能够快速部署和支持与伙伴一起远距离作战的部队的重大重新定位。”他补充说，该大队可以追溯到第二次世界大战，当时澳大利亚军队展示了对沿海联合兵种作战的掌握。

澳大利亚独立海军评论员亚历克斯·勒克（Alex Luck）对此表示同意，称关注沿海行动是“朝着正确方向迈出的一步”。
“鉴于中国军事能力不断增强，扩展到更广阔的太平洋和印度洋战区，澳大利亚在其周边地区面临着严峻的地理挑战。因此，澳大利亚陆军将不得不依赖强大的海军机动能力，以灵活覆盖包括澳大利亚直接控制的岛屿和澳大利亚领土周围的海上通道在内的海域，”他补充道。

他还强调需要与美国和新西兰等澳大利亚邻国和合作伙伴合作，“确保澳大利亚周围的海洋特征，特别是太平洋岛屿空间的安全。”

濒海机动大队将包括三个登陆艇营，每个营拥有四艘中型登陆艇和两艘重型登陆艇。布拉克斯兰和拉克都同意为该小组配备这些登陆艇至关重要。

澳大利亚向 Austal Aust 授予合同

【原文 English Original】
SINGAPORE — The Australian army’s recently created [Littoral Manoeuvre Group](https://www.defence.gov.au/news-events/releases/2026-03-30/new-littoral-manoeuvre-group-established-brisbane)is the correct move for the country’s armed forces, experts told Breaking Defense, especially as tensions continue in the Indo-Pacific.

Australia announced plans to transform its ground forces into a littoral-focused force in its [2024 National Defence Strategy](https://www.defence.gov.au/about/strategic-planning/2024-national-defence-strategy-2024-integrated-investment-program), which called for an army “optimised for littoral manoeuvre with a long range land and maritime strike capability.”

In March, Australian Army established the Littoral Manoeuvre Group to strengthen the service’s “ability to move, deploy and support land forces across coastal and island regions.”

But as[budget cuts to some programs loom](https://thenightly.com.au/politics/defence-budget-cuts-loom-as-aukus-funding-pressure-drives-review-of-military-spending-c-23076920)to make room for AUKUS spending, experts warn that the unit needs to be adequately resourced to ensure it can fulfil that role.

In the wake of increased spending on commitments for the trilateral agreement, the country is conducting a budget review to free up funds for the acquisition of nuclear submarines, even as the country is pledging to bring defense spending up to [three percent of its gross domestic product](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/04/australia-pledges-to-boost-defense-spend-to-3-of-gdp-says-us-remains-key-partner/) in the coming years.

Last month, the Littoral Manoeuvre Group completed a large-scale amphibious exercise during a training event with Indonesia.

John Blaxland,a professor of international security and intelligence studies at Australian National University, told Breaking Defense that an exercis e like that suggests that Australia envisages working with allies and partners to deploy forces to observe and safeguard key littoral sites, as well as control maritime chokepoints in a conflict.

“The Littoral Manoeuvre Group is a radical organisational design concept for Australia which reflects a significant reorientation towards being able to rapidly deploy and support forces operating over considerable distances alongside partners,” Blaxland said, adding that the group harks back to World War II, when Australian forces demonstrated mastery of combined arms warfare in the littorals.

Independent Australian naval commentator Alex Luck agreed, calling the focus on littoral operations “a step in the right direction.”

“Australia faces a difficult geographic challenge in its near abroad, in light of a rising Chinese military capability expanding into the wider Pacific and Indian Ocean theatres. Therefore the Australian Army will have to rely on significant naval mobility allowing for flexible coverage of maritime spaces including islands directly under Australian control and maritime approaches around Australian territory,” he added.

He also stressed the need to work with Australia’s neighbors and partners such as the US and New Zealand “in securing maritime features around Australia, but particularly across Pacific Island spaces.”

The Littoral Manoeuvre Group will include three landing craft battalions, each operating four medium and two heavy landing craft. Both Blaxland and Luck agree that outfitting the group with these landing craft is crucial.

Australia awarded contracts to Austal Australia for [Land Craft Medium](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/12/austal-defence-australia-awarded-681-million-landing-craft-contract-down-under/) in December 2025 and for [Landing Craft Heavy](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/02/austal-secures-second-australian-landing-craft-heavy-contract/) in February. LCM will have a cargo capacity of 80 tonnes (88 tons) while the LCH will be able to transport 200 soldiers and six M1 Abrams tanks or nine Redback infantry vehicles.

Luck said the introduction of the two new classes of landing craft would introduce capabilities that the Australian Army has not operated in recent times.

“The LCH in particular, in conjunction with the Royal Australian Navy’s own amphibious assets, represents an unprecedented new resource the Australian Army will need time to further refine and develo p,” he said.

“It is therefore important to apply a step by step approach maturing these new amphibious capabilities to allow for further refinement, including allocation of additional resources further strengthening the new LMG concept,” he continued.

And while Australia’s plans to equip the new group as outlined in Australia’s defense [Integrated Investment Program](https://www.defence.gov.au/about/strategic-planning/2026-national-defence-strategy-2026-integrated-investment-program) appear to be sufficient, Blaxland cautioned that those plans would take time to come to fruition and was dependent on whether funding is available to follow through.

“The plan appears to be to expand significantly to help move whole battalion groups and supporting elements to work alongside partner forces in the ‘littorals’ across the archipelago. But with significant funding constraints, this is not likely to reach full operational capacity for some years yet,” he said.

|黄仁勋事件暴露硅谷国家安全力量
黄仁勋事件暴露硅谷国家安全实力
中期选举的蓝色海啸刚刚登陆，特朗普政府就遭遇了另一场危机。
11月8日，黄仁勋承认（在新窗口中打开）恋情。据《纽约时报》报道，美国情报机构得出结论，他的情妇是中国国家安全部的情报人员。
此事的消息震惊了市场和监管机构。黄领导的英伟达是全球最有价值的公司，为西方与中国的技术竞争提供核心技术。他与美国政治机构关系密切，今年早些时候，他与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起乘坐空军一号对北京进行国事访问。
黄的事件显示了华盛顿与硅谷关系核心的新矛盾。私营企业高管比以往任何时候都拥有更大的权力，而旨在保护美国国家安全的机构却没有适应这种变化。
国家安全机构的设立是为了保护敏感信息。它们还保护政府决策者免受影响力的影响。针对黄的威胁集中在中国可能影响英伟达向中国出售人工智能芯片的立场，而不是控制任何特定的机密信息。
美国主要科技公司的领导人正在成为美国国家安全政策的结构性决定性人物。
世界各国政府每天都有理由将黄仁勋这样的人视为关键的地缘政治人物。
9 月，五角大楼任命 SpaceX 和特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Anduril Industries 创始人帕尔默·拉基 (Palmer Luckey) 以及前众议院议长纽特·金里奇 (Newt Gingrich) 为 Project Meridian 的领导者。这三人将指导美国战争的未来，包括采购数千亿美元的装备。
2025 年 12 月，黄仁勋本人对 CSIS 表示，“我们国家非凡的科技产业是我们国家安全的一部分”。他的公司控制着全球 80-85% 的人工智能芯片硬件市场（在新窗口中打开），通过对基础设施的控制，将自己定位为美国实力的先锋。
硅谷高管给自己的任务是塑造美国的国家安全利益，而不是满足政府的要求，从而影响世界如何看待美国的实力。

Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
Trump knew about Huang’s Chinese contact months before the public did, and Washington has no rulebook for cases like it.

|Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
Jensen Huang’s affair exposes Silicon Valley’s national security power
The blue tsunami of the midterms had barely landed onshore when yet another crisis hit the Trump administration.
On 8 November, Jensen Huang admitted (Opens in new window) to an affair. American intelligence agencies, according (Opens in new window) to the New York Times, have concluded that his mistress is an intelligence asset for China’s Ministry of State Security.
News of the affair shocked markets and regulators. Huang leads Nvidia, the world’s most valuable company that provides the core technology for the West’s technological competition with China. He is deeply tied with the American political apparatus, flying on Air Force One with President Donald Trump for his state visit to Beijing earlier in the year.
Huang’s affair shows a new contradiction at the heart of Washington’s relationship to Silicon Valley. Private executives have more power than ever, while the institutions designed to protect America’s national security haven’t adapted to that change.
National security apparatuses are set up to protect sensitive information. They also protect government decision-makers from influence efforts. The threat against Huang centred on the potential for China to influence Nvidia’s position on selling AI chips to China, rather than control of any particular item of classified information.
The leaders of major American technology firms are becoming structurally decisive figures in American national security policy.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures.
In September, the Pentagon named (Opens in new window) SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk and Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey, alongside former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, as the leaders of Project Meridian. The three will guide the future of American warfare, including acquisition of hundreds of billions of dollars of equipment.
In December 2025, Huang himself told (Opens in new window) CSIS, “our nation’s extraordinary technology industry is part of our national security”. His company, which controls 80–85% of the global market (Opens in new window) for AI chip hardware, positions itself at the vanguard of American power through its grip on the infrastructure.
Silicon Valley executives are giving themselves the job of shaping America’s national security interests rather than delivering what the government requests – in turn influencing how the world sees American power.
US President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman speak with Elon Musk, Jensen Huang and other business leaders at the US-Saudi Investment Forum, 19 November 2025, at the John F. Kennedy Centre for the Performing Arts in Washington, DC (Daniel Torok/Official White House Photo)
When Musk throttled Starlink access to Ukraine’s soldiers, speculation abounded about who authorised the slowdown between Musk or Trump. The question itself proved the point, that critical decisions may be made on either side of the sector wall.
In Brazil’s presidential election, thousands of protestors gathered outside of Meta’s Sao Paolo office to decry what they saw as the company meddling in their election. In the months prior, the President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s campaign released evidence (Opens in new window) that Meta’s platforms were promoting his opponent’s campaign and limiting Lula’s ability to reach voters. Meta accepted the result but denied any political intention behind it. The reputational damage had been done: a majority of Brazilians believe that American technology poses a risk to their national security.
A Silicon Valley executive who controls technology used by military and intelligence services may not have access to classified information, but can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates.
These companies, deeply tied to the Trump White House and at the vanguard of its definition of American power, are producing consequences that have a significance that rivals that of entire governments.
Governments around the world gain reasons every day to treat people like Jensen Huang as key geopolitical figures. This scandal shows that counterintelligence services need to account for that reality.
The FBI, the key counterintelligence service in the United States, has some efforts in place to protect private industry. They investigate attempts by foreign governments to infiltrate critical companies. Their goal is to protect classified information and hardware that could be stolen and repurposed.
As the public role that these executives play changes, so too does the problem of counterintelligence defence. A Silicon Valley executive who controls the technology used by military and intelligence services around the world may not themselves have access to classified information, but they can make consequential decisions about how the technology operates. These decisions could change what a country is capable of doing, or what technology an adversary is able to access.
Beyond the question of the appropriate counterintelligence protection for figures like Huang, there also comes the question of their political relationships.
Well before the public was made aware, Trump was informed (Opens in new window) about Huang’s relationship, including the intelligence community’s assessment that his mistress was tied to Chinese intelligence. Even after those briefings, Trump continued to speak with Huang and, once the scandal was revealed, publicly defended him.
Even once counterintelligence services adapt to the moving future, they can always be countermanded by chief executives who make political calculations about figures. Trump could have pushed Huang out, but in doing so would have alienated a key political ally, someone central to his strategic competition with China. Huang’s embrace of MAGA has also been helpful to Trump in building a political and economic support base in Silicon Valley.
The decision to do nothing with the information developed by the FBI was a political one, made because Trump saw Huang as indispensable.
This dynamic matters for every country that relies on American technology in both its civilian and public sectors. These new vulnerabilities will not stop at American borders.
The new generation of leaders taking centre stage in the United States must grapple with the seemingly insurmountable power that Silicon Valley has accumulated in the Trump era. Backlash to that very group was part of the substantial rebuke delivered by voters.
In governing, these new leaders from both parties will have to reimagine national security – including counterintelligence – to cover the public power now wielded by private actors.
Cory Alpert is a PhD researcher at the University of Melbourne, where he studies the impact of AI on democracy. Previously, he served in the Biden White House for three years and as the senior adviser to Mayor Steve Benjamin.

title: 黄仁勋丑闻引发人工智能“玩梗”热潮
source: 美国已不是世界老大 - 纽约时报中文网
summary: 英伟达董事会周四宣布，联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已辞职。 Anthony Wallace/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images 黄仁勋和他那身标志性的皮夹克装扮早已成为他联合创立的科技巨头英伟达的代名词。两者之间的联系如此紧密，以至于今年英伟达还推出了售价178美元的毛衣，胸前印着像素艺术风格的黄仁勋肖像。 现在，在接连爆出出轨丑闻后，黄仁勋于周四辞职。其中一起婚外情的对象是一名被美国政府认为是中国间谍的女子。网友拿他的形象大做文章，制造出
content:
英伟达董事会周四宣布，联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋已辞职。 Anthony Wallace/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
黄仁勋和他那身标志性的皮夹克装扮早已成为他联合创立的科技巨头英伟达的代名词。两者之间的联系如此紧密，以至于今年英伟达还推出了售价178美元的毛衣，胸前印着像素艺术风格的黄仁勋肖像。
现在，在接连爆出出轨丑闻后，黄仁勋于周四辞职。其中一起婚外情的对象是一名被美国政府认为是中国间谍的女子。网友拿他的形象大做文章，制造出铺天盖地的迷因。
这些迷因中有不少出自曾经崇拜黄仁勋的人工智能爱好者之手。
黄仁勋的形象出现在各种网络恶搞作品中，从MV、宝莱坞电影、美国情景喜剧到酷玩乐队演唱会上的“亲吻抓拍”(kiss-cam)，不一而足。其中许多作品都是利用人工智能生成的，而正是英伟达生产的芯片让这项技术得以广泛普及。
63岁的黄仁勋是人工智能热潮中最有权势的人物之一。如今，他的婚外情丑闻也成为又一起被网友制成迷因广泛传播的名人出轨事件。
去年，一家科技初创公司的已婚首席执行官在酷玩乐队的演唱会上被现场镜头拍到正拥抱公司的人力资源部门主管。后者虽然也已婚，但当时已与配偶分居。
比利时软件工程师彼得·德德内把黄仁勋的形象移植到了这段广为流传的视频中。他周四在电话采访中说，本周他熬夜看手机，刷关于英伟达的新闻。
43岁的德德内躺在床上，利用一款开源生成式人工智能工具，把酷玩乐队演唱会视频中的男女主角替换成了黄仁勋和黄乐(Alice Huang)。黄乐是那名中国女商人，黄仁勋已承认与她有过婚外情。
谈到自己制作的这个迷因，德德内说：“我当时没太当回事。”
他说，周日早上醒来时，这条帖文的曝光量已经超过100万次。截至周四下午，曝光量已接近700万次。
“我以前真的非常崇拜这个人，”德德内谈到黄仁勋时说。“到头来，他参与创造的技术被用来开他的玩笑，挺讽刺的。”
社交媒体用户还利用人工智能把黄仁勋放进了一些以出轨为主题的经典音乐录影带中。
在一个帖子里，黄仁勋穿着标志性的黑色皮夹克，在Usher的《Confessions, Pt. II》音乐视频中取代了Usher。（不过，论对口型还是原版更胜一筹。）
这段视频的制作者、明尼阿波利斯的人工智能顾问托马斯·尤尼斯表示，他只花了五分钟就在谷歌上找到了四张黄仁勋的照片，然后输入一款人工智能工具，用黄仁勋的形象替换了音乐视频中的Usher。
40岁的尤尼斯说，黄仁勋形象的迷因大量涌现说明这项技术的发展速度有多么惊人。
“一年半以前，人工智能生成的威尔·史密斯吃意大利面的视频画面还是模糊不清的一团，”他谈到这位演员、音乐人时说。“现在你看一段视频，会觉得，‘哇，这看起来还真挺像真的。’”
在另一段视频中，黄仁勋扮演电影《黑客帝国》中的尼奥，特朗普总统则化身墨菲斯，对他大谈与中国保持战略竞争的重要性，以及不要被穿红裙子的女人迷住。
黄仁勋的虚拟形象转过身来，发现那个被替换成黄乐模样的红衣女子，竟然变成了举着枪的中国领导人习近平。
埃隆·马斯克也在这段恶搞视频中客串亮相。截至周四，该视频在X上的观看次数已超过600万。
围绕硅谷那些涉及巨额利益的欺诈事件，一些网友还把黄仁勋的形象植入了纪录片《你可以看见一切》。这部纪录片讲述的是血液检测公司Theranos创始人伊丽莎白·霍姆斯的故事。霍姆斯因欺诈投资者入狱。
借助生成式人工智能，网友重新制作了纪录片预告片中的一组镜头，让黄乐化身霍姆斯，眼睛都不眨一下地坚称：“我当然没有骗你。”
但德德内说，令他“依然感到惊讶”的是，竟然有那么多人看了他制作的视频后问：“这是真的吗？”

content:
香港警方和航空管理局在新界北部和全港设立临时禁飞区中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港警方和航空管理局在新界北部和全港设立临时禁飞区
香港警方和民航处宣布设立两个临时限制飞行区，覆盖新界北部及全港，禁止无人机、滑翔伞、飞艇、风筝以及大部分直升机和小型飞机飞行。违规者将面临罚款和监禁。
香港警务处及民航处提醒公众遵守2026年11月13日公布的两个临时飞行限制区的规定。
第一个区域称为 A 区，覆盖新界北部。在该区域内，禁止进行以下飞行活动：无人机（经警方和民航处特别批准的除外）、滑翔伞、飞艇、风筝、系留气球以及大量气球的释放。
第二个区域称为 B 区，适用于全港。除政府飞行服务队外，所有直升机和小型飞机均禁止在该区域内进行任何飞行活动。
民航处已透过航空情报刊物增刊，向航空公司及机师通报这些临时限制飞行区的详情。小型无人机的详细信息也已上传至SUA一站通电子平台。
警方和民航处警告，任何人未经特别批准，在这些临时限制飞行区内进行飞行活动，即属犯罪。一经定罪，违法者可能面临罚款和监禁。

Hong Kong police and aviation authority issue temporary no-fly zones for northern New Territories and territory-wide | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 13 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong police and aviation authority issue temporary no-fly zones for northern New Territories and territory-wide
Hong Kong police and the Civil Aviation Department announced two temporary restricted flight zones, covering northern New Territories and territory-wide, banning drones, paragliders, airships, kites and most helicopters and small planes. Violators face fines and imprisonment.
The Hong Kong Police Force and the Civil Aviation Department have reminded the public to observe regulations concerning two temporary restricted flight zones, announced on 13 November 2026.
The first zone, designated Zone A, covers northern New Territories. Within this area, the following flight activities are prohibited: drones (except those with special approval from the police and the Civil Aviation Department), paragliders, airships, kites, captive balloons, and the release of large numbers of balloons.
The second zone, designated Zone B, applies territory-wide. Except for the Government Flying Service, all helicopters and small aircraft are banned from conducting any flight activities within this zone.
The Civil Aviation Department has notified airlines and pilots of the details of these temporary restricted flight zones through a supplement to the Aeronautical Information Publication. Details for small unmanned aircraft have also been uploaded to the SUA一站通 electronic platform.
The police and the Civil Aviation Department have warned that any person conducting flight activities within these temporary restricted flight zones without special approval will be committing an offence. Upon conviction, offenders may face a fine and imprisonment.
