summary: 中美俄可能举行的峰会引发了现代雅尔塔会议的警报，三位有权势的人瓜分世界——几乎不顾乌克兰、欧洲、台湾或其他任何人。香港深水埗的一个摊位上展示着美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京等人的面孔的磁铁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。但除了历史性的拍照机会外，习近平主席、唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京在 11 月 18 日至 19 日深圳 APEC 峰会上的会晤可能会实现
content:
中美俄可能举行的峰会引发了现代雅尔塔会议的警报，三位有权势的人瓜分世界——几乎不顾乌克兰、欧洲、台湾或其他任何国家。香港深水埗的一个摊位上展示着美国总统唐纳德·特朗普、中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京等人的面孔的磁铁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。但分析人士表示，除了历史性的拍照机会之外，习近平主席、唐纳德·特朗普和弗拉基米尔·普京在 11 月 18 日至 19 日深圳 APEC 峰会上的会晤可能不会取得什么成果。势力范围 1945 年 2 月，时任美国总统富兰克林·罗斯福、英国温斯顿·丘吉尔和苏联领导人约瑟夫·斯大林在雅尔塔会面，他们制定了二战后的解决方案和欧洲新的领土边界。那次会议在雅尔塔举行，当时在苏联，现在在 2014 年被俄罗斯吞并的乌克兰部分地区举行，为苏联统治东欧和冷战奠定了基础。乌克兰总统泽伦斯基警告称，深圳可能会成为21世纪类似雅尔塔的“势力范围重新分配”。三巨头在雅尔塔会议制定了击败德国的最终计划。照片：维基共享资源。
本周在阿布扎比举行的会谈（自二月份以来的首次会谈）上，俄罗斯谈判代表推动对欧洲大陆安全架构的审查作为任何和平协议的一部分，这让乌克兰及其欧洲支持者感到不安，美国也提出了一个新框架。俄罗斯驻阿布扎比代表团团长弗拉基米尔·梅丁斯基（Vladimir Medinsky）质疑欧洲是否参与进一步谈判，从而煽动了这种担忧。哈德逊研究所的齐波拉·弗里德表示，三边关系令人恼火，因为它标志着“一些大国可以决定其他国家的安全和未来”。她告诉法新社，仅这种形式“就已经传达了一个信息，即谁重要，谁的利益可以由其他人协商”。利益分歧 然而，除了象征意义之外，利益分歧使得在深圳建立新的世界秩序的可能性不大。据报道，就连议程也仍然存在争议：俄罗斯建议会议重点关注乌克兰，特朗普推动就核武器和伊朗战争进行谈判，而中国对这两个问题都守口如瓶。北京人民大学重阳金融研究院院长王文表示，“三方的诉求差异很大，预期管理变得困难。谈判很有可能在没有突破的情况下结束。”三位领导人的意见也很少能带来进展。
例如，北京和华盛顿之间的主要争论点是贸易和人工智能技术竞赛。 自称多边主义捍卫者的北京多次表示，欧洲应该参与乌克兰和平谈判。布鲁塞尔欧盟委员会总部前悬挂着乌克兰和欧盟旗帜。资料图片：欧盟委员会。德国总统施泰因迈尔表示，在最近的一次会议上，当涉及乌克兰问题的三边会谈的想法出现时，习近平表现出了“恼怒”。 “他明确指出，这是一场欧洲冲突，欧洲人也必须参与其中，”施泰因迈尔告诉 ARD。在核裁军问题上，中国长期以来一直坚持美俄削减核裁军

【原文 English Original】
A possible China-US-Russia summit has prompted alarm of a modern-day Yalta Conference, with three powerful men carving up the world — with little regard for Ukraine, Europe and Taiwan or anyone else. Magnets showing faces of US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, alongside others, are displayed at a stall in Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. But apart from an historic photo opportunity, the meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at the November 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen will likely achieve little, analysts say. Spheres of influence When then US president Franklin D. Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Yalta in February 1945, they laid out the post-WWII settlement and new territorial boundaries in Europe. That meeting in Yalta, then in the Soviet Union and now in a part of Ukraine annexed by Russia in 2014, laid out the foundations for the Soviet domination of Eastern Europe and the Cold War. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised alarm that Shenzhen could be a Yalta-like “redistribution of spheres of influence” for the 21st century. Conference of the Big Three at Yalta makes final plans for the defeat of Germany. Photo: Wikicommons. At talks in Abu Dhabi this week — the first since February — Russian negotiators rattled Ukraine and its European supporters by pushing a review of the continent’s security architecture as part of any peace deal, with the US also floating a new framework. Russia’s delegation chief in Abu Dhabi, Vladimir Medinsky, fanned such fears by questioning the inclusion of Europe in further talks. The trilateral rankles because it signals “the idea that a few great powers can decide the security and future of other countries over their heads”, according to Tsiporah Fried at the Hudson Institute. The format alone “would already send a message about who counts, and whose interests can be negotiated by others”, she told AFP. Divergent interests Beyond the symbolism, however, divergent interests make the creation of a new world order in Shenzhen unlikely. Even the agenda reportedly remains contentious: Russia has suggested the meeting focus on Ukraine, Trump has pushed for talks on nuclear weapons and the Iran war, and China has remained tight-lipped on both. “The three parties have vastly different demands, making the management of expectations difficult. There is a high probability that talks could end without a breakthrough,” according to Wang Wen, dean of the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University in Beijing. There are also few issues where input from all three leaders could bring progress. The main points of contention between Beijing and Washington are trade and the AI technology race, for instance. Beijing — which presents itself as a champion of multilateralism — has repeatedly said that Europe should be part of peace negotiations over Ukraine. Ukrainian and European Union flags in front of the European Commission’s headquarters in Brussels. File photo: European Commission. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier said that in a recent meeting, Xi showed “irritation” when the idea of the trilateral talks covering Ukraine came up. “He explicitly pointed out that this is a European conflict, in which the Europeans must also be at the table,” Steinmeier told ARD. On nuclear disarmament, China has long insisted that the US and Russia reduce their own giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its own stockpile. The summit therefore is more likely to produce minor outcomes such as crisis hotlines or some cooperation on counter-terrorism, public health, or climate change, Wang told AFP. “There is no single enemy to unite all three great powers the way that the fight against Nazi Germany united Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin,” said Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at Australian National University. “It follows that piecemeal horse-trading is in; a grand bargain is out.” However, Taiwan — which China claims — will still be watching the meeting closely, Sung said. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te. File photo: Taiwan’s Presidential Office, via Flickr. “If the Trump administration is open to abandoning one partner (Ukraine) out of convenience, then it can abandon another,” he said. A post-Shenzhen world The Trump administration has sought to reassert US dominance over the “Western hemisphere” — including by capturing Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January — but splitting the world among great powers like it’s 1945 may not guarantee security. China has opposed the logic of Yalta — the clandestine division of spheres of influence and major powers determining the fate of other nations — “from the very beginning”, according to Renmin University’s Wang. See also: What the US midterms mean for ties with China China could allay fears of a second Yalta by using the summit to “emphasise the defence of sovereignty and support for multilateral organisations”, Wang said. If Beijing uses the meeting to insist on European inclusion in talks regarding the continent’s security, it “could, in fact, open a new window for communication between China and Europe”, he said. “The original Yalta opened the path to the Korean War and Indochina Wars in addition to various conflicts and insurgencies across Asia, Africa, and Latin America,” said Chong Ja Ian at the National University of Singapore. Any Yalta 2.0 agreement “will almost certainly run into the same kinds of issues”, Chong said.

title: 秦伟平参加Katy ISD两所学校退伍军人节活动：致敬军人、倾听教师，关注下一代教育
summary: 纵览中国｜美国德克萨斯州Katy消息｜2026年11月12日 2026年11月11日美国退伍军人节当天，美国海军退伍军人、Katy ISD学区董事会第六选区候选人秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）先后参加了德克萨斯州Katy独立学区（Katy Independent School District，简称Katy ISD）两所学校举办的退伍军人节活动，分别是Shafer Elementary小学和Seven Lakes Junior High初中。 秦伟平随后通
content: 纵览中国｜美国德克萨斯州Katy消息｜2026年11月12日 2026年11月11日美国退伍军人节当天，美国海军退伍军人、Katy ISD学区董事会第六选区候选人秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）先后参加了德克萨斯州Katy独立学区（Katy Independent School District，简称Katy ISD）两所学校举办的退伍军人节活动，分别是Shafer Elementary小学和Seven Lakes Junior High初中。 秦伟平随后通过个人Facebook、X（原Twitter）及Substack等平台发布活动照片和文字，分享当天的经历与感受。从校园对退伍军人的致敬，到与一线教育工作者的交流，两场活动也使教师薪酬、特殊教育支持以及学校人才队伍建设等问题成为他关注的议题。 Shafer Elementary：学生以歌声和荣誉墙向退伍军人致敬 当天，秦伟平首先参加了Shafer Elementary举办的退伍军人节庆祝活动。 根据秦伟平在社交媒体发布的介绍，学校在图书馆为退伍军人、现役军人、军人家长、教师及家庭成员准备了早餐和咖啡，让来自不同家庭和服役背景的社区成员有机会交流。 活动特别设置了退伍军人荣誉墙，展示与学校有关的退伍军人照片及个人故事，其中也包括秦伟平本人，以及目前仍在美国军队服役的学生家长。学生们还亲手制作了表达感谢的留言，向曾经和正在服役的军人及其家庭致敬。 当天的学生表演也是活动的重要环节。学生们演唱了代表美国不同军种的歌曲。当相应军种的歌曲响起时，曾在该军种服役的退伍军人起立，全校师生则以掌声表达敬意。 此外，学校Student Council（学生会）的学生代表还朗诵了一首献给退伍军人的诗歌。 秦伟平在个人文章中表示，学生们真挚的表演和表达令他十分感动。他也特别向学校校长Gonzales及全体教职员工表达感谢，肯定学校为活动所作出的准备和安排。 秦伟平表示，自从离开美国海军以来，今年已经是他连续第四年参加学校举办的退伍军人节活动。他注意到，今年活动的规模比往年更大，也看到了更多退伍军人家庭和现役军人家庭参与学校及社区生活。 他在文章中向学生们表达了自己的期望：珍惜学习机会，勇敢追求梦想，充分利用自由社会所提供的成长机会。他认为，孩子们能够安心学习、快乐成长并自由追求未来，正是几代美国军人长期服役、努力守护的重要意义。 Seven Lakes Junior High：与教育工作者交流，关注教师待遇 随后，秦伟平还参加了Seven Lakes Junior High举办的退伍军人节活动。 与Shafer Elementary以学生表演和校园庆祝为主的活动氛围不同，这次活动也为秦伟平提供了与其他退伍军人家长、教师及学校社区成员交流的机会。 在秦伟平发布的另一篇文章中，他特别提到，与一位从事特殊教育工作的代课教师交谈，给自己留下了深刻印象。 据秦伟平转述，这位教师主要协助有特殊学习及行为需求的学生，工作需要高度的耐心、责任感和持续投入，但她向他表示，自己的时薪只有13美元。 这一情况引起了秦伟平对学校基层教育人员薪酬和人才留任问题的关注。 他在文章中提出一个问题：如果教育工作者承担的工作责任和实际压力，无法得到相应的薪酬与支持，学区又该如何吸引和留住足够优秀、富有责任感的教育人才？ 秦伟平认为，教师和学校工作人员是公共教育体系的重要组成部分，他们的工作不仅关系到课堂教学，也直接影响学生的学习体验、特殊教育支持以及学校整体运行。 需要指出的是，13美元时薪是秦伟平根据与一位代课教师的个人交谈所转述的信息，目前并非经过学区公开薪酬资料独立核实的普遍薪酬标准。不同岗位、雇佣方式和工作安排之间可能存在差异。 不过，这次交流反映出他希望进一步了解基层教育工作人员实际工作状况的意愿，也将教师薪酬与人才招聘、留任问题带入其对当地教育治理的讨论。 从军旅服役到教育公共事务：关注服务与下一代 秦伟平曾在美国海军服役，退役后继续从事美国联邦政府公共服务工作。目前，他居住在Katy社区，是三个Katy ISD在校学生的父亲。 2026年11月11日，他选择在美国退伍军人节正式宣布竞选Katy ISD Board of Trustees, Position 6（学区董事会第六选区），计划参加2027年5月的学区董事会选举。 在其近期公开发布的竞选信息和个人文章中，教育工作者支持、学生发展、校园环境、学区财政管理及社区沟通等问题，均是其重点关注的方向。 对于此次参加两所学校的活动，秦伟平将其视为一次与学校社区深入交流的机会。他认为，退伍军人节不仅是纪念军人服役经历的日子，也让社区有机会重新认识公共服务、家庭责任以及下一代成长所需要的社会支持。 他在Substack文章中写道，作为一名美国海军退伍军人和三个孩子的父亲，他希望将对服务与责任的理解延伸到社区教育事务中。如果当选学区董事，他将关注教师薪酬和工作支持，倾听教师及学校工作人员的意见，并推动学区政策和资源配置更加贴近学生与教育一线的实际需求。 秦伟平表示，教师待遇不仅是劳动报酬问题，也关系到学区能否吸引和留住教育人才，以及学生能否获得稳定、持续的教育支持。 教师支持与学生发展：地方教育治理中的长期议题 Katy ISD是休斯顿西部地区重要的公共教育学区，学校教育涉及学生、家长、教师、行政人员及不同背景的社区家庭。 教师招聘与留任、特殊教育资源、学校工作人员待遇以及教育资源配置，都是地方学区治理中需要持续关注的议题。 从Shafer Elementary学生为退伍军人准备的荣誉墙和表演，到Seven Lakes Junior High一线教育工作者分享的工作经历，秦伟平在同一天接触到学校社区的不同侧面。 前者体现了学校对军人及其家庭的尊重，后者则使教师工作条件和基层教育支持问题进入他的视野。 秦伟平在文章最后向两所学校的领导、教师、工作人员、家长及学生表达感谢，并表示，希望继续倾听社区不同群体的声音，为改善Katy ISD教育环境和学生成长机会贡献力量。 他将当天的感受概括为：致敬曾经服役的人，关爱今天教书育人的人，投资明天的下一代。 这也成为他在2026年退伍军人节参加两所学校活动后，对公共服务与地方教育责任所作出的个人总结。 相关信息： 秦伟平竞选职务：Katy ISD Board of Trustees, Position 6 选举时间：2027年5月 竞选网站： https://www.weipingqintx.com/ 个人动态：X、Facebook及Substack平台。

title: Military Makes up Majority of Expulsions at Fifth Plenum
zh_title: 五中全会驱逐人员中军人占多数
summary: 内容提要：五中全会的三分之二驱逐事件与中华人民共和国（PRC）的国防机构有关。被开除干部的背景表明，无论是专业资格还是与习近平的长期个人关系都无法提供可靠的保护以免受纪律调查。正在进行的清洗主要影响的是中国人民解放军（PLA）军队。与此同时，空军没有被驱逐，这强化了这样的评估：空军可能会在重建后的解放军最高指挥部中获得更大的影响力。正式开除
content:
内容提要：五中全会的三分之二驱逐事件与中华人民共和国（PRC）的国防机构有关。被开除干部的背景表明，无论是专业资格还是与习近平的长期个人关系都无法提供可靠的保护以免受纪律调查。正在进行的清洗主要影响的是中国人民解放军（PLA）军队。与此同时，空军没有被驱逐，这强化了这样的评估：空军可能会在重建后的解放军最高指挥部中获得更大的影响力。全会上正式开除的决定表明，无理缺席党内重大活动是政治垮台的明确信号：16名被开除的官员中有11人缺席2025年10月的四中全会，另外两人随后立即从公众视野中消失。中国反腐败监管机构正在密切关注国防工业领导人。进一步的调查可能会扰乱航空航天和造船业，给中国的国防工业基础和军事现代化带来新的挑战。中国共产党中央委员会最近召开了五中全会，重点关注党内纪律、权力集中、思想强化和人事调整（《中国简报》，11 月 3 日；IISS，11 月 4 日）。
其中一项突出进展是开除33名中央委员的党籍（IDSS报，11月4日）。其中涉及16名武装部队军官和17名文职干部，其中六人与国防国有企业关系密切（《早报》，10月30日）。尽管中央军委副主席张升民进入政治局引起了分析人士的广泛关注，但大规模驱逐前军官和国防工业领导人也同样重要，甚至更重要——揭示了对中国武装部队状况的有意义的见解。军队开除 在被开除军官名单中名列前茅的是前解放军将军、中央军委副主席张又侠。作为中越边境冲突期间的一名功勋指挥官，张在2017年至2026年担任中央军委副主席期间还一直担任政治局委员，是最高军事和民事决策机构之间的关键纽带。尽管张与习近平有着长期的关系，但他不知何故与中国领导人发生了冲突，并于 2026 年 1 月被免职并被拘留，与他在一起的还有刘振立。刘振立是一位陆军将领、战争英雄，曾在中央军委任职，并于 2022 年至 2026 年担任中国人民解放军参谋长。
中央于 2026 年 9 月首次开除张、刘的党籍，随后在五中全会上重申了这一决定（中国最高法院，9 月 21 日）继张、刘之后的是中国人民解放军海军上将王仁华，他于 2019 年至 2025 年担任中央军委政法委员会书记，负责军事司法系统和反间谍工作。王于 2025 年 10 月失踪，一切都没有发生。直到最近他被开除出中共，才听说过他（财新，2025 年 10 月 28 日）。刘青松，海军上将，2023年至2025年任东部战区政委。他与去年10月被清洗的东部战区司令员林向阳一起工作（《中国简报》，2025年11月25日）。刘就是其中之一

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Two thirds of the Fifth Plenum’s expulsions are tied to the national defense apparatus in the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The backgrounds of expelled cadres suggest that neither professional credentials nor longstanding personal relationships with Xi offer reliable protection against disciplinary investigations. The ongoing purge mainly affected the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Army. The absence of Air Force expulsions, meanwhile, reinforces the assessment that the service may gain greater influence in the reconstructed PLA high command. Expulsions formalized at the plenum suggest that unjustified absence from major Party events is an unambiguous signal of political downfall: Eleven of the 16 expelled officers were absent from the Fourth Plenum in October 2025, while two others disappeared from public view immediately afterwards. Chinese anti-corruption watchdogs are keeping defense industry leaders under close scrutiny. Further investigations could disrupt the aerospace and shipbuilding sectors, creating new challenges for the PRC’s defense industrial base and military modernization. The Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) Central Committee recently concluded its Fifth Plenum, focusing on internal Party discipline, the centralization of power, ideological reinforcement, and personnel reshuffles ( China Brief , November 3; IISS , November 4). One outstanding development was the expulsion of 33 Central Committee members from the Party ( IDSS Paper , November 4). These involved 16 armed forces officers and 17 civilian cadres, six of whom were closely linked with defense state-owned enterprises ( Zaobao , October 30). Although the promotion of Central Military Commission (CMC) Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin (张升民) to the Politburo attracted considerable analyst attention, the mass expulsion of former military officers and defense industry leaders is of equal, if not greater, importance—revealing meaningful insights on the state of the Chinese armed forces. Armed Forces Expulsions At the top of the list of expelled military officers is former People’s Liberation Army (PLA) general and CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Youxia (张又侠). As a decorated commander during the Sino-Vietnamese border conflict, Zhang also served on the Politburo throughout his tenure as CMC vice chairman from 2017–2026, serving as a critical link between top military and civilian decision-making organs. Despite his longstanding ties with Xi, Zhang somehow ran afoul of the Chinese leader and was removed and detained in January 2026, alongside Liu Zhenli (刘振立), a fellow Army general and war hero who served on the CMC and as the PLA chief of staff from 2022–2026. The Central Committee first expelled Zhang and Liu from the Party in September 2026, before it reaffirmed the decision at the Fifth Plenum ( China Supreme Court , September 21) Following Zhang and Liu is PLA Navy admiral Wang Renhua (王仁华), who served as secretary of the CMC political and legal affairs commission from 2019–2025, in charge of the military justice system and counterespionage. Wang disappeared in October 2025 and nothing was heard of him until his recent expulsion from the CCP ( Caixin , October 28, 2025). Liu Qingsong (刘青松) is a Navy admiral who served as the political commissar of the Eastern Theater Command from 2023–2025. He worked with the disgraced Eastern Theater Command Commander Lin Xiangyang (林向阳), who was purged in October last year ( China Brief , November 25, 2025). Liu was one of at least 18 officers absent at the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 ( Sing Tao Daily , October 27, 2025; BBC , November 7, 2025). His whereabouts remained unknown until his expulsion at the Fifth Plenum. Army general Huang Ming (黄铭) first vanished from public view in July 2025 and was absent at the subsequent Fourth Plenum. The commander of the Northern Theater Command from 2024–2025, Huang was once regarded as a promising leader within the Army ( Zaobao , August 3, 2024). His expulsion at the Fifth Plenum, however, sealed his fate. Li Qiaoming (李桥铭) was another elite Army general with a long list of professional accomplishments. He rose from a simple soldier to become the fourth commander of the PLA Army in 2022. Yet Li was missing in action during the Fourth Plenum last year and was booted out of the National People’s Congress (NPC) in February 2026 ( Xinhua , February 26). His expulsion from the CCP at the Fifth Plenum made him the third Army commander to be purged since the post was created in 2015 amid changes to the military’s organizational structure known as the “Deepening National Defense and Military Reform” (深化国防和军队改革). Army general Li Wei (李伟) was the third political commissar of the now-disbanded Strategic Support Force and then became the first political commissar of the Information Support Force, founded in 2024 to succeed the Strategic Support Force’s cyber capabilities ( Zaobao , April 20, 2024; China Brief, April 26, 2024 [ a ], [ b ]). Like Li Qiaoming, Li Wei failed to attend the Fourth Plenum and was removed from the NPC in February 2026. He was formally expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. Zhang Hongbing (张红兵) spent most of his career in the PLA Army before transferring to the People’s Armed Police in 2022 as its political commissar, attaining the rank of general. He disappeared from public view for most of 2025, including the Fourth Plenum, and was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum ( Zaobao , December 24, 2025). Wang Haijiang (汪海江) was regarded as a capable Army officer who fought in the Sino-Vietnamese border conflict ( China Brief , June 7). He spent over a decade serving at senior PLA posts in Xinjiang and Tibet before becoming the Western Theater Command commander in 2021. He did not attend the Fourth Plenum in October 2025 and was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. The same fate befell Army lieutenant general Yang Cheng (杨诚), the political commissar of the Xinjiang military district from 2020–2025 who most likely maintained working relations with Wang Haijiang ( Caixin , April 6, 2021). Three former heads of CMC departments were also expelled following their absence from last year’s Fourth Plenum. They were Army lieutenant general Wang Peng (王鹏), who headed the CMC training and administration department from 2021–2025; Army lieutenant general Liu Faqing (刘发庆), who led the CMC national defense mobilization department from 2021–2025; and Navy vice admiral Zhao Xiaozhe (赵晓哲), who previously oversaw the CMC science and technology department. Separately, Army lieutenant general Zhang Lin (张林), director of the CMC logistics support department from 2022–2025, was removed from the NPC last October and expelled at the Fifth Plenum ( Zaobao , October 16, 2025). Last but not least, Army lieutenant generals Zhong Shaojun (钟绍军) and Fang Yongxiang (方永祥) were both considered confidants of Xi. Zhong assisted Xi since the latter’s tenure in Zhejiang in the early 2000s ( VOA , August 29). After Xi came to power, he brought Zhong into the PLA as a senior colonel, despite having no military experience, to manage the crucial CMC chairman’s office that supported Xi’s daily work schedule ( China Brief , September 14). Zhong subsequently became director of the CMC general office that provided administrative and logistical support to all CMC members, before eventually serving as political commissar of the National Defense University. He vanished in October 2025 and was removed from the NPC in August 2026, prior to his expulsion from the Party in October ( Zaobao , October 29). Fang succeeded Zhong in leading both the CMC chairman’s office and CMC general office, indicating a high level of trust that Xi had in him ( SCMP , October 26, 2024). Like many previously mentioned officers, Fang failed to attend the Fourth Plenum, with no news regarding his whereabouts until his expulsion from the CCP at the recent Fifth Plenum. Defense Industry Expulsions Other than military officers, Sun Shaopin (孙绍骋), former minister of veterans affairs from 2018–2022, was also expelled from the Party ( Caixin , January 29). Moreover, one third of the 17 civilian cadres expelled at the Fifth Plenum were associated with state-owned defense enterprises. At the top of the expulsion list was Lei Fanpei (雷凡培). He had a long career in the country’s aerospace industry, rising from an ordinary designer to become chairman of the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC). From 2018–2022, Lei was the chairman of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC) ( World Ships , October 31). From 2022–2025, Lei served as the deputy director at the Office of Central Military-Civil Fusion Development Commission (中央军民融合发展委员会办公室) ( Zaobao , October 31, 2024). Despite being an experienced technocrat and crucial link between defense companies and policymakers, Lei was expelled from the Party at the Fifth Plenum. Several other senior leaders from the defense sector were expelled at the same time. They include former chairman of the China National Nuclear Corporation Yu Jianfeng (余剑锋); former chairman of CASC Yuan Jie (袁洁), who was removed in 2024 likely in connection with the Rocket Force investigations that year ( Radio Free Asia , April 15, 2024); Zhang Zhongyang (张忠阳), former chairman of CASC and head of the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology, the country’s largest research, development, and production institution for carrier rockets and missile systems ( Zaobao , January 30, 2024); Wen Gang (温刚), former chairman of Norinco and CSSC ( Caixin , October 30); and Jin Donghan (金东寒), an engine and marine propulsion research specialist and former president of Shanghai University and Tianjin University. Jin spent decades researching engines for the PRC’s defense industry and led the CSSC’s Shanghai Marine Diesel Engine Research Institute that specializes in marine diesel and gas engines, power systems, electrical and automation systems, and energy equipment ( 163 , January 15). Scope of Purge Shows Inter-Service Political Priorities As the largest PLA service, the Army predominated among those expelled, accounting for 11 of the 16 military officers. The Navy follows with three officers, Information Support Force and the People’s Armed Police each account for one. Neither the Air Force nor Rocket Force saw any expulsions this time. While the lack of Rocket Force expulsions may be linked to the broad purges that decimated its top leadership in 2023 and the subsequent years, the absence of Air Force expulsions again highlights this service as the least affected by the purges so far. This reinforces the author’s previous assessment that the Air Force is set to gain influence within the reconstructed PLA high command, as its senior leadership remains comparatively intact ( The Diplomat , August 11). The professional backgrounds of expelled officers also reveal important patterns in the direction of the purge. Military officers with extensive command experience constitute seven cases while political commissars account for six, followed by three defense technocrats. This shows that the commanders and commissars of major PLA organizations are most at risk. The authorities appear to make no distinction between commanders or commissars when conducting investigations. In comparison, defense technocrats, who tend to stay in the background, seem to be less affected by the current campaign. Interestingly, three expelled officers had close personal ties with Xi, with relations dating back years, if not decades. But this did not save them from being purged, indicating that Xi does not tolerate any malfeasance or signs of disloyalty among military officers, regardless of their personal relations with him. Fourth Plenum Absences as a Potential Purge Indicator Another recurring theme is the connection between the expelled and the Fourth Plenum. Out of 16 officers expelled at the Fifth Plenum, 11 were absent from the Fourth Plenum in October 2025, with two more—Wang Renhua and Zhong Shaojun—disappearing from public view immediately after the gathering. This suggests that these 13 officers had likely been detained and placed under investigation around the time of the Fourth Plenum. This sequence teaches us that absence from key Party meetings is an early warning sign of political trouble and missing individuals are likely to end up as purge victims. It is worth noting that several other officers absent from the Fourth Plenum have not yet been expelled. They include Commander of the Southern Theater Command Wu Ya’nan (吴亚男); Political Commissar of the Central Theater Command Xu Deqing (徐德清); Commander of the PLA Navy Hu Zhongming (胡中明), and Political Commissar of the PLA Rocket Force Xu Xisheng (徐西盛) ( Sing Tao Daily , October 27, 2025; BBC , November 7, 2025). Despite having no news and public appearance since the Fourth Plenum, events at the Fifth Plenum suggest that they have met their downfall. Turning to the defense industry, the affiliations of the expelled executives reveal a clear concentration of those associated with CASC and CSSC. Others were linked to the China National Nuclear Corporation, Norinco, and key research institutions developing missiles and marine engines. There may be parallels between the depth of corruption within these corporations and the quality of their equipment, echoing concerns previously raised about Rocket Force vulnerabilities ( CNA , January 11, 2024). As investigations are likely to expand in these sectors, the disruptions could have negative consequences for the PRC’s defense industrial base and military modernization. Conclusion The armed forces and defense industry cadres constitute a two-third majority of Fifth Plenum expulsions, an extraordinary development when personnel involved in national defense only account for a minority within the entire Party-state elite. While the rise of CMC Vice Chairman Zhang Shengmin reestablished formal communications between the Politburo and the PLA, the Fifth Plenum’s expulsions offer broader insights into the state of the PLA. As Xi reconstructs the high command, the Fifth Plenum reminds us that trust between the commander-in-chief and his generals remains low ( The Diplomat , July 6). While it is not difficult to appoint new people to top posts, building confidence and rapport is a long-term project that might be undermined by frequent leadership instability. The post Military Makes up Majority of Expulsions at Fifth Plenum appeared first on Jamestown .

title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia boss entered Taiwan on Hong Kong passport
zh_title: 被指控监视英伟达老板的中国女子持香港护照进入台湾
summary: 台湾移民机构周三表示，在当局调查这一事件时，这名被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。这张来自 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，爱丽丝·黄（右二，粉红色）于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台北一家餐厅参加由 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左二，黑色后置摄像头）举办的晚宴。照片：法新社。据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡 Megaspeed w 的中国前高管 Alice Huang 有染。
content:
台湾移民机构周三表示，在当局调查这一事件时，这名被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。这张来自 CTI 视频片段的屏幕截图显示，爱丽丝·黄（右二，粉红色）于 2025 年 5 月 22 日在台北一家餐厅参加由 Nvidia 首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋（左二，黑色后置摄像头）举办的晚宴。照片：法新社。据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡Megaspeed公司前中国高管爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，美国官员认为她为中国情报机构工作。北京否认了间谍指控。英伟达董事会周日宣布，已对该公司首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋展开调查，他与黄爱丽没有任何关系。入出国及移民署署长林弘恩对记者表示，“我国政府相关机构已充分了解相关记录和信息”，并证实黄丽娟使用香港护照进入台湾。 “我们知道她所有的相关出入境记录。”一般来说，香港护照持有者比持有中国大陆护照的人更容易进入台湾，后者还必须申请特别许可才能前往台湾。额外的限制部分是由于中国与台湾之间的复杂关系，北京声称并誓言要将台湾置于其控制之下。
积极调查 台湾内政部长刘世芳表示，黄爱丽“确实入境了，但她目前在海外”。“如果我们知道她是间谍，我们肯定不会让她进入台湾，”刘在国会告诉议员。她说：“我们将审查我们的程序，特别是预筛选、临时抽查和访谈以及访问后措施。” “据我们了解，这名黄女士的通行证已被吊销，这意味着她不可能再次进入台湾。”黄仁勋于 2025 年 10 月 31 日在庆州庆州艺术中心举行的亚太经济合作组织 (APEC) 首席执行官峰会上发表演讲。照片：Anthony Wallace/法新社。台湾官员拒绝透露黄爱丽访问台湾的日期，也拒绝透露她访问台湾的次数。刘周二表示，台湾“国家安全部门正在积极调查此事”。 2025 年 5 月，台湾顶级科技博览会台北国际电脑展期间，黄仁勋 (Alice Huang)，又名黄乐 (Huang Le)，出席了黄仁勋在台北一家中餐厅举办的晚宴。记者站在餐厅外，透过玻璃门窗拍摄黄仁勋和一名身穿粉色连衣裙、名叫爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的女子与其他与会者混在一起的情况。媒体直播显示，有一次，黄仁勋用手臂搂住黄爱丽丝，而她亲吻了他的右脸颊。

【原文 English Original】
The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan, the island’s immigration agency said Wednesday, as authorities investigate the incident. This screengrab from video footage by CTI shows Alice Huang (2nd R in pink) attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (2nd L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025. Photo: AFP. Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a Chinese former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it had opened a probe into Jensen Huang, the company’s chief executive and co-founder, who is no relation to Alice Huang. “Our government’s relevant agencies are fully informed of the relevant records and information,” National Immigration Agency Director-General Lin Horng-en told reporters, confirming that Alice Huang used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan. “We were aware of all her relevant entry and exit records.” It is generally easier for Hong Kong passport holders to enter Taiwan than those with mainland Chinese passports, who must also apply for special permission to travel there. The additional restrictions are partly due to the complex relations between China and Taiwan, which Beijing claims and has vowed to bring under its control. Active investigation Taiwan’s Interior Minister Liu Shyh-fang said Alice Huang “did indeed enter the country, but she is currently overseas”. “If we had known she was a spy, we certainly would not have let her enter Taiwan,” Liu told lawmakers in parliament. “We will review our procedures, specifically our pre-screening, interim spot checks and interviews, and post-visit measures,” she said. “As far as we understand, this Ms Huang has had her permit revoked, meaning it is impossible for her to enter Taiwan again.” Jensen Huang delivers a speech during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit at the Gyeongju Arts Center in Gyeongju on October 31, 2025. Photo: Anthony Wallace/AFP. Taiwanese officials refused to share the dates of Alice Huang’s trips to Taiwan or say how many times she had visited. On Tuesday, Liu said Taiwan’s “national security units are actively investigating the matter”. Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show.

content:
Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

（中央社記者李雅雯上海13日電）2026中美政黨對話在北京舉行，適逢川習年度三會前。中共中聯部長劉海星強調，中美應秉持相互尊重、和平共處、合作共贏原則，共同夯實中美建設性戰略穩定關係基礎。
2026中美政黨對話12日在北京舉行。據新華社、新京報等媒體報導，美國政黨、戰略界、工商界代表與中國有關部門、地方政府、智庫、大學、民間機構代表與會，雙方以「在變化的亞太和世界中探索新時代中美正確相處之道」為交流主題。
劉海星在主旨講話中表示，一個穩定、健康、可持續發展的中美關係不僅符合兩國人民利益，也是亞太和世界和平繁榮的重要保障。
他說，中國國家主席習近平、美國總統川普（Donald Trump）在半年內實現互訪，創造中美交往歷史。兩國元首同意構建「基於尊重、公平、對等的中美建設性戰略穩定關係」，為中美關係未來發展指明方向。
他強調，中美應秉持相互尊重、和平共處、合作共贏的原則，一起探索新時代兩個大國正確相處之道。雙方應樹立正確認知，有效管控分歧、拓展互利合作、促進人文交流、承擔大國責任，共同努力夯實中美建設性戰略穩定關係基礎。
美方代表表示，美中關係趨於穩定平衡，有利於各自發展目標的實現和國際治理難題解決。雙方應持續加強溝通對話，透過良性競爭和互利合作實現共同發展。
前美國駐中大使包可士（Max Baucus）與會2026中美政黨對話。
包可士接受央視採訪時說，非常高興中美兩國元首今年已經會晤兩次，兩國元首見面愈多次愈好，因為他們都希望取得好成果。中美是兩個不一樣的國家，不過都實力強大，關鍵在於找到力量、經濟、地緣政治影響力的平衡。
亞太經濟合作會議（APEC）深圳領導人峰會將於下週召開，習近平、川普擬將進行今年第3度會晤，前兩次會晤分別為5月北京、9月華盛頓；雙方有望將於12月邁阿密G20峰會上進行今年第4度會晤。（編輯：陳鎧妤）1151113

summary: 河套区年底引领香港创新及跨境数据流动 |中国劳工布告栏 周五, 13 11 2026 · 香港 香港和中国劳工新闻英文版 河套区将在年底引领香港创新及跨境数据流动 创新科技及工业局常任秘书长蔡康永表示，河套深港科技创新合作区将引领香港创新发展，并预计在2026年底前实现跨境数据流动成果。其他发言者强调了人工智能领域的机遇，创新局常任秘书长蔡杰明、
content:
河套区年底引领香港创新及跨境数据流动 |中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
河套区年底前引领香港创新及跨境数据流动
创新科技及工业局常任秘书长蔡康永表示，河套深港科技创新合作区将引领香港创新发展，预计2026年底跨境数据流动取得成果。其他发言者强调了人工智能的机遇，
创新科技及工业局常任秘书长蔡杰明周五在星岛环球经济峰会2026论坛上表示，河套深港科技创新合作区是香港创新科技发展的引领者。他表示，高新区将发挥国家制度创新试验区作用，促进创新要素跨境有序流动。
蔡先生预计，跨境数据流动的成果将在年底前收获，支持人工智能、生命科学等创新科技产业的发展。他表示，跨境数据壁垒一直是深港创新科技合作的障碍。
香港城市大学人工智能首席教授、香港人工智能科学研究所所长马伟英建议，当前全球社会正处于新科学时代，香港应重点关注人工智能+生物制药的赛道。他指出，香港拥有强大的大学集群、完善的生物安全和数据监管体系等先天优势，可以实现中国内地生物科技创新资源与全球市场的双向融合，促进医药研究成果向全球开放。
香港数字资产协会联合创始人区伟志在同一论坛上表示，随着监管和基础设施日益完善，香港现在拥有大规模实施区块链应用的黄金机遇。他进一步建议通过代币化存款优化港股交易机制，实现T+0即时交易，突破现有T+2限制。他表示，香港可以利用本地财库优势，发展人民币和黄金稳定币，打造国际黄金交易中心。
人工智能代理B.AI产品总监Nick Chen表示，人工智能代理支付技术已经成熟，但指出目前在收付场景上面临局限性，行业多采用发行代币的方式完成交易。

Hetao zone to lead HK innovation, cross-border data flow by year-end | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 13 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hetao zone to lead HK innovation, cross-border data flow by year-end
Kevin Choi, Permanent Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, said the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone will lead HK's innovation development and expects cross-border data flow results by end-2026. Other speakers highlighted opportunities in AI,
Kevin Choi Kit-ming, Permanent Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry, said on Friday at a discussion forum of the Sing Tao Global Economic Summit 2026 that the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science and Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone serves as a leader for Hong Kong's innovation and technology development. He added that the zone will leverage its designated role as a pilot zone for institutional innovation granted by the state to promote the orderly cross-border flow of innovative elements.
Choi expects that the fruits of cross-border data flow will be reaped by the end of the year, supporting the development of innovation and technology industries such as artificial intelligence and life sciences. He noted that cross-border data barriers have always been an obstacle in Shenzhen-Hong Kong innovation and technology cooperation.
Ma Wei-ying, Chief of AI and Director of the Hong Kong Institute of AI for Science (HKAI-Sci) at City University of Hong Kong, suggested that Hong Kong focus on the track of AI plus biopharmaceuticals, as the global society is currently in a new scientific era. He pointed to Hong Kong's inherent advantages, including a strong cluster of universities, as well as a comprehensive biosafety and data regulatory system, which enables two-way integration of mainland China's biotechnology innovation resources with the global market, thus facilitating global access to pharmaceutical research results.
Alex Au Wai-chi, Co-Founder of Hong Kong Digital Asset Society, said on the same forum that Hong Kong now possesses the golden opportunity for large-scale implementation of blockchain applications, citing increasingly comprehensive regulations and infrastructure. He further suggested optimising the Hong Kong stock trading mechanism through tokenised deposits to achieve T+0 instant trading, breaking through the existing T+2 limitation. He indicated that Hong Kong can leverage its local treasury advantages to develop yuan and gold stablecoins, creating an international gold trading centre.
Nick Chen, Product Director of B.AI, an AI agent, stated that AI agent payment is technically mature, but pointed out that it currently faces limitations in collection and payment scenarios, with industries often using token issuance to complete transactions.

content:
香港海关在机场缉毒行动中逮捕内地男子中国劳工公告栏
星期五, 13 十一月 2026 · 香港 香港及中国劳工新闻英文版
香港海关在机场缉毒行动中逮捕内地男子
香港海关人员在香港国际机场从一名57岁的中国内地男子身上检获怀疑大麻。他被指控贩运危险毒品，将于 11 月 14 日出庭。
2026 年 11 月 13 日 17:55 香港时间 · 更新于 11 月 13 日 18:18 · 阅读时间 1 分钟
11月13日，香港海关人员在香港国际机场缉毒行动中截获一名57岁的中国内地男性旅客。搜查他的手提行李时发现了一定数量的疑似大麻，导致他立即被捕。
该男子被指控犯有一项贩运危险毒品罪。他定于11月14日在西九龙裁判法院受审。
海关表示，将继续通过情报分析加强打击贩毒活动。发言人呼吁公众保持警惕，不要接受任何将受管制物品运进或运出香港以获取经济利益的提议或指派，也不要在未核实物品性质的情况下帮助他人携带该等物品。
根据香港《危险药物条例》，贩运危险药物属严重罪行。犯罪者一经定罪，最高可被罚款港币 500 万元及终身监禁。
海关表示，将维持风险管理模式，重点检查来自高风险地区的旅客，有效打击跨境贩毒活动。
市民可致电海关24小时热线182 8080、电邮[email protected]或使用网上表格eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002举报怀疑贩毒活动。

Hong Kong customs arrest mainland man in airport drug bust | China Labour Bulletin Board
Friday, 13 Nov 2026 · Hong Kong Hong Kong and China labour news in English
Hong Kong customs arrest mainland man in airport drug bust
Hong Kong customs officers seized suspected cannabis from a 57-year-old mainland Chinese man at Hong Kong International Airport. He was charged with trafficking a dangerous drug and will appear in court on 14 November.
13 Nov 2026 at 17:55 HKT · updated 13 Nov, 18:18 · 1 min read
Hong Kong customs officers intercepted a 57-year-old mainland Chinese male passenger at Hong Kong International Airport on 13 November during an anti-drug operation. A search of his hand luggage uncovered a quantity of suspected cannabis, leading to his immediate arrest.
The man has been charged with one count of trafficking a dangerous drug. He is scheduled to appear before the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 14 November.
Customs said it would continue to strengthen efforts to combat drug trafficking through intelligence analysis. It urged the public to remain vigilant and not to accept any offer or assignment to transport controlled items into or out of Hong Kong for financial gain, nor to help others carry such items without verifying their nature.
Under Hong Kong's Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking in a dangerous drug is a serious offence. Upon conviction, an offender faces a maximum fine of HK$5 million and life imprisonment.
Customs said it would maintain its risk-management approach, focusing inspections on passengers arriving from high-risk areas to effectively combat cross-border drug trafficking.
Members of the public can report suspected drug trafficking activities by calling the customs 24-hour hotline at 182 8080, emailing [email protected], or using the online form at eform.cefs.gov.hk/form/ced002.

summary: Nvidia 在台北市政府规划中的总部的履行义务 - 焦点台湾 Nvidia 在台北市政府规划中的总部的履行义务 要激活文本转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。中新社台北11月13日电 台北市政府周五表示，英伟达台湾子公司正在履行该公司计划在北投士林科技园区设立海外总部的所有合同义务。英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋周四因涉嫌与女性发生婚外情而辞职。
content:
台北市政府：英伟达履行了规划总部的义务 - 焦点台湾
台北市政府：英伟达履行了规划总部的义务
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
中新社台北11月13日电 台北市政府周五表示，英伟达台湾子公司正在履行该公司计划在北投士林科技园区设立海外总部的所有合同义务。
英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋周四因涉嫌与一名涉嫌为中国情报机构工作的女性发生婚外情而辞职。
英伟达董事会随后宣布黄仁勋辞去总裁、首席执行官和董事会成员的职务，首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)同意担任临时首席执行官。
市政府表示，该土地权合同由英伟达台湾公司签署，该公司已按照协议规定缴纳了履约保证金、土地出让金和土地租金。
市政府表示，Nvidia 于 7 月 15 日提交了建筑许可申请，审查小组于 11 月 5 日批准了该项目的基础工作计划。
台北市政府城市发展局预计将于11月底召开城市设计审查委员会会议。
市政府补充说，如果该计划获得批准，英伟达将能够开始建设。
英伟达收购的北投士林科技园T17、T18地块。 CNA档案照片
市政府表示，英伟达在评估该项目并寻求土地使用权后，决定通过当地子公司设立海外总部。
因此，预计首席执行官的变更不会影响子公司的合同义务，并敦促公众避免可能损害双方之间信任或破坏协议的猜测。
市政府承诺将继续监督该项目并帮助该公司获得必要的批准，以帮助总部尽快竣工并投入运营。
今年 2 月，台北与 Nvidia 签署了价值 122 亿新台币（约合 3.71 亿美元）的协议，获得北投士林科技园区 T17 和 T18 地块 50 年土地使用权，并可选择将期限延长至 20 年。

Nvidia meeting obligations for planned HQ: Taipei City gov't
To activate the text-to-speech service, please first agree to the privacy policy below.
Taipei, Nov. 13 (CNA) The Taipei City government said Friday that Nvidia Corp.'s Taiwan subsidiary was meeting all its contractual obligations for the company's planned overseas headquarters at the Beitou-Shilin Technology Park.
The statement came after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (黃仁勳) resigned Thursday following reports of an alleged extramarital relationship involving a woman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia's board subsequently announced Huang had resigned as president, CEO and a board member, and that Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress had agreed to serve as interim CEO.
The city government said the land rights contract was signed by Nvidia Iconic Taiwan Co., which has made the required performance bond, land premium and land rent payments in accordance with the agreement.
Nvidia submitted its building permit application on July 15, while a review panel approved plans for the project's foundation work on Nov. 5, the city government said.
The Taipei City government's Department of Urban Development is expected to convene an urban design review committee meeting by the end of November.
If the plan is approved, Nvidia will be able to begin construction, the city government added.
The T17 and T18 plots at Beitou-Shilin Technology Park acquired by Nvidia. CNA file photo
The city government said Nvidia's decision to establish its overseas headquarters through its local subsidiary came after the company assessed the project and sought to secure the land rights.
It therefore did not expect a change of CEO to affect the subsidiary's contractual obligations and urged the public to avoid speculation that could damage trust between the parties or undermine the agreement.
The city government pledged to continue monitoring the project and helping the company obtain the necessary approvals to help complete the headquarters and make it operational as soon as possible.
In February, Taipei signed a NT$12.2 billion (US$371 million) agreement with Nvidia for 50-year land rights to the T17 and T18 plots at Beitou-Shilin Technology Park, with an option to extend the term by up to 20 years.

summary: 新报告确定了香港在世界航运中的地位 - Splash247 香港海事周即将拉开帷幕。为了庆祝这一时刻，Splash 今天出版了一本 48 页的杂志，介绍该市的海运中心资质。船舶可以在中国大陆的造船厂订购，通过香港的一家租赁公司拥有，在伦敦投保，通过亚洲的管理机构配备船员，并从新加坡租用。其货物永远不需要经过香港港口。就连其香港融资工具也可能必须在其他地方寻求信贷批准。航运地理一直很复杂
content:
新报告确定香港在世界航运中的地位 - Splash247
香港海事周即将拉开帷幕。为了庆祝这一时刻，Splash 今天出版了一本 48 页的杂志，介绍该市的海运中心资质。
船舶可以在中国大陆的造船厂订购，通过香港的一家租赁公司拥有，在伦敦投保，通过亚洲的管理机构配备船员，并从新加坡租用。其货物永远不需要经过香港港口。就连其香港融资工具也可能必须在其他地方寻求信贷批准。
航运地理一直很复杂。改变的是香港必须询问真正的业务发生在哪里的紧迫性。这座城市本身是否仍然是一个海事之都，因其提供的服务而被国际业主、贸易商和金融家选择？或者它正在成为隔壁庞大的工业和商业机器的高度复杂的服务柜台？
从纸面上看，答案看起来令人放心。香港在2026年新华-波罗的海国际航运中心排名中仍排名第四，仅次于新加坡、上海和伦敦。三大世界领先的船舶管理公司总部均设于此，主要的保赔协会在此运营，这座城市拥有大量的律师、金融家和技术专家。
然而，望向海滨，却出现了不同的景象。 2025 年，该集装箱港口吞吐量为 1,299 万标准箱，仅相当于 2008 年峰值的一半。由于地缘政治动荡，登记吨位大幅减少，到今年 6 月已降至 1.09 亿吨。上海、深圳、广州已经成长为航运巨头，其物理优势是香港无法现实推翻的。
这些故事并不矛盾。他们共同定义了贯穿本特别报告的核心问题：香港能否将其继承的海事优势转化为 2030 年可持续的商业模式，即使其传统的重要性衡量标准变得不再那么讨人喜欢。
香港船东会主席理查德·赫斯特(Richard Heext)反对香港被降级为内地附属机构的说法。
他表示：“世界排名前 10 的船舶管理公司中的 3 个、12 个国际集团保赔协会中的 11 个、排名前 10 的船舶融资账簿管理人中的 8 个都没有在‘附属建筑’中入驻。”他还提到了该市的法律机构和国际行业组织。
该库存代表了数十年的投资和商业信任。然而，它并没有解决更困难的问题，即这些机构在这里实际做什么，或者它们的下一次扩张是否会在其他地方进行。
香港在这十年的大部分时间里都在努力提高自己在税收方面的吸引力。符合资格的船舶出租商可享受零利得税；符合条件的船舶租赁经理、船舶经理、代理人和经纪人可享受半费待遇，某些海上保险公司也是如此。政府还试图将这一提议扩大到实物商品交易商，认识到交易商创造了对租船、保险、金融和法律服务的需求
第一个结果是有形的，但可以解释。政府数据显示，享受相关优惠制度的船舶租赁企业数量从2020/21年度的11家增加到2022/23年度的46家。这证明结构和企业已经做出了反应。它很少提及信用委员会的地点、选择船只的人员或谈判租船的团队

【原文 English Original】
New report identifies Hong Kong’s place in world shipping - Splash247
Hong Kong Maritime Week is about to kick off. To celebrate the occasion, Splash today publishes a 48-page magazine on the city’s maritime hub credentials.
A ship can be ordered at a mainland Chinese yard, owned through a leasing company in Hong Kong, insured in London, crewed through a management operation in Asia and chartered from Singapore. Its cargo need never pass through Hong Kong’s harbour. Even its Hong Kong financing vehicle may have to seek credit approval elsewhere.
The geography of shipping has always been complicated. What has changed is the urgency with which Hong Kong must ask where the real business takes place. Is the city still a maritime capital in its own right, chosen by international owners, traders and financiers because of what it offers? Or is it becoming a highly sophisticated services counter for the vast industrial and commercial machine next door?
On paper, the answer looks reassuring. Hong Kong remains fourth in the 2026 Xinhua-Baltic international maritime centre rankings, behind Singapore, Shanghai and London. Three of the world’s leading shipmanagement companies are headquartered here, major P&I clubs operate here, and the city retains a formidable concentration of lawyers, financiers and technical expertise.
Look towards the waterfront, however, and a different picture emerges. The container port handled 12.99m teu in 2025, scarcely half its 2008 peak. The register has shed substantial tonnage amid geopolitical upheaval, falling to 109m gt by June this year. Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou have grown into maritime giants whose physical advantages Hong Kong cannot realistically overturn.
These are not contradictory stories. Together they define the central question running through this special report: whether Hong Kong can convert its inherited maritime strengths into a sustainable business model for 2030, even as its traditional measures of importance become less flattering.
Richard Hext, chairman of the Hong Kong Shipowners Association, resists the suggestion that the city is being reduced to an adjunct of the mainland.
“An ‘annex’ does not host three of the world’s top 10 shipmanagers, 11 of the 12 International Group P&I associations, eight of the top ten ship-finance bookrunners,” he says, pointing also to the city’s legal institutions and international industry organisations.
This inventory represents decades of investment and commercial trust. Yet it does not settle the more difficult question of what those institutions actually do here, or whether their next expansion will take place somewhere else.
Hong Kong has spent much of this decade making itself more attractive on tax. Qualifying ship lessors can enjoy a zero profits-tax rate; eligible ship leasing managers, shipmanagers, agents and brokers benefit from half-rate treatment, as do certain marine insurers. The administration has also sought to broaden the proposition to physical commodity traders, recognising that traders create demand for chartering, insurance, finance and legal services
The first results are tangible, but open to interpretation. Government figures show the number of ship leasing enterprises under the relevant preferential regime rising from 11 in 2020/21 to 46 in 2022/23. That is evidence that structures and businesses have responded. It says much less about the location of credit committees, the people selecting vessels or the teams negotiating charters.
“Tax is necessary but not sufficient,” Hext says. Companies, he argues, follow customers, skills, capital and regulatory certainty. He wants the next phase judged by “regional headquarters, underwriting authority, credit decisions, trading desks and skilled jobs, and not by company registrations alone”.
Gautam Chellaram, chairman of KC Maritime, is more sceptical about what tax reform has delivered. He sees genuine growth in leasing and mainland-linked finance, but says: “I do not yet see clear evidence that the measures have resulted in substantial headquarters relocation involving decision-makers, fund managers, and independent shipowners physically basing themselves in Hong Kong.”
It would be equally wrong to dismiss the developments as bookkeeping. Hong Kong is a place where ships are managed, risks assessed and capital arranged, not merely where documents are signed. Dockendale Group is among the companies expanding management operations locally. Its chief executive, Vikrant Gusain, says Hong Kong’s ease of doing business is an important factor in the decision, alongside access to Asian markets and international talent.
The competitive comparison nevertheless remains Singapore.
“Singapore continues to offer broader tax incentives and a larger concentration of commodity traders,” says Jim James, senior consultant at Hill Dickinson.
The latter point may be more important than the former. Traders and charterers bring transactions, and transactions bring the brokers, lenders, insurers and lawyers who serve them. A critical mass of principals is extraordinarily difficult to manufacture through concessions alone.
Hong Kong has distinct advantages of its own. Its banking network connects Chinese and international capital; its offshore renminbi role creates opportunities for trade and leasing; and its links with a vast manufacturing and shipbuilding hinterland provide access that a competing maritime centre cannot reproduce. But geographical proximity is not the same thing as commercial gravity. The city must persuade companies to put people with mandates and budgets here, not just a local subsidiary.
June’s tax amendment bill, including a proposed half-rate concession for qualifying physical commodity trading, gives the policy another push. September’s first five-year plan adds a ‘Finance + Maritime’ agenda built around ship finance, insurance, trade finance and related services. Neither initiative can be called successful solely because it exists. Their test will be new trading desks, lending decisions and customers with genuine freedom to transact elsewhere.
Where does this leave the argument that Hong Kong is becoming Shanghai’s professional-services annex? Chellaram offers the report’s most uncomfortable formulation: as a cargo port, the city is being functionally subordinated to mainland competitors, but as a financial, legal and arbitration centre it retains qualities not available in the same combination across the border.
“On the professional-services side, Hong Kong is the piece Shanghai structurally cannot replicate,” he says.
The separate customs territory, common-law system, freely convertible currency and established international business practices all give the city a distinctive purpose. The opportunity is to sell those qualities to the world, not simply to companies moving through China.
Damien Laracy, partner and head of Hill Dickinson’s Hong Kong office, describes a transition “from a cargo-driven port hub to a specialised centre for maritime services”. Rather than an annex, he sees “the region’s high-value maritime services platform, complementing the manufacturing, cargo, and port capacity of neighbouring cities”.
The distinction is subtle but critical. A law firm advising a mainland shipowner on a vessel financing can be doing genuine international business from Hong Kong. So can an insurer handling a casualty thousands of miles away or a manager overseeing a fleet trading between Brazil and India. But the city’s position becomes more vulnerable if its principal attraction is merely that it makes mainland transactions easier. The international test is whether owners and counterparties with no direct mainland connection still choose Hong Kong.
The machinery of a genuine maritime centre is already here. English-language maritime contracts, established common-law precedents, internationally recognised arbitration and access to mainland enforcement arrangements give it a credible offering. Rosita Lau, a partner at Ince, is among those urging the city to promote its legal and dispute-resolution capabilities far more systematically. The fact that Hong Kong can be chosen in a contract is not proof that it will be.
There are also more prosaic measures of legal competitiveness. Martyn Huckerby, head of competition law and regulatory at Hill Dickinson, points to the extension of the block exemption for liner vessel-sharing agreements to 2031. The renewal, he says, preserves “legal certainty for operational cooperation between liner shipping companies”. It is a narrow regulatory decision, but one of the many predictable rules on which internationally mobile businesses build long-term operations.
Insurance offers another illustration of integration without inevitable subordination. London P&I has served shipowners from Hong Kong for decades and opened an office in Shanghai in 2025. Deborah Yu, its regional director for Asia, says the two offices work together with the club’s operations in London and Athens. The point is not to force every Asian insurance decision into Hong Kong, but to ensure the city continues to handle work that could plausibly be located elsewhere.
An international city must keep choosing to be international. That means foreign owners can operate comfortably, specialist staff can build careers and global counterparties can trust their contracts, information and capital to an environment they understand.
This issue explores what that requirement means in practice. Hong Kong’s shipmanagement concentration provides a genuine strategic asset: it would take years to reproduce the crewing, technical and training networks that leading managers have built here. The challenge is keeping enough experienced people to make decisions locally as digitalisation, alternative fuels and increasingly complex compliance change the skill set.
The same logic applies to finance and insurance. An internationally recognised logo on a Hong Kong office does not tell us whether it can approve a ship loan or underwrite a specialist risk. A registry’s gross tonnage does not establish where the family that owns the ship runs its business. A port’s box count says little about the value of transactions governed by local law, but the loss of container activity cannot be waved away simply by relabelling the city a services centre.
Technology adds a further test. Hong Kong’s Port Community System is meant to help connect cargo movements, documentation and financing across the supply chain. But common platforms are only as useful as the trust and security behind them. Paul Haswell, technology partner at Hill Dickinson, notes that digitisation will bring “increased emphasis on data security and the monitoring of systems”. A financial and logistics crossroads cannot afford to treat cyber resilience as an optional extra.
The city’s new maritime ambitions, particularly green bunkering and transition finance, depend on the same mixture of hard infrastructure and intangible trust. There is little value in promoting alternative fuels unless ships can take them safely, on schedule and at competitive prices. There is little point marketing green ship finance unless lenders and owners are prepared to commit capital against realistic assumptions about technology, fuel availability and earnings.
Government has clearly recognised the need to change. Its first five-year plan shifts the emphasis from volume to value, promising stronger maritime services, a greener and smarter port, closer links with the Greater Bay Area and a more developed marine finance ecosystem. The question is no longer whether officials have ambitions. It is whether businesses can see projects proceeding quickly enough, and with sufficient commercial substance, to justify staying and expanding.
That demands a sharper understanding of competition. Singapore can be a partner and a rival. Shanghai can be a customer, collaborator and competitor. The Greater Bay Area can supply Hong Kong with enormous commercial opportunities while simultaneously taking cargo, talent and investment from it. Those apparently inconsistent propositions are the reality of a maritime industry in which business moves wherever the overall proposition is strongest.
The defensible future is neither a nostalgic campaign to win back every container nor a comfortable acceptance of being the mainland’s legal and financial back office. It is a city that remains indispensable to international shipping because substantive work is done there: ships are managed, cargo is traded, capital is committed, risks are insured and disputes are resolved.
By 2030, Hong Kong should be judged less by how many companies have an address in Central or how many development plans have been published, and more by who has authority to do business from the city. Are the next fleet acquisitions decided here? Are traders locating profitable operations here? Are international parties choosing Hong Kong law when they have no obligation to do so? Are young maritime professionals staying because the best opportunities are available here?
A gateway is somewhere business passes through. A maritime capital is somewhere business chooses to stay. Hong Kong has spent generations proving it can be both. The coming four years will show whether it still can.

title: Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
zh_title: 埃隆·马斯克表示，能够聘请被罢免的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋“将是一种荣幸”
summary: 黄仁勋在情报来源披露他与一名疑似中国间谍的关系两周后，以及他与英伟达副总裁的恋情曝光一天后，辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。但在此举之前几个小时，当有传言称 Nvidia 董事会计划将他驱逐时，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 就已经表示愿意聘用这位 Nvidia 前首席执行官。一位随机的 X 用户发帖称，“埃隆请雇用詹森”，这位亿万富翁回答道：“那将是一种荣幸。” @zerohedge 这将是一种荣幸 2026 年 11 月 12 日，尽管詹森有丑闻
content:
黄仁勋在情报来源披露他与一名疑似中国间谍的关系两周后，以及他与英伟达副总裁的恋情曝光一天后，辞去了英伟达首席执行官的职务。但在此举之前几个小时，当有传言称 Nvidia 董事会计划将他驱逐时，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 就已经表示愿意聘用这位 Nvidia 前首席执行官。一位随机的 X 用户发帖称，“埃隆请雇用詹森”，这位亿万富翁回答道：“那将是一种荣幸。” @zerohedge 这将是一种荣誉，2026 年 11 月 12 日 尽管 Jensen 目前面临丑闻，但他仍然拥有工程专业知识、对行业及其内部运作的深入了解，再加上在世界各地的多重联系，这对于任何想要进入半导体行业的公司来说都是极其有价值的。这正是埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在他的 Terafab 项目中所做的事情，他于 2025 年 11 月首次提到该项目。黄仁勋甚至警告说，这将是一个挑战，并指出“台积电谋生的工程、科学和艺术是极其困难的。”尽管如此，马斯克仍将资源投入到该项目中，Terafab 工厂的建设正如火如荼地进行，并计划在 2028 年下半年实现芯片量产。马斯克本人表示，该工厂的目标是到 2032 年实现每月 100 万片晶圆的产能。
特斯拉有着雄心勃勃的人工智能加速器路线图，SpaceX 甚至宣称在未来制造自己的 GPU。我们仍然不知道黄仁勋的计划是什么，但尽管他不再是 Nvidia 董事会及其领导层的成员，Jensen 和他的妻子 Lori 仍然通过各种信托和有限责任公司共同持有约 8 亿股 Nvidia 股票，而黄仁勋本人则拥有约 7000 万股 Nvidia 股票。除此之外，他仍然收到国会发出的讨论英伟达安全协议的邀请，如果他拒绝的话，这可能会变成传票，尽管我们不知道他的辞职会对闭门会议产生什么影响。据报道，FBI 正在调查他与 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 的关系，后者据称在向中国进口价值 75 亿美元的 Nvidia AI GPU 过程中发挥了重要作用，并涉嫌与中国国家安全部合作。黄仁勋只是因与下属发生关系或外遇而辞职或被免职的高管名单中最新的一个。其中包括2005年的波音前首席执行官哈里·斯通西弗(Harry Stonecipher)、2010年的惠普首席执行官马克·赫德(Mark Hurd)、2018年的英特尔首席执行官布莱恩·科兹安尼克(Brian Krzanich)和2019年的前麦当劳首席执行官史蒂夫·伊斯特布鲁克(Steve Easterbrook)。
据了解，马斯克本人与多家公司的下属有过关系，他甚至通过试管受精与 2017 年开始在特斯拉工作的 Neuralink 高管 Shivon Zilis 生了四个孩子。目前尚不清楚马斯克的回复是否是对黄仁勋的认真报价。但如果这位前 Nvidia 首席执行官决定为 Musk 的 Terafab 项目工作，那么 Jensen 可以利用他的努力和专业知识，将其变成 Nvidia 的强大竞争对手。

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO two weeks after his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy was revealed by intelligence sources and a day after his affair with an Nvidia vice president became publicly known. But hours before this move, when it was just rumored that the Nvidia board was planning to oust him , Elon Musk had already stated his willingness to hire the former Nvidia chief on X . A random X user posted, “Elon please hire Jensen,” to which the billionaire replied, “That would be an honor.” @zerohedge That would be an honor November 12, 2026 Despite the scandals that Jensen is currently facing, he still has the engineering know-how, deep knowledge of the industry and its inner workings, plus multiple connections across the world, which would be extremely valuable for any company looking to break into the semiconductor industry. This is exactly what Elon Musk is doing with his Terafab project, which he first mentioned in November 2025 . Jensen Huang even warned that this was going to be a challenge, pointing out that “the engineering, the science, and the artistry of doing what TSMC does for a living is extremely hard.” Nevertheless, Musk poured his resources into the project, with construction on the Terafab facility in full swing and with plans to hit volume chip production by the second half of 2028 . Musk himself said that the site targets a production capacity of a million wafers a month by 2032. Tesla has an ambitious AI accelerator roadmap , and SpaceX has even touted making its own GPUs in the future . We still don’t know what Jensen Huang’s plans are, but even though he’s no longer a part of the Nvidia board and its leadership, Jensen and his wife, Lori, still jointly own approximately 800 million Nvidia shares through various trusts and LLCs, while Huang himself personally owns around 70 million Nvidia shares. Aside from that, he still has an outstanding invitation from Congress to discuss Nvidia’s security protocols, which could turn into a subpoena if he snubs them, although we don’t know how his resignation would affect the closed-door meeting. There’s also a reported FBI investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang , the Megaspeed executive who was allegedly instrumental in the import of $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia AI GPUs into China and is suspected of working with China’s Ministry of State Security . Jensen Huang is just the latest in the long list of executives who resigned or were ousted from their leadership position because of a relationship or an affair with a subordinate. This includes former Boeing CEO Harry Stonecipher in 2005, HP CEO Mark Hurd in 2010, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich in 2018, and former McDonald’s CEO Steve Easterbrook in 2019. Musk himself is known to have had relationships with subordinates from his various companies, and that he has even fathered four children with Shivon Zilis, a top executive at Neuralink who started working at Tesla in 2017, through IVF. It’s still not confirmed if Musk’s reply is a serious offer for Jensen Huang. But if the former Nvidia chief ever decides to work for Musk on his Terafab project, then Jensen could put his effort and expertise into turning it into a formidable competitor to Nvidia.

content: 作者： 徒步的骑手 2026年11月10日   徒步的騎手播客 中美跨国腐败 Preview   Listen now   中美跨国腐败 美国大案意外揭开中美跨国腐败；中国官二代的跨国裙带网：官学商勾结，利益输送，权钱交易，防火墙失灵；哈佛和美国学术界的遮羞布；收割与被收割的游戏...... 大家好，又虚度了一个周末。照常划艇钓鱼，走路举重，吃吃喝喝，跟朋友聊聊天。我们继续娱乐政治，说说美国版西门庆、王婆跟中国官二代千金联袂主演的一场大戏。这个频道有些听众是跟孩子一起听，这期节目，还是让孩子跳过去吧。 前一阵，美国的主流和非主流媒体，同时爆出一个大瓜，主角是横跨官学商三界的大咖Larry Summers。萨默斯曾经担任过美国财政部长、哈佛大学校长、世界银行首席经济学家。事发时，他仍然担任哈佛大学教授，还有一些大公司的董事。 事情的起因是，美国众议院决定公开一部分爱泼斯坦案文件。很多听众可能知道爱泼斯坦案。这人是美国当代最有名的皮条客——也可能是世界历史上最有名的皮条客，为很多名人拉过皮条，包括比尔·盖茨，还有后来当上总统的川普。川普第一任时，爱泼斯坦因为涉嫌组织未成年人性交易，被抓捕起诉，不久在监狱中死亡，狱方说是自杀。 前年，川普竞选总统的时候，保证他当选以后，公布爱泼斯坦文件。但他去年当上总统以后，改口说文件中没什么东西，不再公布，引起他的基本盘不满。一直到现在，仍然在发酵。上周，共和党控制的众议院像挤牙膏一样公布了一些文件，包括爱泼斯坦的一些email。人们发现萨默斯跟爱泼斯坦交往密切，关系不一般。他向爱泼斯坦请教，如何跟一位中国官二代千金上床。 这位被萨默斯盯上的中国官二代千金，在公开的邮件中，名字被隐去。她的身份非常特殊。虽然媒体没有直接点名，但根据邮件和《华尔街日报》等媒体披露的细节，比如中国籍、哈佛大学博士、伦敦政经学院副教授、父亲是中国副部级高官……所有的线索都指向一个人——金刻羽。 这几年，金刻羽在西方媒体上特别活跃，她以著名经济学家面目出现，高调为党国辩护。她出身不凡，父亲是中国财政部前副部长，也是中国发起的亚洲基础设施投资银行行长。 2015年，中国挑头搞亚洲投资银行，美国决定不参与。萨默斯在媒体上公开抨击美国的做法。当时，很多中文媒体大幅报导，标题特别吸引眼球。比如说 “美国前财长萨默斯：亚投行见证美国丧失全球经济霸主地位”、“萨默斯谈亚投行：美国一意孤行的苦果”、“萨默斯：亚投行见证美国丧失全球经济霸主地位”、“美国前财长萨默斯：亚投行开门红为美国敲响警钟”、“美国坚持不加入亚投行，前财长萨默斯怒斥国家不作为”… 萨默斯为美国操碎了心，指责美国不响应中国号召加入亚投行，他抨击美国不作为。爱泼斯坦邮件公布以后，人们才发现，萨默斯的痛心疾首可能另有原因。三年后，他向爱泼斯坦敞开心扉，求教如何跟亚投行行长的千金上床。现在，外界知道，这才是他头脑中的作为，其他作为不作为，都是些高大上名词包装。 萨默斯邮件门曝光以后，一些中文媒体开始八卦，加入很多想像。英文媒体，不管是主流还是非主流，大部分报导还是依据邮件的内容，没有展开想象力。萨默斯有没有跟金刻羽上床，我对这种话题不感兴趣。上床了又能怎么样？不上床又能怎么样？到底是谁引诱谁，谁想利用谁，引诱到哪一步，利用到哪步，是半推半就，还是半推不就，看客自己去发挥想象力。那不是这期节目的话题。 我感兴趣的是，美国、中国，这两个世界大国的学界和官场、著名大学和官办机构，是怎么沆瀣一气，把学术研究、国家利益弄成包装男盗女娼的遮羞布的？ 所以，这个事件不仅仅是一个在官商学界通吃了一辈子的老男人，下半身那点事儿。如果只看到了性，那你就太小看美国、中国的高官和学阀了。萨默斯邮件门提供了一个接近完美的解剖样本。我们可以用思维的手术刀，切开这个长期被名人、名校、名学者光环掩盖的腐败肿瘤。这个肿瘤就是：官、学、商相互勾结的裙带网。 这个裙带联盟早就跨越了国界。中国加入世贸以后，官学商界成了最大受益者。中国的官僚、学阀和富商，迅速积累了巨额财富。他们开始利用手中的财富，带着他们的孩子，官二代、学二代、富二代，打入美国的官学商裙带网。 中国式腐败跟美国式腐败叠加，让这个本来就是为腐败而存在的裙带网，就像注入了类固醇，急剧膨胀。一些大学、智库、半官方机构，几乎变成了王婆、西门庆叱咤风云的紫石街。为了名，为了利，为了欲望，他们什么都干得出来，而且能把什么恶心的东西都包装成学术。 估计大部分听众都读过《水浒传》，知道武大郎、王婆住的街道，叫“紫石街”。武大郎在街上挑担子卖烧饼。王婆在家里开茶坊，既当老板，又当服务员，而且还当媒婆。她不但给单身男女说媒，也给有夫之妇和有妇之夫说媒，观念比较超前，可以说是宋朝的女爱泼斯坦，比美国超前了900年。 中国历史上在有些方面，至少是在小说中，还是挺超前的。如果西门庆混到现在，怎么也得是个知名企业家、著名学者、博士生导师、文化部副部长之类，怎么也得到哈佛公费进修一年，怎么也得把孩子弄到哈佛拿个学位。 说起来，都很有穿越感。王婆、西门庆、萨默斯、爱泼斯坦、金刻羽……美国的官僚、学阀，中国的官一代、官二代，再加上个全球皮条客，在哈佛的紫石街茶坊，各取所需，心有灵犀，还点都不用点。... 附：

title: The Jensen Huang Scandal Should Change Everything
zh_title: 黄仁勋丑闻应该改变一切
summary: 黄仁勋在与女性爱丽丝·黄（美国情报官员认为她是中国情报资产）的婚外情被曝光后突然离开英伟达，应该会迫使美国从根本上重新思考人工智能战略。黄仁勋不仅仅是世界上最重要的半导体公司的首席执行官。他也是唐纳德·特朗普最亲密、最有影响力的人工智能顾问之一。黄说服特朗普放弃最初的出口管制，认为美国科技公司应该在中国竞争。他坚持认为人工智能更类似于电力
content:
黄仁勋在与女性爱丽丝·黄（美国情报官员认为她是中国情报资产）的婚外情被曝光后突然离开英伟达，应该会迫使美国从根本上重新思考人工智能战略。黄仁勋不仅仅是世界上最重要的半导体公司的首席执行官。他也是唐纳德·特朗普最亲密、最有影响力的人工智能顾问之一。黄说服特朗普放弃最初的出口管制，认为美国科技公司应该在中国竞争。他坚持认为，人工智能更像是电力，而不是武器，而且有关人工智能安全的警告被过分夸大了——特朗普完全内化了这一观点。在接下来的几个月中，国会将仔细审查丑闻的各个方面。其中包括商务部暂停对Alice Huang担任董事的新加坡公司Megaspeed的调查；未能打击中国在东南亚广泛的芯片走私活动；英伟达对特朗普最喜欢的项目（例如白宫舞厅）的财务贡献；以及中国可能对美国其他商界领袖产生非法影响。 [阅读：价值 5.7 万亿美元的面部工厂] 这起丑闻发生在全国对人工智能深感不满和焦虑的时刻，它可能会加剧公众的担忧，即开发这项技术的公司对其管理方式拥有过多影响力。
在最近的中期选举中，承诺限制数据中心建设的候选人取得了重大进展。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的负责人达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和 OpenAI 的萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 分别警告称，新模式可能会带来巨大风险，并建议两家公司“在前沿领域保持步伐”。几乎每周都会有前所未有的网络攻击的消息，其中一些是由人工智能驱动的。例如，今年 7 月，在 OpenAI 接受安全测试的自主代理逃离了沙箱，并侵入了另一家人工智能公司 Hugging Face 的系统。美国的难题是：美国必须领先于中国，但也必须认真对待安全。答案不是加速发展或寻求与北京讨价还价，而是加强出口管制。加强控制将有助于保持美国的领先地位，为减缓开发创造空间，并确保新车型在发布前经过严格测试。赢得与中国的竞争已成为企业高管提升公司利益并拒绝任何形式监管呼声的万能借口。政客们也陷入了这个陷阱。 9 月，参议员特德·克鲁兹 (Ted Cruz) 告诉 Politico，“如果他们要成为杀手机器人，我宁愿他们是美国杀手机器人，而不是中国杀手机器人。”地缘政治并不是做非理性事情的糟糕借口。
但像黄说的那样，谁赢得比赛并不重要同样是错误的。 今年 4 月，Anthropic 宣布开发了一种名为 Mythos 的模型，该模型为用户提供了极其先进的网络攻击能力。 Anthropic 没有向公众发布 Mythos，而是与特朗普政府合作建立了 Project Glasswing，该项目让美国顶尖公司能够使用该网络防御模型，以便他们能够尽快弥补漏洞。如果中国或任何其他国家首先发展出类似神话的能力，它就不太可能与美国分享这种模式。

【原文 English Original】
Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure from Nvidia, following revelations of an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence officials believe to be a Chinese-intelligence asset, should force a fundamental rethinking of America’s AI strategy. Jensen Huang was not just the CEO of the world’s most important semiconductor company. He was also one of Donald Trump’s closest and most influential advisers on AI. Huang persuaded Trump to abandon his initial embrace of export controls, arguing that U.S. technology firms should compete in China. He persistently argued that AI is more akin to electricity than a weapon and that warnings about AI safety were wildly overblown—a view that Trump fully internalized. In the coming months, Congress will scrutinize every aspect of the scandal. Among these are the Commerce Department’s suspension of its investigation into Megaspeed, the Singaporean company that Alice Huang was a director of; the failure to crack down on China’s extensive chip-smuggling operation in Southeast Asia; Nvidia’s financial contributions to Trump’s pet projects, such as the White House ballroom; and China’s possible illicit influence over other business leaders in America. [ Read: A $5.7 trillion face-plant ] The scandal comes at a moment of deep national dissatisfaction and anxiety about AI, and it is likely to reinforce public concerns that the companies developing this technology are given too much influence over how it is governed. In the recent midterm elections, candidates promising restrictions on data-center construction made significant gains. Dario Amodei and Sam Altman , the heads of Anthropic and OpenAI, respectively, have warned that new models could come with tremendous risk and suggested that the companies should “pace the frontier.” Hardly a week passes without news of unprecedented cyberattacks, some of which are powered by AI. In July, for example, autonomous agents undergoing safety testing at OpenAI escaped their sandbox and hacked into the systems of Hugging Face, another AI company. America’s conundrum is this: The United States must stay ahead of China, but it also has to take safety seriously. The answer is not to accelerate development or to seek a grand bargain with Beijing, but to strengthen export controls. Stronger controls will help preserve America’s lead, creating the room to slow down development and ensure that new models are rigorously tested before they are released. Winning the race with China has become a one-size-fits-all excuse for business executives to advance their company’s interests and reject calls for regulation of any kind. Politicians have also fallen into this trap. In September, Senator Ted Cruz told Politico , “If they’re going to be killer robots, I’d rather they be American killer robots and not Chinese killer robots.” Geopolitics are a poor excuse for doing something irrational. But to say , as Huang did, that who wins the race doesn’t really matter is equally wrong. In April, Anthropic announced that it had developed a model called Mythos, which gave users extremely advanced cyberattack capabilities. Rather than releasing Mythos to the public, Anthropic worked with the Trump administration to set up Project Glasswing, which gave the top U.S. companies access to the model for cyberdefense, so that they could plug their gaps as quickly as possible. If China or any other state had developed Mythos-like capabilities first, it would not likely have shared the model with U.S. companies, which would have been left exposed. Several senators have proposed a tempting solution: The United States should negotiate a comprehensive arms control with China to pause or slow down AI development. Altman has said that such a deal would be easy for Trump and Xi Jinping to agree to. But this is a fantasy. Verification would be extremely difficult. China would likely see the pursuit of such an agreement as a U.S. attempt to lock in a lead. In a recent statement , the head of the Ministry for State Security, China’s intelligence services, made clear that China sees AI competition with the United States in adversarial terms. That doesn’t rule out talks and coordinated actions to address specific safety risks, but it does mean that a grand bargain is extremely unlikely. Taking safety seriously is impossible if the AI developers continue at full throttle. The models are close to being able to improve themselves, a capacity that could dramatically accelerate technological progress beyond the ability of humans to evaluate and control it. That’s why the United States needs to strengthen its export controls and double down on safety in the lead time that gives it over China. Although China is working hard to develop its indigenous chip-manufacturing capability, it is still struggling. In June 2025, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testified to Congress that China produces only about 200,000 advanced chips annually, a tiny number compared with what it needs. Chips are the one advantage that the United States has over China, and Washington needs to capitalize on this. Much of China’s progress appears to have depended on access to American AI models. Chinese companies have used distillation, a technique whereby a less capable model is trained by a more powerful one, allowing it to duplicate some of those capabilities quickly. In February, Anthropic revealed that DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax had generated more than 16 million exchanges with Claude through approximately 24,000 fraudulent accounts to extract its capabilities. The company later uncovered an even larger operation by Alibaba, involving more than 150 million exchanges designed to improve its Qwen models. In September, the FBI and the NSA warned that Chinese laboratories were using large-scale distillation to acquire American AI capabilities at a fraction of the cost of developing them independently. As we now know from the Nvidia scandal, espionage also likely plays a role. Huang knew more than any other individual about who was getting advanced chips. Access to that information could have proved invaluable to a foreign actor. The AI labs are also very vulnerable to spying. Last month, federal prosecutors charged a Saudi national employed at OpenAI with installing a covert recording device. The labs’ crown jewels are model weights—the mathematical parameters that encode what the models have learned. If a foreign intelligence service steals those weights, it could acquire capabilities that the labs spent years developing. The U.S. government needs to significantly increase counterintelligence cooperation with the labs and other companies doing work that pertains to U.S. national security. [ Read: The scandal is bigger than Jensen Huang ] Ensuring adequate safety of new AI models depends on slowing the race, not just between the U.S. and China, but also among the American labs. AI engineers and experts have been discussing how to do this. One of the leading ideas is to require the labs to reallocate their computing power, devoting far less of it to research and development and far more to customer service and safety. This would slow the pace of development—and it could be done within parameters that allow the United States to stay ahead of China, and the AI companies to maintain their profitability. President Trump has spent much of the past two years bullying some of America’s closest and oldest allies, and his posture has hardly generated confidence in Washington’s stewardship of AI. America’s Five Eyes allies (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom) had to wait months before gaining access to Mythos to improve their private-sector cyberdefenses. These and other traditional allies will surely worry that an American president may use powerful AI against them. Trump is unlikely to assuage these fears, but the new Congress can begin to lay the foundation for a new AI alliance that lays down criteria for access to chips, computing infrastructure, and frontier models, and proposes restraints and assurances for how the United States will use powerful AI. One lesson of the Jensen Huang scandal is that policy makers gave extraordinary influence to technology executives whose commercial interests did not always align with American interests. His departure offers a rare opportunity to rethink the assumptions that have underpinned AI strategy for the past two years, address mounting concerns about the technology, and establish a new approach that protects both American AI leadership and public safety.

content:
Titan Mining（纽约证券交易所股票代码：TII；多伦多证券交易所股票代码：TI）正致力于成为 70 年来美国第一家商业石墨生产商，同时寻求与陆军达成历史性协议，在阿拉巴马州基地建立石墨加工厂。根据拟议的交易，泰坦将把石墨精矿从其主要的基尔伯恩矿场和纽约州北部的示范工厂运送到安尼斯顿陆军仓库，泰坦的帝国矿业子公司将在那里利用一些现有的基础设施进一步加工石墨。该仓库位于阿拉巴马州首府蒙哥马利东北约145公里处。 Titan 首席执行官丽塔·阿迪亚尼 (Rita Adiani) 在 10 月份接受《北方矿工》采访时表示：“能够生产精矿真是太好了，但除非你能进一步精炼，否则你最终会面临同样的情况，即基本上将中游出口回中国或其他地方。” “这使我们能够有效地在国内生产端到端产品，从供应链安全的角度来看，这非常重要。”  政府与行业动力 6 月份，根据美国陆军战略资本计划 (SCI) 计划，该基地合作伙伴关系标志着政府、军方和工业界之间的重大合作，因为美国越来越多地寻求将关键矿产供应链置于国内控制之下并摆脱中国的影响。
在正在考虑的三个陆军基地中，包括纽约的德拉姆堡和阿肯色州的派恩布拉夫兵工厂，泰坦的安尼斯顿基地交易已进展为商业条款清单，尽管最终的租约尚未完成。安尼斯顿的租约涵盖最初的 50 年，以及两个额外的 25 年续约选项。根据 SCI 计划入选的其他公司包括 REalloys (纳斯达克股票代码：ALOY) 和 Ioneer (ASX: INR)，它们获得了有条件租赁合同，分别在犹他州 Tooele Army Depot 开发单独的重稀土和硼加工设施；私人公司 EnergyX 拥有德克萨斯州红河基地一座锂工厂的有条件租赁权。 13 年使用寿命 根据 2025 年起的初步经济评估 (PEA)，Kilbourne 在 13 年使用寿命内每年可按铭牌产能生产约 40,000 吨石墨精矿。Titan 于 1 月份开始在 Kilbourne 生产，并已向客户运送了至少 1,600 公斤石墨精矿。按 7% 折现，其税后净现值为 5.13 亿美元，税后内部收益率为 37%，初始成本为 1.56 亿美元。根据 2024 年的初步估计，PEA 基于 240 万吨品位为 2.91% 的石墨碳 (Cg) 推断，其中露天有限资源中含有 653,000 短吨石墨。综合采矿和加工业务的可行性研究正在进行中，预计将于 2027 年上半年发布。
